source_summaries.scope: Nigerian software, web, data, artificial intelligence, networking, cybersecurity, digital services, information systems, privacy and compliance work
findings: NITDA identifies digital skills, software and hardware development, cybersecurity, digital trust, research and an agile technology workforce as Nigerian strategic priorities.
NBTE lists Nigerian programmes and national occupational standards spanning software, web, data, AI, networking, robotics, computer hardware, cybersecurity and digital service operations.
NDPC describes data-protection compliance, information privacy, information audit, data management and information-security evidence relevant to Nigerian privacy and compliance work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technology-sector, training and regulatory context; it does not prove a specific employer requirement, salary, vacancy count or universal certificate for every ICT title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian industrial automation, robotics and mechatronics training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian industrial automation, programmable logic controllers, robotics, mechatronics, automated production, assembly, instrumentation and manufacturing technology
findings: NBTE curricula identify Nigerian training in automation and robotics, including relays, switches, contactors, machine programming, automated production lines, numerical control, automated assembly, PLC programming and fault diagnosis, robotics, mechatronics and human-machine interfaces.
source_summaries.limitations: The curricula establish a Nigerian technical-training pathway and competency categories, not evidence that every employer uses the same controller, software, machine or certification.

findings: NITDA and 3MTT explicitly list product management, data analysis and visualisation, data science, cloud computing, DevOps, UI/UX and quality assurance among Nigerian technical-skill tracks.
source_summaries.limitations: A national training track is evidence of a Nigerian skills pathway and ecosystem signal, not a guarantee of employment demand or a universal requirement for each related subgroup.

findings: NITDA identifies digital skills, software and hardware development, cybersecurity, digital trust, research and an agile technology workforce as Nigerian strategic priorities.
NBTE lists Nigerian programmes and national occupational standards spanning software, web, data, AI, networking, robotics, computer hardware, cybersecurity and digital service operations.
NDPC describes data-protection compliance, information privacy, information audit, data management and information-security evidence relevant to Nigerian privacy and compliance work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technology-sector, training and regulatory context; it does not prove a specific employer requirement, salary, vacancy count or universal certificate for every ICT title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.name: 3 Million Technical Talent technical skills tracks
Choice Talents Nigeria game developer vacancy
Computer Professionals Registration Council of Nigeria
CPN 2021 Examination Syllabus
Nigerian creative-industry and media sources
Esports Federation of Nigeria national esports programmes
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian competitive gaming, schools and university esports, broadcasting, refereeing, tournament operations and team programmes
findings: The federation described a National Esports Championship, Team Nigeria programme, schools and university league, and training for referees, broadcasters and tournament officials.
The federation's career-pathway language identifies athletes, content creators, event managers, analysts and game developers as roles within the Nigerian esports ecosystem.
EFN's current about page identifies players, coaches, referees and support staff as participants in Nigeria's organised esports pathway and describes national representation and player development.
source_summaries.limitations: Federation programmes demonstrate ecosystem and role-family context; they do not establish national job volume or a mandatory credential.

source_summaries.name: Federation of Interactive Games of Nigeria career pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian and African interactive-games pathways covering casting, game development, voice and content creation
findings: FIGN presents distinct pathways for commentary and casting, game development across design/engineering/art/audio, voiceover and content/creator work.
source_summaries.limitations: A pathway page demonstrates ecosystem and portfolio direction; it is not a vacancy count, universal job requirement or personal licence.

source_summaries.name: Federal Ministry of Arts, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy gaming sector context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria gaming, game development, esports and immersive creative economy
findings: Government identifies game development, esports and immersive experiences as a Nigerian creative-economy growth area.
The ministry describes local talent support, digital-skills development and job creation as sector objectives.
source_summaries.limitations: Sector policy context is not a count of vacancies and does not establish an individual licence or credential requirement.

source_summaries.name: Creative Economy Development Fund gaming and animation value-chain map
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria gaming and animation value chain
findings: The value chain distinguishes skill and content creation, production and post-production, marketing, and distribution and monetisation.
The map names training, animators, game programmers, game-development studios and mobile gaming platforms as ecosystem participants.
source_summaries.limitations: The value-chain map describes ecosystem categories, not role-level hiring volume or guaranteed employment.

source_summaries.name: Gameloft Nigeria careers and game-studio signal
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria game-studio and game-business career ecosystem
findings: Gameloft maintains a Nigeria careers presence and identifies studio, creative and business-development pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: The careers landing page is a studio signal, not a complete Nigerian vacancy census.

source_summaries.name: Jobberman Nigeria jobs
LinkedIn Nigeria game-design job-search snapshot
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria game-design and game-development search results
findings: The search surface included Nigerian and remote listings using titles such as game designer, game developer, Unity developer, Unreal gameplay developer and Python game developer.
source_summaries.limitations: A search-results page is a directional market signal, not a deduplicated vacancy dataset and not proof that all results remain open.

source_summaries.name: Maliyo Games Nigerian studio and career ecosystem
source_summaries.scope: Lagos-based mobile-game design, development, art, narrative and distribution
findings: Maliyo identifies Lagos as its headquarters and describes work spanning African stories, characters, environments, visuals, sound and mobile-game distribution.
The studio links to careers, GameUp Africa and junior-internship pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: Studio capability and career pathways do not imply that every named role is currently open.

source_summaries.name: MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
Nigerian creative-media and performing-production standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film and media production, cinematography, lighting, sound, editing, production design, performance, special effects and stage/creative production
findings: The Nigerian NBTE Creative Media Production standard covers storytelling, cinematography, sound, production design, editing, performance, special effects, video-camera operation, lighting and casting; National Theatre materials identify stage performances, film shows, exhibitions, cultural shows, circus shows and related production facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian training and production ecosystems, not a national vacancy count or direct evidence for every highly specialised performance title; role-specific gaps remain explicit where the source does not support the title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Film Corporation creative-media National Occupational Standards workshop
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian creative-media trades including film, audio, content, photography, animation, graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies
findings: The Nigerian Film Corporation reported a July 2026 critique and validation workshop intended to develop National Occupational Standards for creative-media trades, including film production, audio production, content creation, digital photography, animation, digital graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies.
source_summaries.limitations: The workshop demonstrates Nigerian standardisation activity and named trade families; it does not mean final standards or a personal certificate already exist for every listed role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian digital technology, software, AI, cybersecurity and data-protection context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian software, web, data, artificial intelligence, networking, cybersecurity, digital services, information systems, privacy and compliance work
findings: NITDA identifies digital skills, software and hardware development, cybersecurity, digital trust, research and an agile technology workforce as Nigerian strategic priorities.
NBTE lists Nigerian programmes and national occupational standards spanning software, web, data, AI, networking, robotics, computer hardware, cybersecurity and digital service operations.
NDPC describes data-protection compliance, information privacy, information audit, data management and information-security evidence relevant to Nigerian privacy and compliance work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technology-sector, training and regulatory context; it does not prove a specific employer requirement, salary, vacancy count or universal certificate for every ICT title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian digital product-management occupational standard and vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian digital product lifecycle, roadmapping, stakeholder management, product-management tools, Agile/Scrum/Waterfall methods and product-manager employment
findings: NBTE's Digital Product Management standard covers the product lifecycle, roadmaps, stakeholder engagement, product-management software and Agile, Scrum and Waterfall methods; Nigerian job pages identify Product Manager and Product Owner roles with product vision, requirements, roadmaps, backlogs, discovery and cross-functional delivery responsibilities.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a Nigerian occupational and vacancy signal, not a national demand total or a universal certification requirement for every product, business-analysis or innovation role.

source_summaries.name: Quantity Surveyors Registration Board of Nigeria 2024 newsletter
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian quantity-surveying practice and professional registration context
findings: The QSRBN newsletter supplies Nigerian quantity-surveying professional-body context and practice material.
source_summaries.limitations: The newsletter supports professional context; specific registration gates must be shown only where the applicable rule is explicit.

source_summaries.name: NCC and NITDA ICT ecosystem sources
University of Lagos Gamr Lab video-game development laboratory
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria game-development and esports training
findings: UNILAG describes Gamr Lab as a video-game development laboratory and talent hub opened in Lagos in March 2025.
The facility is intended to train game developers, designers and esports entrepreneurs and includes Unreal Engine, VR, motion-capture and high-end PC facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: A training facility is a capacity and pathway signal, not proof of a specific vacancy or salary.

source_summaries.name: Unreal Engine Lagos developer community
source_summaries.scope: Lagos real-time 3D, game, animation and immersive-development ecosystem
findings: The Lagos community page identifies a need to grow skills and training resources for games, animation and VFX and highlights Unreal Engine as a development tool.
source_summaries.limitations: Community participation does not establish a role requirement, employment count or certification gate.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian XR and immersive-technology ecosystem signals
source_summaries.scope: Lagos and Nigerian AR/VR/XR training, immersive media, education, healthcare and construction use cases
findings: Lagos XR ecosystem sources describe skills including 360 video, Unity, Unreal Engine, event planning and team leadership; local reporting also describes VR training and Nigerian immersive-technology education and emergency-services use cases.
source_summaries.limitations: These are ecosystem and training signals, not evidence of a national vacancy count or universal tool requirement.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian creative-media trades including film, audio, content, photography, animation, graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies
findings: The Nigerian Film Corporation reported a July 2026 critique and validation workshop intended to develop National Occupational Standards for creative-media trades, including film production, audio production, content creation, digital photography, animation, digital graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies.
source_summaries.limitations: The workshop demonstrates Nigerian standardisation activity and named trade families; it does not mean final standards or a personal certificate already exist for every listed role.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian software, web, data, artificial intelligence, networking, cybersecurity, digital services, information systems, privacy and compliance work
findings: NITDA identifies digital skills, software and hardware development, cybersecurity, digital trust, research and an agile technology workforce as Nigerian strategic priorities.
NBTE lists Nigerian programmes and national occupational standards spanning software, web, data, AI, networking, robotics, computer hardware, cybersecurity and digital service operations.
NDPC describes data-protection compliance, information privacy, information audit, data management and information-security evidence relevant to Nigerian privacy and compliance work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technology-sector, training and regulatory context; it does not prove a specific employer requirement, salary, vacancy count or universal certificate for every ICT title.

source_summaries.limitations: This is a Nigerian occupational and vacancy signal, not a national demand total or a universal certification requirement for every product, business-analysis or innovation role.

Nigerian digital technology, software, AI, cybersecurity and data-protection context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian software, web, data, artificial intelligence, networking, cybersecurity, digital services, information systems, privacy and compliance work
findings: NITDA identifies digital skills, software and hardware development, cybersecurity, digital trust, research and an agile technology workforce as Nigerian strategic priorities.
NBTE lists Nigerian programmes and national occupational standards spanning software, web, data, AI, networking, robotics, computer hardware, cybersecurity and digital service operations.
NDPC describes data-protection compliance, information privacy, information audit, data management and information-security evidence relevant to Nigerian privacy and compliance work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technology-sector, training and regulatory context; it does not prove a specific employer requirement, salary, vacancy count or universal certificate for every ICT title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian industrial automation, robotics and mechatronics training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian industrial automation, programmable logic controllers, robotics, mechatronics, automated production, assembly, instrumentation and manufacturing technology
findings: NBTE curricula identify Nigerian training in automation and robotics, including relays, switches, contactors, machine programming, automated production lines, numerical control, automated assembly, PLC programming and fault diagnosis, robotics, mechatronics and human-machine interfaces.
source_summaries.limitations: The curricula establish a Nigerian technical-training pathway and competency categories, not evidence that every employer uses the same controller, software, machine or certification.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing and metal-production training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing, foundry, metal forming, machining, fitting, assembly, workshop safety and technical production
findings: NBTE publishes Nigerian national curricula and occupational standards for fabrication and welding, fitting, welding and fabrication, blacksmithing and foundry, and related technical pathways; the standards include safety, statutory compliance, marking out, welding, fastening, bending, thermal cutting, sawing and abrasive cutting.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technical-training and occupational-standard context; it does not prove that every specialist metal role has a distinct local vacancy or that one certificate is universally required.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian teacher, technical-instructor and digital-learning training pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian teacher professional development, digital literacy, classroom practice, technical teacher training and education technology implementation
findings: The Federal Ministry of Education's teacher platform describes structured teaching-methodology and digital-literacy modules.
Government education and TVET sources describe technical-teacher training, accredited centres and practical instruction pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: The sources support education-workforce and instructor foundations; they do not establish a universal licence or exact hiring requirement for every teaching, training or coaching title.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian software, web, data, artificial intelligence, networking, cybersecurity, digital services, information systems, privacy and compliance work
findings: NITDA identifies digital skills, software and hardware development, cybersecurity, digital trust, research and an agile technology workforce as Nigerian strategic priorities.
NBTE lists Nigerian programmes and national occupational standards spanning software, web, data, AI, networking, robotics, computer hardware, cybersecurity and digital service operations.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technology-sector, training and regulatory context; it does not prove a specific employer requirement, salary, vacancy count or universal certificate for every ICT title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian industrial automation, robotics and mechatronics training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian industrial automation, programmable logic controllers, robotics, mechatronics, automated production, assembly, instrumentation and manufacturing technology
findings: NBTE curricula identify Nigerian training in automation and robotics, including relays, switches, contactors, machine programming, automated production lines, numerical control, automated assembly, PLC programming and fault diagnosis, robotics, mechatronics and human-machine interfaces.
source_summaries.limitations: The curricula establish a Nigerian technical-training pathway and competency categories, not evidence that every employer uses the same controller, software, machine or certification.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing and metal-production training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing, foundry, metal forming, machining, fitting, assembly, workshop safety and technical production

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technical-training and occupational-standard context; it does not prove that every specialist metal role has a distinct local vacancy or that one certificate is universally required.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian software, web, data, artificial intelligence, networking, cybersecurity, digital services, information systems, privacy and compliance work
findings: NITDA identifies digital skills, software and hardware development, cybersecurity, digital trust, research and an agile technology workforce as Nigerian strategic priorities.
NBTE lists Nigerian programmes and national occupational standards spanning software, web, data, AI, networking, robotics, computer hardware, cybersecurity and digital service operations.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technology-sector, training and regulatory context; it does not prove a specific employer requirement, salary, vacancy count or universal certificate for every ICT title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian industrial automation, programmable logic controllers, robotics, mechatronics, automated production, assembly, instrumentation and manufacturing technology
findings: NBTE curricula identify Nigerian training in automation and robotics, including relays, switches, contactors, machine programming, automated production lines, numerical control, automated assembly, PLC programming and fault diagnosis, robotics, mechatronics and human-machine interfaces.
source_summaries.limitations: The curricula establish a Nigerian technical-training pathway and competency categories, not evidence that every employer uses the same controller, software, machine or certification.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technical-training and occupational-standard context; it does not prove that every specialist metal role has a distinct local vacancy or that one certificate is universally required.

findings: Nigeria-focused MyJobMag pages identify Business Analyst vacancies, including an analyst role in Lagos supporting business objectives, analysis, testing and solution delivery.
source_summaries.limitations: These are vacancy and title signals, not a national demand count, universal qualification requirement or evidence that every business-analyst speciality uses the same tools.

Nigerian digital technology, software, AI, cybersecurity and data-protection context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian software, web, data, artificial intelligence, networking, cybersecurity, digital services, information systems, privacy and compliance work
findings: NITDA identifies digital skills, software and hardware development, cybersecurity, digital trust, research and an agile technology workforce as Nigerian strategic priorities.
NBTE lists Nigerian programmes and national occupational standards spanning software, web, data, AI, networking, robotics, computer hardware, cybersecurity and digital service operations.
NDPC describes data-protection compliance, information privacy, information audit, data management and information-security evidence relevant to Nigerian privacy and compliance work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technology-sector, training and regulatory context; it does not prove a specific employer requirement, salary, vacancy count or universal certificate for every ICT title.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria statistician and mathematician vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based statistics, mathematics, data and quantitative-analysis employment
findings: Nigeria-focused vacancy pages identify Statistician, Statistics Graduate and combined Statistician/Mathematician roles in Lagos, including National Bureau of Statistics and private-sector signals.
source_summaries.limitations: These are vacancy and institutional title signals, not a national demand count or a universal qualification route for every quantitative role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian digital product-management occupational standard and vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian digital product lifecycle, roadmapping, stakeholder management, product-management tools, Agile/Scrum/Waterfall methods and product-manager employment
findings: NBTE's Digital Product Management standard covers the product lifecycle, roadmaps, stakeholder engagement, product-management software and Agile, Scrum and Waterfall methods; Nigerian job pages identify Product Manager and Product Owner roles with product vision, requirements, roadmaps, backlogs, discovery and cross-functional delivery responsibilities.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a Nigerian occupational and vacancy signal, not a national demand total or a universal certification requirement for every product, business-analysis or innovation role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian procurement, freight and supply-chain professional context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian procurement, purchasing, stores, logistics, supply-chain management, freight forwarding, cargo and professional capacity
findings: CIPSMN identifies procurement, stores, purchasing, supply, logistics and supply-chain management professionals across public and private sectors and describes Nigerian professional certification and training; CRFFN regulates freight forwarding and promotes competence, conduct and supply-chain capacity in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian professional and regulatory pathways; they do not establish one universal certificate or current demand ranking for every procurement, logistics or supply-chain role.

source_summaries.name: NITDA 3MTT Nigerian product, data, cloud, DevOps and digital-skills pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian technical-talent pathways in product management, data analysis, data science, cloud computing, DevOps, UI/UX, quality assurance, software, AI, cybersecurity and game development
findings: NITDA and 3MTT explicitly list product management, data analysis and visualisation, data science, cloud computing, DevOps, UI/UX and quality assurance among Nigerian technical-skill tracks.
source_summaries.limitations: A national training track is evidence of a Nigerian skills pathway and ecosystem signal, not a guarantee of employment demand or a universal requirement for each related subgroup.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian accountancy, audit, financial reporting, banking, insurance, tax and public-finance competency context

source_summaries.name: Jobberman Nigeria jobs
Current Nigerian vacancy-market signals from Jobberman
source_summaries.scope: Current Nigerian vacancy categories and selected finance, insurance, technology, aviation, agriculture, hospitality, legal, engineering and related hiring signals
findings: Jobberman currently exposes Nigerian vacancies across finance, insurance, IT, agriculture, automotive and aviation, legal, healthcare, hospitality, mining and other categories; a listed Financial Analyst vacancy names financial analysis, modelling, reporting and Excel.
The source is used as a dated market signal, not as a complete census of Nigerian hiring or a universal requirement.
source_summaries.limitations: Vacancy counts and titles change; one listing or category count cannot establish a permanent demand ranking, universal skill requirement or licensing rule.

Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian industrial automation, robotics and mechatronics training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian industrial automation, programmable logic controllers, robotics, mechatronics, automated production, assembly, instrumentation and manufacturing technology
findings: NBTE curricula identify Nigerian training in automation and robotics, including relays, switches, contactors, machine programming, automated production lines, numerical control, automated assembly, PLC programming and fault diagnosis, robotics, mechatronics and human-machine interfaces.
source_summaries.limitations: The curricula establish a Nigerian technical-training pathway and competency categories, not evidence that every employer uses the same controller, software, machine or certification.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing and metal-production training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing, foundry, metal forming, machining, fitting, assembly, workshop safety and technical production
findings: NBTE publishes Nigerian national curricula and occupational standards for fabrication and welding, fitting, welding and fabrication, blacksmithing and foundry, and related technical pathways; the standards include safety, statutory compliance, marking out, welding, fastening, bending, thermal cutting, sawing and abrasive cutting.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technical-training and occupational-standard context; it does not prove that every specialist metal role has a distinct local vacancy or that one certificate is universally required.

findings: C-LMIS/CORBON identifies construction as a major Nigerian employer and publishes National Occupational Standards for building trades including electrical installation, carpentry and joinery, masonry, painting and decoration, plumbing, tiling and decorative stonework; CORBON describes standards, compliance, safety, sustainability, builder registration and practice-licence verification.
source_summaries.limitations: The sources support the named building-trade and builder families; they do not establish a Nigerian counterpart for every specialist engineering, transport, energy or infrastructure role in the library.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian industrial automation, robotics and mechatronics training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian industrial automation, programmable logic controllers, robotics, mechatronics, automated production, assembly, instrumentation and manufacturing technology
findings: NBTE curricula identify Nigerian training in automation and robotics, including relays, switches, contactors, machine programming, automated production lines, numerical control, automated assembly, PLC programming and fault diagnosis, robotics, mechatronics and human-machine interfaces.
source_summaries.limitations: The curricula establish a Nigerian technical-training pathway and competency categories, not evidence that every employer uses the same controller, software, machine or certification.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing and metal-production training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing, foundry, metal forming, machining, fitting, assembly, workshop safety and technical production
findings: NBTE publishes Nigerian national curricula and occupational standards for fabrication and welding, fitting, welding and fabrication, blacksmithing and foundry, and related technical pathways; the standards include safety, statutory compliance, marking out, welding, fastening, bending, thermal cutting, sawing and abrasive cutting.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technical-training and occupational-standard context; it does not prove that every specialist metal role has a distinct local vacancy or that one certificate is universally required.

source_summaries.name: NESREA national environmental-regulation review
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian chemicals, waste, energy and environmental-management standards
findings: NESREA reported review of national environmental regulations covering chemicals and waste management and highlighted the role of industry, government, civil society and research in environmental management.
source_summaries.limitations: Regulatory review supports environmental-practice context; it does not establish a certificate or a particular tool for every environmental role.

Construction and Labour Market Information System Nigerian construction National Occupational Standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian construction trades including electrical, carpentry and joinery, masonry, painting, plumbing and tiling
findings: C-LMIS provides Nigerian construction National Occupational Standards across building trades, including electrical, carpentry and joinery, masonry, painting and decorating, plumbing and tiling.
source_summaries.limitations: The standards support construction-trade skills and pathways; they do not establish a licence for every worker or a universal requirement for construction managers and engineers.

source_summaries.name: COREN 2026 engineering regulation and public-safety reforms
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian engineering practice, registration, public safety, project monitoring and anti-quackery context
findings: COREN's 2026 reforms emphasise qualified and registered practitioners, public safety, project monitoring and enforcement against unqualified engineering practice.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports regulated-engineering context; it is not a personal registration requirement for every technician or non-engineering role in an engineering organisation.

Jobberman Nigeria jobs
MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
Nigerian Film Corporation creative-media National Occupational Standards workshop
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian creative-media trades including film, audio, content, photography, animation, graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies
findings: The Nigerian Film Corporation reported a July 2026 critique and validation workshop intended to develop National Occupational Standards for creative-media trades, including film production, audio production, content creation, digital photography, animation, digital graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies.
source_summaries.limitations: The workshop demonstrates Nigerian standardisation activity and named trade families; it does not mean final standards or a personal certificate already exist for every listed role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian architecture, surveying, geospatial and built-environment practice context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian architecture education and registration, surveying and mapping, cadastral and geospatial practice, building-plan approval and built-environment documentation
findings: ARCON controls architecture training and practice and publishes registration and education requirements.
SURCON regulates surveying and mapping practice, while Nigerian building-plan guidance requires appropriately registered professionals to sign and seal relevant plans.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian professional and built-environment context; it does not establish a vacancy count or one licence for every technician, designer, planner, GIS or assistant title.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria civil-engineering technician vacancy signal
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based civil-engineering technician, construction installation and commissioning support
findings: A Nigeria-focused construction vacancy page identifies Civil Engineering Technician work involving construction, installation and commissioning support, engineering drawings, analysis and digital reporting.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a vacancy signal for one role family; it does not establish a national demand count, universal qualification or one software stack for every civil-engineering technician.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian construction, building trades and builder-standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian building construction, building trades, construction skills, safety, quality, professional standards, masonry, carpentry, joinery, painting, plumbing, electrical installation, tiling and decorative stonework
findings: C-LMIS/CORBON identifies construction as a major Nigerian employer and publishes National Occupational Standards for building trades including electrical installation, carpentry and joinery, masonry, painting and decoration, plumbing, tiling and decorative stonework; CORBON describes standards, compliance, safety, sustainability, builder registration and practice-licence verification.
source_summaries.limitations: The sources support the named building-trade and builder families; they do not establish a Nigerian counterpart for every specialist engineering, transport, energy or infrastructure role in the library.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian environmental science, biodiversity, water-quality and environmental-health context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian environmental science, environmental health, biodiversity conservation, water and air quality, pollution control, environmental audit, natural resources and sustainability
findings: NESREA describes Nigerian environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, water-quality and pollution standards, environmental audits, environmental data, ecosystem conservation and research; EHCON regulates and licenses environmental-health specialists, officers, technicians and assistants; the Federal Ministry of Environment identifies chemical, waste, sewage, air-emissions and environmental-health functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian environmental and environmental-health practice context; it is not a national vacancy count and environmental-health registration should not be applied to every environmental scientist or ecologist.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian interior-design postgraduate education and local-practice curriculum
Quantity Surveyors Registration Board of Nigeria 2024 newsletter
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian quantity-surveying practice and professional registration context
findings: The QSRBN newsletter supplies Nigerian quantity-surveying professional-body context and practice material.
source_summaries.limitations: The newsletter supports professional context; specific registration gates must be shown only where the applicable rule is explicit.

source_summaries.name: Standards Organisation of Nigeria building and construction conference
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian building construction standards, structural integrity, materials, risk management and sustainable development
findings: SON reported a 2024 national conference emphasizing standards practice, structural integrity, sustainable materials and risk management in Nigeria's building and construction industry.
source_summaries.limitations: Conference and standards context does not assign one tool or credential to every construction role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian XR and immersive-technology ecosystem signals
source_summaries.scope: Lagos and Nigerian AR/VR/XR training, immersive media, education, healthcare and construction use cases
findings: Lagos XR ecosystem sources describe skills including 360 video, Unity, Unreal Engine, event planning and team leadership; local reporting also describes VR training and Nigerian immersive-technology education and emergency-services use cases.
source_summaries.limitations: These are ecosystem and training signals, not evidence of a national vacancy count or universal tool requirement.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria geological and engineering-geology vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based geological engineering, geotechnical, mining, construction and infrastructure work
findings: Nigeria-focused job listings identify Geological Engineer, Engineering Geologist, Wellsite Geologist and related geotechnical roles in Abuja, Lagos and other Nigerian locations.
source_summaries.limitations: The checked listings demonstrate a Nigerian geological-engineering role family; they do not establish one universal registration, sector requirement or tool stack for every geology or geotechnical role.

source_summaries.name: HotNigerianJobs metallurgical and materials engineering vacancy snapshot
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian metallurgical, materials, steel and welding-related vacancies
findings: The Nigerian discipline page listed metallurgical and materials engineering vacancies, including steel melt-shop and mechanical/metallurgical engineering roles, with welding and fabrication qualifications appearing in requirements.
source_summaries.limitations: Job listings are time-bound and title conventions vary; this is an observed market signal, not a national demand estimate or universal qualification requirement.

source_summaries.name: Jobberman Nigeria jobs
Nigeria mining titles, geoscience and oil-and-gas local-content training framework
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian mineral titles, exploration, quarrying, mining operations, geoscience, drilling, oil-and-gas technical training, local-content competence and NOGICJQS-linked certification
findings: The Mining Cadastre Office identifies reconnaissance, exploration, small-scale mining, quarry and mining leases and administers mineral titles.
NCDMB describes competence-based classroom, practical, on-the-job training and certification across petroleum/geosciences, drilling, production, engineering, HSE and related sectors.
source_summaries.limitations: A mineral title or NOGICJQS/training requirement applies to the relevant activity or project, not automatically to every worker in a mining or energy-adjacent subgroup.

source_summaries.name: MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
Nigerian Association of Metallurgical and Materials Engineers role-context publication
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian metallurgical and materials engineering role families
findings: The publication identifies Nigerian role families including metallurgical engineer, foundry technician and welding/inspection engineer across steel, aluminium, copper, foundry and upstream or midstream settings.
source_summaries.limitations: Professional role context does not establish current vacancy volume or that every role requires professional registration.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian metallurgy, foundry, forging and metal-processing training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian foundry technology, forging, metallurgy, mineral processing, welding, fabrication, alloys, casting, machining, quality and engineering technology
findings: NBTE recognises foundry technology, metallurgy, mineral processing, mechanical, industrial, welding and fabrication engineering technology pathways.
NBTE curriculum material covers foundry development in Nigeria, casting, alloys, molten-metal behaviour and foundry production fundamentals.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technical-training and industry context; it does not establish a vacancy count, one universal plant process or a professional licence for every operator, technician, artisan or manager title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian environmental science, biodiversity, water-quality and environmental-health context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian environmental science, environmental health, biodiversity conservation, water and air quality, pollution control, environmental audit, natural resources and sustainability
findings: NESREA describes Nigerian environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, water-quality and pollution standards, environmental audits, environmental data, ecosystem conservation and research; EHCON regulates and licenses environmental-health specialists, officers, technicians and assistants; the Federal Ministry of Environment identifies chemical, waste, sewage, air-emissions and environmental-health functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian environmental and environmental-health practice context; it is not a national vacancy count and environmental-health registration should not be applied to every environmental scientist or ecologist.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority radiation-safety training for mining
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian solid-mineral mining and processing radiation-safety roles and adjacent technical occupations
findings: NNRA announced a 2026 national course for current or prospective Radiation Safety Officers in mining and mineral processing, covering NORM/TE-NORM, monitoring, dose assessment, radiation protection, handling, transport, waste management and regulatory compliance.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a specialised radiation-safety pathway and does not apply to every mining or geology role.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technical-training and industry context; it does not establish a vacancy count, one universal plant process or a professional licence for every operator, technician, artisan or manager title.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian environmental science, environmental health, biodiversity conservation, water and air quality, pollution control, environmental audit, natural resources and sustainability
findings: NESREA describes Nigerian environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, water-quality and pollution standards, environmental audits, environmental data, ecosystem conservation and research; EHCON regulates and licenses environmental-health specialists, officers, technicians and assistants; the Federal Ministry of Environment identifies chemical, waste, sewage, air-emissions and environmental-health functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian environmental and environmental-health practice context; it is not a national vacancy count and environmental-health registration should not be applied to every environmental scientist or ecologist.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority radiation-safety training for mining
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian solid-mineral mining and processing radiation-safety roles and adjacent technical occupations
findings: NNRA announced a 2026 national course for current or prospective Radiation Safety Officers in mining and mineral processing, covering NORM/TE-NORM, monitoring, dose assessment, radiation protection, handling, transport, waste management and regulatory compliance.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a specialised radiation-safety pathway and does not apply to every mining or geology role.

source_summaries.limitations: Professional role context does not establish current vacancy volume or that every role requires professional registration.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian metallurgy, foundry, forging and metal-processing training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian foundry technology, forging, metallurgy, mineral processing, welding, fabrication, alloys, casting, machining, quality and engineering technology
findings: NBTE recognises foundry technology, metallurgy, mineral processing, mechanical, industrial, welding and fabrication engineering technology pathways.
NBTE curriculum material covers foundry development in Nigeria, casting, alloys, molten-metal behaviour and foundry production fundamentals.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technical-training and industry context; it does not establish a vacancy count, one universal plant process or a professional licence for every operator, technician, artisan or manager title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian environmental science, biodiversity, water-quality and environmental-health context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian environmental science, environmental health, biodiversity conservation, water and air quality, pollution control, environmental audit, natural resources and sustainability
findings: NESREA describes Nigerian environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, water-quality and pollution standards, environmental audits, environmental data, ecosystem conservation and research; EHCON regulates and licenses environmental-health specialists, officers, technicians and assistants; the Federal Ministry of Environment identifies chemical, waste, sewage, air-emissions and environmental-health functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian environmental and environmental-health practice context; it is not a national vacancy count and environmental-health registration should not be applied to every environmental scientist or ecologist.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority radiation-safety training for mining
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian solid-mineral mining and processing radiation-safety roles and adjacent technical occupations
findings: NNRA announced a 2026 national course for current or prospective Radiation Safety Officers in mining and mineral processing, covering NORM/TE-NORM, monitoring, dose assessment, radiation protection, handling, transport, waste management and regulatory compliance.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a specialised radiation-safety pathway and does not apply to every mining or geology role.

NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian aviation approved training organisations, personnel licensing, airworthiness, flight operations, air traffic control and maintenance-repair-overhaul capacity
findings: NCAA publishes approved training organisations and regulations for aviation personnel licensing, training, airworthiness, flight operations and air traffic services.
Federal aviation sources describe new Nigerian MRO capacity and local aviation workforce development.
source_summaries.limitations: Licensing, ratings and approvals apply to defined aviation duties and organisations; they are not generalized to every airport, airline, hospitality or aviation-support job.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operations context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian railway stations, rail operations, train safety, signalling, route planning, airport operations, baggage, airspace and air-transport services, aviation fuel and road-transport administration
findings: NRC describes passenger and goods carriage, station management, train safety, control and signalling, route planning, traffic and commercial operations; NCAA regulates air transport, aviation fuel and aerodrome services; FAAN manages Nigerian commercial airports, airport operations, cargo and passenger services; NAMA describes air-traffic-management, communications, navigation and surveillance; the Federal Ministry of Transportation lists rail, road, engineering and transport-planning functions.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operation context, not a vacancy count or a counterpart for every global vehicle, pipeline, event, warehouse or specialist infrastructure title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian digital-forensics and cybercrime-investigation context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian digital evidence acquisition, forensic analysis, cybercrime investigation, incident understanding and law-enforcement support
findings: Nigeria's National Digital Forensic Laboratory describes forensic acquisition, preservation and analysis of digital evidence as a national cybersecurity capability.
The Nigeria Police Force National Cybercrime Centre provides authorised officers with digital-forensics and cybercrime-investigation protocols and legal-framework resources.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian institutional and occupational context; they do not establish a universal private-sector title, vacancy count or one certificate for every forensic or investigation role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian petroleum operations, process safety and workforce competency context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian upstream, midstream and downstream petroleum operations, control-room work, pipeline and facility safety, competent-person training and permits
findings: NUPRC publishes Nigerian upstream regulations and facility guidelines requiring competent persons, training, safe work procedures and records.
NMDPRA publishes downstream guidelines and MISTDO safety training requirements for downstream personnel.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian petroleum operations and safety context; it does not establish a vacancy count or one credential for every operator, technician, contractor or manager title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian security, fire, border and correctional-service context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fire prevention and rescue, emergency response, border security, immigration control, policing, correctional custody, probation, rehabilitation and public safety
findings: The Federal Fire Service describes fire prevention, mitigation, rescue, life and property protection, training and emergency response; NIS describes border control, surveillance, immigration compliance, airport, seaport, intelligence and cybersecurity functions; NCoS describes secure and humane custody, risk and needs assessment, rehabilitation, probation, parole and non-custodial measures; PSC/NPF materials establish Nigerian police recruitment and service context.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources support the named public-service families and functions; they do not establish a counterpart, private-security licence or vacancy count for every global guard, transport, animal, gaming or specialist rescue title.

Nigerian archives, records, museum collections and digitisation context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian records management, archives, museum collections, cataloguing, conservation, digitisation, audio-visual preservation and public access
findings: The National Archives describes preservation, records-management training, digitisation and training collaborations for archivists and records officers.
National museum and film-archive sources describe collection documentation, cataloguing, imaging, conservation and audio-visual preservation.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources support records and collections practice but do not establish one universal museum, archive or commercial software stack.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE National Occupational Standards and Federal TVET trade pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian vocational and technical pathways including garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web, health and safety and other occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current NOS catalogue names occupational standards and levels for garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web and other trades.
The Federal TVET initiative describes accredited centres, practical skills, employment and entrepreneurship pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS or TVET pathway is evidence of a Nigerian training route, not a claim that every employer requires the listed level or that one trade credential is interchangeable with a degree or professional licence.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian construction-equipment operator training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian construction-equipment operation, excavators, bulldozers, graders, loaders, concrete mixers, maintenance, workplace safety and road regulations
findings: NBTE National Skills Qualifications for Nigerian construction-equipment operations identify operator-helper and operator competencies, daily checks, equipment maintenance, health and safety, road and workplace regulations, and specific excavator, bulldozer, grader, loader and concrete-truck-mixer operation units.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian construction-equipment training context, not a vacancy count or a local counterpart for every mining, snow, cable-vehicle, elevator or specialist crane title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian energy planning, efficiency and sustainable-energy context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian energy policy, planning, statistics, renewable energy, energy efficiency, electricity, fossil fuels and sustainable-energy development
findings: The Energy Commission of Nigeria identifies national energy planning and policy implementation, energy statistics, energy information systems, electricity and fossil-fuel functions, renewable-energy research and energy-efficiency or sustainable-development work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian energy-sector and planning context, not a universal building-assessor licence, project-vacancy count or qualification for every hydropower, pipeline, energy or conservation title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian automotive repair, vehicle engineering, EV and motorsport training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian automobile repair and maintenance, electric and CNG vehicle training, automotive engineering design tools, vehicle inspection and motorsport officials and engineering pathways
findings: Government and NADDC sources describe nationwide automobile-maintenance, electric-vehicle, CNG and automotive software-capacity training.
ATCN describes Nigerian motorsport governance, driver/official training and an FIA engineering scholarship pathway.
source_summaries.limitations: These are sector training and ecosystem signals; they do not establish one universal automotive tool stack or a licence for every vehicle, motorsport or engineering role.

Nigerian digital technology, software, AI, cybersecurity and data-protection context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian software, web, data, artificial intelligence, networking, cybersecurity, digital services, information systems, privacy and compliance work
findings: NITDA identifies digital skills, software and hardware development, cybersecurity, digital trust, research and an agile technology workforce as Nigerian strategic priorities.
NBTE lists Nigerian programmes and national occupational standards spanning software, web, data, AI, networking, robotics, computer hardware, cybersecurity and digital service operations.
NDPC describes data-protection compliance, information privacy, information audit, data management and information-security evidence relevant to Nigerian privacy and compliance work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technology-sector, training and regulatory context; it does not prove a specific employer requirement, salary, vacancy count or universal certificate for every ICT title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian industrial automation, robotics and mechatronics training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian industrial automation, programmable logic controllers, robotics, mechatronics, automated production, assembly, instrumentation and manufacturing technology
findings: NBTE curricula identify Nigerian training in automation and robotics, including relays, switches, contactors, machine programming, automated production lines, numerical control, automated assembly, PLC programming and fault diagnosis, robotics, mechatronics and human-machine interfaces.
source_summaries.limitations: The curricula establish a Nigerian technical-training pathway and competency categories, not evidence that every employer uses the same controller, software, machine or certification.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian petroleum operations, process safety and workforce competency context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian upstream, midstream and downstream petroleum operations, control-room work, pipeline and facility safety, competent-person training and permits
findings: NUPRC publishes Nigerian upstream regulations and facility guidelines requiring competent persons, training, safe work procedures and records.
NMDPRA publishes downstream guidelines and MISTDO safety training requirements for downstream personnel.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian petroleum operations and safety context; it does not establish a vacancy count or one credential for every operator, technician, contractor or manager title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian teacher, technical-instructor and digital-learning training pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian teacher professional development, digital literacy, classroom practice, technical teacher training and education technology implementation
findings: The Federal Ministry of Education's teacher platform describes structured teaching-methodology and digital-literacy modules.
Government education and TVET sources describe technical-teacher training, accredited centres and practical instruction pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: The sources support education-workforce and instructor foundations; they do not establish a universal licence or exact hiring requirement for every teaching, training or coaching title.

NBTE National Occupational Standards and Federal TVET trade pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian vocational and technical pathways including garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web, health and safety and other occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current NOS catalogue names occupational standards and levels for garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web and other trades.
The Federal TVET initiative describes accredited centres, practical skills, employment and entrepreneurship pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS or TVET pathway is evidence of a Nigerian training route, not a claim that every employer requires the listed level or that one trade credential is interchangeable with a degree or professional licence.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian architecture, surveying, geospatial and built-environment practice context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian architecture education and registration, surveying and mapping, cadastral and geospatial practice, building-plan approval and built-environment documentation
findings: ARCON controls architecture training and practice and publishes registration and education requirements.
SURCON regulates surveying and mapping practice, while Nigerian building-plan guidance requires appropriately registered professionals to sign and seal relevant plans.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian professional and built-environment context; it does not establish a vacancy count or one licence for every technician, designer, planner, GIS or assistant title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian geospatial, land administration and smart-urban-planning context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian GIS, cadastral mapping, land administration, housing, urban and regional planning and smart-city applications
findings: Nigerian government and geospatial agencies describe GIS, satellite data, cadastral mapping, land administration, urban planning and smart-city applications as active public-development functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian practice and institutional context; it does not establish a universal licence, employer requirement or demand ranking for every planning or GIS title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian real-estate, valuation, property-management and land-practice context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian estate surveying and valuation, property management, development, land and property agency, housing and real-estate practice
findings: ESVARBON regulates estate surveying and valuation practice in Nigeria and maintains practitioner registration and professional requirements.
NIESV describes valuation, property management, property development and land-related services as parts of the Nigerian profession.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes professional and regulatory context; it does not establish a vacancy count or a licence requirement for every property, housing or agency title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian automotive repair, vehicle engineering, EV and motorsport training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian automobile repair and maintenance, electric and CNG vehicle training, automotive engineering design tools, vehicle inspection and motorsport officials and engineering pathways
findings: Government and NADDC sources describe nationwide automobile-maintenance, electric-vehicle, CNG and automotive software-capacity training.
ATCN describes Nigerian motorsport governance, driver/official training and an FIA engineering scholarship pathway.
source_summaries.limitations: These are sector training and ecosystem signals; they do not establish one universal automotive tool stack or a licence for every vehicle, motorsport or engineering role.

source_summaries.name: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria specialist-practice context

source_summaries.limitations: The board establishes Nigerian professional and regulatory context; it does not establish a current vacancy count or equivalent demand for every specialty.
