Nigeria public-health surveillance, laboratory and emergency-response context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian disease surveillance, public-health laboratories, emergency preparedness and response, field epidemiology, risk communication and health-information coordination
findings: NCDC leads prevention, detection and response to infectious-disease outbreaks and public-health emergencies in Nigeria.

Its functions include surveillance, laboratory networks, emergency preparedness and response, applied epidemiology, research and coordination with state surveillance teams and public-health emergency operations centres.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian public-health system context and relevant work functions; it does not establish a universal licence, vacancy count or identical qualification for every health-support title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian allied-health, radiography, rehabilitation and optometry context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian radiography, nuclear and diagnostic imaging, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, chiropractic, osteopathy, prosthetics and orthotics, optometry and allied-health education
findings: RRBN regulates radiography and related diagnostic or therapeutic radiography practice; MRTB regulates and licenses rehabilitation professions including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, prosthetics/orthotics, chiropractic and osteopathic practice; ODORBN regulates Nigerian optometrists and dispensing opticians; NUC allied-health standards identify Nigerian allied-health degree pathways and professional information practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian digital technology, software, AI, cybersecurity and data-protection context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian software, web, data, artificial intelligence, networking, cybersecurity, digital services, information systems, privacy and compliance work
findings: NITDA identifies digital skills, software and hardware development, cybersecurity, digital trust, research and an agile technology workforce as Nigerian strategic priorities.
NBTE lists Nigerian programmes and national occupational standards spanning software, web, data, AI, networking, robotics, computer hardware, cybersecurity and digital service operations.
NDPC describes data-protection compliance, information privacy, information audit, data management and information-security evidence relevant to Nigerian privacy and compliance work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technology-sector, training and regulatory context; it does not prove a specific employer requirement, salary, vacancy count or universal certificate for every ICT title.

source_summaries.name: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria midwifery context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian midwifery education, registration, licensing and professional practice
findings: NMCN identifies Midwives as a national register, describes basic midwifery registration and qualifying examinations, and provides licensing, renewal and verification services for Nigerian nursing and midwifery professionals.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian midwifery practice and regulatory context; it is not a current vacancy count or a claim about every maternity-care support role.

Nigeria public-health surveillance, laboratory and emergency-response context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian disease surveillance, public-health laboratories, emergency preparedness and response, field epidemiology, risk communication and health-information coordination
findings: NCDC leads prevention, detection and response to infectious-disease outbreaks and public-health emergencies in Nigeria.

Its functions include surveillance, laboratory networks, emergency preparedness and response, applied epidemiology, research and coordination with state surveillance teams and public-health emergency operations centres.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian public-health system context and relevant work functions; it does not establish a universal licence, vacancy count or identical qualification for every health-support title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian allied-health, radiography, rehabilitation and optometry context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian radiography, nuclear and diagnostic imaging, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, chiropractic, osteopathy, prosthetics and orthotics, optometry and allied-health education
findings: RRBN regulates radiography and related diagnostic or therapeutic radiography practice; MRTB regulates and licenses rehabilitation professions including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, prosthetics/orthotics, chiropractic and osteopathic practice; ODORBN regulates Nigerian optometrists and dispensing opticians; NUC allied-health standards identify Nigerian allied-health degree pathways and professional information practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian digital technology, software, AI, cybersecurity and data-protection context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian software, web, data, artificial intelligence, networking, cybersecurity, digital services, information systems, privacy and compliance work
findings: NITDA identifies digital skills, software and hardware development, cybersecurity, digital trust, research and an agile technology workforce as Nigerian strategic priorities.
NBTE lists Nigerian programmes and national occupational standards spanning software, web, data, AI, networking, robotics, computer hardware, cybersecurity and digital service operations.
NDPC describes data-protection compliance, information privacy, information audit, data management and information-security evidence relevant to Nigerian privacy and compliance work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technology-sector, training and regulatory context; it does not prove a specific employer requirement, salary, vacancy count or universal certificate for every ICT title.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian midwifery education, registration, licensing and professional practice

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian midwifery practice and regulatory context; it is not a current vacancy count or a claim about every maternity-care support role.

source_summaries.limitations: The report is sector context, not a role-by-role vacancy census or universal competency specification.

Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria practice and registration framework
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian medicine, dentistry and alternative-medicine practice regulation, provisional registration and housemanship context
findings: MDCN describes its mandate to regulate medicine, dentistry and alternative medicine and provides provisional-registration, housemanship and practitioner-verification services.
source_summaries.limitations: MDCN requirements apply to the regulated professions within its mandate, not to every health, biomedical or administrative role.

source_summaries.name: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria specialist-practice context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian medical registration, specialist qualifications, licensing, housemanship and continuing professional development
findings: MDCN states that medical practice in Nigeria requires appropriate registration and an annual practising licence, and its registration and CPD materials cover additional qualifications, specialist recognition, housemanship and multiple medical specialties.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian legal and professional context for medical specialties; it is not a current vacancy count and does not prove that every specialty has equal local demand.

source_summaries.name: Medical Rehabilitation Therapists Registration Board of Nigeria professional context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, clinical audiology, chiropractic and prosthetics/orthotics regulation
findings: MRTB identifies the Nigerian health professions it regulates, including clinical audiology, chiropractic medicine and prosthetics and orthotics, and provides registration and licence-renewal services for medical rehabilitation professionals.
source_summaries.limitations: The board establishes Nigerian professional and regulatory context; it does not establish a current vacancy count or equivalent demand for every specialty.

National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
Nigeria public-health surveillance, laboratory and emergency-response context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian disease surveillance, public-health laboratories, emergency preparedness and response, field epidemiology, risk communication and health-information coordination
findings: NCDC leads prevention, detection and response to infectious-disease outbreaks and public-health emergencies in Nigeria.

Its functions include surveillance, laboratory networks, emergency preparedness and response, applied epidemiology, research and coordination with state surveillance teams and public-health emergency operations centres.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian public-health system context and relevant work functions; it does not establish a universal licence, vacancy count or identical qualification for every health-support title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian allied-health, radiography, rehabilitation and optometry context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian radiography, nuclear and diagnostic imaging, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, chiropractic, osteopathy, prosthetics and orthotics, optometry and allied-health education
findings: RRBN regulates radiography and related diagnostic or therapeutic radiography practice; MRTB regulates and licenses rehabilitation professions including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, prosthetics/orthotics, chiropractic and osteopathic practice; ODORBN regulates Nigerian optometrists and dispensing opticians; NUC allied-health standards identify Nigerian allied-health degree pathways and professional information practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian digital technology, software, AI, cybersecurity and data-protection context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian software, web, data, artificial intelligence, networking, cybersecurity, digital services, information systems, privacy and compliance work
findings: NITDA identifies digital skills, software and hardware development, cybersecurity, digital trust, research and an agile technology workforce as Nigerian strategic priorities.
NBTE lists Nigerian programmes and national occupational standards spanning software, web, data, AI, networking, robotics, computer hardware, cybersecurity and digital service operations.
NDPC describes data-protection compliance, information privacy, information audit, data management and information-security evidence relevant to Nigerian privacy and compliance work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technology-sector, training and regulatory context; it does not prove a specific employer requirement, salary, vacancy count or universal certificate for every ICT title.

source_summaries.name: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria midwifery context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian midwifery education, registration, licensing and professional practice
findings: NMCN identifies Midwives as a national register, describes basic midwifery registration and qualifying examinations, and provides licensing, renewal and verification services for Nigerian nursing and midwifery professionals.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian midwifery practice and regulatory context; it is not a current vacancy count or a claim about every maternity-care support role.

findings: NIMR describes Nigerian molecular epidemiology, food-safety, immunogenetics, theranostics, microbiome and molecular-technique laboratories; NABDA describes Nigerian biomedical biotechnology work in immunology, vaccinology, antibody generation, DNA, biobanking and diagnostics; NIPRD describes pharmaceutical, biological-product, toxicology, quality-assurance and environmental-science research.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian research and institutional role families, not a vacancy count, personal licence or universal academic route for every biomedical or scientific occupation.

Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security National Agricultural Growth Strategy 2.0
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian agriculture, food security, agribusiness, crop and livestock production and agricultural technology context
findings: The strategy document describes agriculture's Nigerian economic and food-security role and references the National Agricultural Technology and Innovation Policy 2022-2027.
source_summaries.limitations: A national strategy establishes sector context and priorities, not a role-specific certification or employer requirement.

source_summaries.name: Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare hospital-services policy resources
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian health-facility, laboratory quality, biosafety, patient-safety, eye-health and oxygen-care guidance
findings: The ministry lists a 2024 guideline on integration of medical laboratory services, a 2025 guideline on medical-laboratory quality management, and a 2026 guideline on laboratory biosafety and biosecurity.
The same policy resource lists patient-safety and care-quality guidance and an eye-health strategic plan for 2024-2028.
source_summaries.limitations: These are system and practice guidance documents; they do not by themselves establish an individual licence or a vacancy for every health occupation.

source_summaries.name: Federal Ministry of Health State of Health of the Nation Report 2024
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian health-system workforce and service-delivery context reported for 2024
findings: The report describes Nigeria's primary, secondary and tertiary health-delivery levels and discusses doctors, dentists, mental-health and rehabilitation professionals in the national health system.
source_summaries.limitations: The report is sector context, not a role-by-role vacancy census or universal competency specification.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian health-profession regulators
Nigerian health records registration and digital health information context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian health records officers, health-information management, registration and licensure, electronic content management, digital health, EMR/EHR, data quality and confidentiality
findings: The Federal Ministry of Health describes HRORBN registration, digital compliance and health-records workforce demand, and describes ECM and national digital-health/EMR direction.
source_summaries.limitations: The regulatory requirement applies to defined health-records practice; digital-health context does not make every medical, data or administrative role a registered health-records profession.

source_summaries.name: Jobberman Nigeria jobs
MDCN and MLSCN Nigerian medical, dental and laboratory registration and training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian medical and dental education, housemanship, professional registration, annual practice licensing, medical laboratory training, laboratory registration and continuing professional development
findings: MDCN publishes medical and dental education, accreditation, registration, practising-licence and CPD services.
MLSCN publishes medical-laboratory training, registration, licensure, laboratory accreditation and CPD services, including the 2025 ND curriculum.
source_summaries.limitations: The regulations apply to defined health professions and facilities; they do not establish a universal licence for every health-support, research, technology or administrative role.

source_summaries.name: Medical Laboratory Science Council of Nigeria mandate and licensing portal
MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
NBRDA genetics, genomics and bioinformatics workshop
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian molecular biology, genetics, genomics, bioinformatics and public research infrastructure
findings: NBRDA reported a practical workshop through its Genetics, Genomics and Bioinformatics Department and connected it to Nigeria BioGenome and national genomics/bioinformatics data infrastructure goals.
source_summaries.limitations: The workshop supports Nigerian research and skills context; it does not establish broad private-sector demand or a universal certificate.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
Nigerian agricultural research, horticulture, crop, livestock and extension context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian crop production, horticulture, livestock, plant genetics, biotechnology, agricultural training, extension and production improvement
findings: ARCN coordinates agricultural research, training and extension through national institutes and colleges across Nigeria's agro-ecological zones; its plant-resources work covers crop improvement, seed production, irrigation, pest and disease management, genetics and biotechnology; NIHORT covers fruits, vegetables, spices, ornamentals, post-harvest processing and sustainable horticultural production; NBTE lists Nigerian crop-production and livestock-production technical pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian agricultural role-family and training context, not a universal farm system, commodity, equipment stack, licence or vacancy count for every agricultural occupation.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria environmental-scientist vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based environmental monitoring, assessment, compliance, remediation and field-science work
findings: Nigeria-based listings identify Environmental Scientist roles involving environmental data collection, sampling, analysis, impact or compliance work, reporting and field health, safety and environmental requirements.
source_summaries.limitations: The listings demonstrate a Nigerian environmental-science role family; they do not establish one universal environmental licence, certification, employer requirement or software stack.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria microbiologist vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based microbiology, laboratory testing, quality control, food, pharmaceutical, environmental and research work
findings: Nigeria-focused biological-sciences vacancy pages identify Microbiologist roles in Port Harcourt and Lagos involving laboratory testing, experimental protocols, quality control, food, pharmaceutical and environmental applications.
source_summaries.limitations: The listings demonstrate a Nigerian microbiology role family; they do not establish one universal laboratory credential, instrument stack or regulator for every microbiology setting.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian biomedical, biotechnology, pharmaceutical and epidemiology research context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian biomedical research, molecular biology, biotechnology, immunology, epidemiology, toxicology, pharmacology, diagnostics, vaccines and pharmaceutical development
findings: NIMR describes Nigerian molecular epidemiology, food-safety, immunogenetics, theranostics, microbiome and molecular-technique laboratories; NABDA describes Nigerian biomedical biotechnology work in immunology, vaccinology, antibody generation, DNA, biobanking and diagnostics; NIPRD describes pharmaceutical, biological-product, toxicology, quality-assurance and environmental-science research.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian research and institutional role families, not a vacancy count, personal licence or universal academic route for every biomedical or scientific occupation.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian environmental science, biodiversity, water-quality and environmental-health context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian environmental science, environmental health, biodiversity conservation, water and air quality, pollution control, environmental audit, natural resources and sustainability
findings: NESREA describes Nigerian environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, water-quality and pollution standards, environmental audits, environmental data, ecosystem conservation and research; EHCON regulates and licenses environmental-health specialists, officers, technicians and assistants; the Federal Ministry of Environment identifies chemical, waste, sewage, air-emissions and environmental-health functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian environmental and environmental-health practice context; it is not a national vacancy count and environmental-health registration should not be applied to every environmental scientist or ecologist.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian fisheries, aquaculture and aquatic-research context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fisheries, aquaculture development, aquatic research, training, extension, marine and inland-water resources and sustainable production
findings: The Agricultural Research Council of Nigeria identifies a Fisheries and Aquaculture department responsible for coordinating, supervising and regulating research and training, policy, facilities, industry collaboration, sustainable practices and productivity across Nigerian fisheries and aquaculture institutions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian fisheries and aquaculture institutional context, not a vacancy count or one universal qualification, species, production system or equipment stack.

source_summaries.name: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria registration and approved schools
University of Ibadan AFRIGENE genomics and computational-skills programme
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian genomics, bioinformatics, computational biology, evolutionary biology and biodiversity research skills
findings: The University of Ibadan described AFRIGENE 2026 hands-on learning focused on computational tools and approaches for genomics, evolutionary biology and biodiversity conservation.
source_summaries.limitations: University training is research and capacity-building evidence, not a role-specific vacancy or licence requirement.

source_summaries.name: Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare hospital-services policy resources
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian health-facility, laboratory quality, biosafety, patient-safety, eye-health and oxygen-care guidance

The same policy resource lists patient-safety and care-quality guidance and an eye-health strategic plan for 2024-2028.
source_summaries.limitations: These are system and practice guidance documents; they do not by themselves establish an individual licence or a vacancy for every health occupation.

source_summaries.limitations: The report is sector context, not a role-by-role vacancy census or universal competency specification.

Nigerian agricultural research, horticulture, crop, livestock and extension context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian crop production, horticulture, livestock, plant genetics, biotechnology, agricultural training, extension and production improvement
findings: ARCN coordinates agricultural research, training and extension through national institutes and colleges across Nigeria's agro-ecological zones; its plant-resources work covers crop improvement, seed production, irrigation, pest and disease management, genetics and biotechnology; NIHORT covers fruits, vegetables, spices, ornamentals, post-harvest processing and sustainable horticultural production; NBTE lists Nigerian crop-production and livestock-production technical pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian agricultural role-family and training context, not a universal farm system, commodity, equipment stack, licence or vacancy count for every agricultural occupation.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria environmental-scientist vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based environmental monitoring, assessment, compliance, remediation and field-science work
findings: Nigeria-based listings identify Environmental Scientist roles involving environmental data collection, sampling, analysis, impact or compliance work, reporting and field health, safety and environmental requirements.
source_summaries.limitations: The listings demonstrate a Nigerian environmental-science role family; they do not establish one universal environmental licence, certification, employer requirement or software stack.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria microbiologist vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based microbiology, laboratory testing, quality control, food, pharmaceutical, environmental and research work
findings: Nigeria-focused biological-sciences vacancy pages identify Microbiologist roles in Port Harcourt and Lagos involving laboratory testing, experimental protocols, quality control, food, pharmaceutical and environmental applications.
source_summaries.limitations: The listings demonstrate a Nigerian microbiology role family; they do not establish one universal laboratory credential, instrument stack or regulator for every microbiology setting.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian biomedical, biotechnology, pharmaceutical and epidemiology research context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian biomedical research, molecular biology, biotechnology, immunology, epidemiology, toxicology, pharmacology, diagnostics, vaccines and pharmaceutical development
findings: NIMR describes Nigerian molecular epidemiology, food-safety, immunogenetics, theranostics, microbiome and molecular-technique laboratories; NABDA describes Nigerian biomedical biotechnology work in immunology, vaccinology, antibody generation, DNA, biobanking and diagnostics; NIPRD describes pharmaceutical, biological-product, toxicology, quality-assurance and environmental-science research.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian research and institutional role families, not a vacancy count, personal licence or universal academic route for every biomedical or scientific occupation.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian environmental science, biodiversity, water-quality and environmental-health context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian environmental science, environmental health, biodiversity conservation, water and air quality, pollution control, environmental audit, natural resources and sustainability
findings: NESREA describes Nigerian environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, water-quality and pollution standards, environmental audits, environmental data, ecosystem conservation and research; EHCON regulates and licenses environmental-health specialists, officers, technicians and assistants; the Federal Ministry of Environment identifies chemical, waste, sewage, air-emissions and environmental-health functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian environmental and environmental-health practice context; it is not a national vacancy count and environmental-health registration should not be applied to every environmental scientist or ecologist.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian fisheries, aquaculture and aquatic-research context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fisheries, aquaculture development, aquatic research, training, extension, marine and inland-water resources and sustainable production
findings: The Agricultural Research Council of Nigeria identifies a Fisheries and Aquaculture department responsible for coordinating, supervising and regulating research and training, policy, facilities, industry collaboration, sustainable practices and productivity across Nigerian fisheries and aquaculture institutions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian fisheries and aquaculture institutional context, not a vacancy count or one universal qualification, species, production system or equipment stack.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian crop production, horticulture, livestock, plant genetics, biotechnology, agricultural training, extension and production improvement
findings: ARCN coordinates agricultural research, training and extension through national institutes and colleges across Nigeria's agro-ecological zones; its plant-resources work covers crop improvement, seed production, irrigation, pest and disease management, genetics and biotechnology; NIHORT covers fruits, vegetables, spices, ornamentals, post-harvest processing and sustainable horticultural production; NBTE lists Nigerian crop-production and livestock-production technical pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian agricultural role-family and training context, not a universal farm system, commodity, equipment stack, licence or vacancy count for every agricultural occupation.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria environmental-scientist vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based environmental monitoring, assessment, compliance, remediation and field-science work
findings: Nigeria-based listings identify Environmental Scientist roles involving environmental data collection, sampling, analysis, impact or compliance work, reporting and field health, safety and environmental requirements.
source_summaries.limitations: The listings demonstrate a Nigerian environmental-science role family; they do not establish one universal environmental licence, certification, employer requirement or software stack.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria microbiologist vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based microbiology, laboratory testing, quality control, food, pharmaceutical, environmental and research work
findings: Nigeria-focused biological-sciences vacancy pages identify Microbiologist roles in Port Harcourt and Lagos involving laboratory testing, experimental protocols, quality control, food, pharmaceutical and environmental applications.
source_summaries.limitations: The listings demonstrate a Nigerian microbiology role family; they do not establish one universal laboratory credential, instrument stack or regulator for every microbiology setting.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian biomedical, biotechnology, pharmaceutical and epidemiology research context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian biomedical research, molecular biology, biotechnology, immunology, epidemiology, toxicology, pharmacology, diagnostics, vaccines and pharmaceutical development
findings: NIMR describes Nigerian molecular epidemiology, food-safety, immunogenetics, theranostics, microbiome and molecular-technique laboratories; NABDA describes Nigerian biomedical biotechnology work in immunology, vaccinology, antibody generation, DNA, biobanking and diagnostics; NIPRD describes pharmaceutical, biological-product, toxicology, quality-assurance and environmental-science research.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian research and institutional role families, not a vacancy count, personal licence or universal academic route for every biomedical or scientific occupation.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian environmental science, biodiversity, water-quality and environmental-health context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian environmental science, environmental health, biodiversity conservation, water and air quality, pollution control, environmental audit, natural resources and sustainability
findings: NESREA describes Nigerian environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, water-quality and pollution standards, environmental audits, environmental data, ecosystem conservation and research; EHCON regulates and licenses environmental-health specialists, officers, technicians and assistants; the Federal Ministry of Environment identifies chemical, waste, sewage, air-emissions and environmental-health functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian environmental and environmental-health practice context; it is not a national vacancy count and environmental-health registration should not be applied to every environmental scientist or ecologist.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian fisheries and aquaculture institutional context, not a vacancy count or one universal qualification, species, production system or equipment stack.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian biomedical, biotechnology, pharmaceutical and epidemiology research context

findings: The Nigeria Association of Clinical Psychologists describes standardisation, practice regulation, training, continuing education and clinical-psychology services in Nigerian health and community settings; a Nigerian clinical initiative also identifies licensed clinical psychologists and supervised clinical roles.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish a Nigerian clinical-psychology role and professional pathway; they do not establish a national vacancy count or a single universal route for every psychology-adjacent role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian psychology professional-body context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian psychology education, membership, psychosocial service and professional-development context
findings: The Nigerian Psychological Association describes psychology practice, education, research and psychosocial services in the public interest and lists Nigerian membership pathways for students, graduates, associates and full members.
source_summaries.limitations: The professional-body page establishes Nigerian psychology practice context; it is not a vacancy count and does not by itself settle every licensing or specialty requirement.

source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian physiotherapy, rehabilitation, radiography, medical laboratory, nutrition, occupational therapy, audiology and related allied-health practice

Nigerian university curricula describe anatomy, physiology, therapeutic exercise and patient-care preparation for rehabilitation practice.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian profession and education context; exact registration, scope and supervision depend on the profession and current regulator, and it does not establish a vacancy count for every therapy title.

Nigerian allied-health regulators establish profession-specific registration boundaries for rehabilitation and related patient-facing practice.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian wellness and lifestyle-medicine context; it does not establish one licence or clinical scope for every coach, trainer, therapist, dietitian or recreational role.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian wellness and lifestyle-medicine context; it does not establish one licence or clinical scope for every coach, trainer, therapist, dietitian or recreational role.

Nigerian allied-health, radiography, rehabilitation and optometry context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian radiography, nuclear and diagnostic imaging, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, chiropractic, osteopathy, prosthetics and orthotics, optometry and allied-health education
findings: RRBN regulates radiography and related diagnostic or therapeutic radiography practice; MRTB regulates and licenses rehabilitation professions including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, prosthetics/orthotics, chiropractic and osteopathic practice; ODORBN regulates Nigerian optometrists and dispensing opticians; NUC allied-health standards identify Nigerian allied-health degree pathways and professional information practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian lifestyle medicine, rehabilitation, fitness and wellness context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian lifestyle medicine, nutrition, rehabilitation, health coaching, physical activity, behavioural change and allied-health practice
findings: The Society of Lifestyle Medicine of Nigeria describes a multidisciplinary community including physicians, allied-health professionals, researchers, educators, medical students and health coaches and promotes evidence-based lifestyle interventions.
Nigerian allied-health regulators establish profession-specific registration boundaries for rehabilitation and related patient-facing practice.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian wellness and lifestyle-medicine context; it does not establish one licence or clinical scope for every coach, trainer, therapist, dietitian or recreational role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian sports coaching, fitness, exercise and wellness training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian sports coaching, strength and conditioning, fitness instruction, personal training, exercise, massage, recreation and wellness support
findings: An NBTE National Diploma curriculum for sports coaching and training includes anatomy and physiology of sport, strength and conditioning, fitness and massage and practical sport training.
Nigerian lifestyle-medicine and allied-health sources provide adjacent context for exercise, rehabilitation and behaviour-change work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes training and adjacent professional context; it does not imply that every trainer, coach, massage or leisure title is a regulated clinical profession or that one certificate is mandatory for all roles.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian radiography, nuclear and diagnostic imaging, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, chiropractic, osteopathy, prosthetics and orthotics, optometry and allied-health education
findings: RRBN regulates radiography and related diagnostic or therapeutic radiography practice; MRTB regulates and licenses rehabilitation professions including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, prosthetics/orthotics, chiropractic and osteopathic practice; ODORBN regulates Nigerian optometrists and dispensing opticians; NUC allied-health standards identify Nigerian allied-health degree pathways and professional information practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian lifestyle medicine, rehabilitation, fitness and wellness context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian lifestyle medicine, nutrition, rehabilitation, health coaching, physical activity, behavioural change and allied-health practice
findings: The Society of Lifestyle Medicine of Nigeria describes a multidisciplinary community including physicians, allied-health professionals, researchers, educators, medical students and health coaches and promotes evidence-based lifestyle interventions.
Nigerian allied-health regulators establish profession-specific registration boundaries for rehabilitation and related patient-facing practice.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian wellness and lifestyle-medicine context; it does not establish one licence or clinical scope for every coach, trainer, therapist, dietitian or recreational role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian sports coaching, fitness, exercise and wellness training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian sports coaching, strength and conditioning, fitness instruction, personal training, exercise, massage, recreation and wellness support
findings: An NBTE National Diploma curriculum for sports coaching and training includes anatomy and physiology of sport, strength and conditioning, fitness and massage and practical sport training.
Nigerian lifestyle-medicine and allied-health sources provide adjacent context for exercise, rehabilitation and behaviour-change work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes training and adjacent professional context; it does not imply that every trainer, coach, massage or leisure title is a regulated clinical profession or that one certificate is mandatory for all roles.

source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

Nigerian allied-health regulators establish profession-specific registration boundaries for rehabilitation and related patient-facing practice.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian wellness and lifestyle-medicine context; it does not establish one licence or clinical scope for every coach, trainer, therapist, dietitian or recreational role.

source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based business-analysis and operational analytics work
findings: Nigeria-focused MyJobMag pages identify Business Analyst vacancies, including an analyst role in Lagos supporting business objectives, analysis, testing and solution delivery.
source_summaries.limitations: These are vacancy and title signals, not a national demand count, universal qualification requirement or evidence that every business-analyst speciality uses the same tools.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: National Electronic Labour Exchange Nigerian customer-service and administrative vacancy
Nigerian energy planning, efficiency and sustainable-energy context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian energy policy, planning, statistics, renewable energy, energy efficiency, electricity, fossil fuels and sustainable-energy development
findings: The Energy Commission of Nigeria identifies national energy planning and policy implementation, energy statistics, energy information systems, electricity and fossil-fuel functions, renewable-energy research and energy-efficiency or sustainable-development work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian energy-sector and planning context, not a universal building-assessor licence, project-vacancy count or qualification for every hydropower, pipeline, energy or conservation title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian public-service administration, integrity, privacy and compliance context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian public administration, policy, planning, public-sector compliance, anti-corruption, ethics, data protection and government records or programme work
findings: OHCSF publishes Nigerian public-service rules, policy and civil-service resources; ICPC describes review of public-body systems, anti-corruption transparency units, monitoring, reporting, ethics and compliance work in MDAs; NDPC documents data-protection compliance, audits, data-protection officers and licensed compliance organisations in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian public-service and compliance functions; they are not evidence that every global public-office title exists locally, nor a universal qualification or vacancy count for each role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian procurement, freight and supply-chain professional context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian procurement, purchasing, stores, logistics, supply-chain management, freight forwarding, cargo and professional capacity
findings: CIPSMN identifies procurement, stores, purchasing, supply, logistics and supply-chain management professionals across public and private sectors and describes Nigerian professional certification and training; CRFFN regulates freight forwarding and promotes competence, conduct and supply-chain capacity in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian professional and regulatory pathways; they do not establish one universal certificate or current demand ranking for every procurement, logistics or supply-chain role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian project-management professional and regulatory pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian project management, PMO, programme delivery, project consulting, professional development, certification and practice standards
findings: PMI Nigeria describes a Nigerian project-management professional community, learning, job and networking pathways; CIPMN describes Nigerian training, examination, certification, licensing, supervision and standards for project managers and PMO or consulting practitioners.
source_summaries.limitations: The bodies establish professional and training pathways, not a national vacancy count or a universal requirement that every project or programme worker hold a particular credential.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Management professional standards and pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian management, leadership, administration, organisational development, professional membership and management-practice standards
findings: The Nigerian Institute of Management (Chartered) states that its charter empowers it to control and regulate management practice in Nigeria, build management and leadership capacity and support members in managerial and executive positions across public and private sectors.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes management-profession context and a professional pathway; it is not a vacancy count or proof that every management, executive or business role requires NIM membership.

source_summaries.name: NITDA 3MTT Nigerian product, data, cloud, DevOps and digital-skills pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian technical-talent pathways in product management, data analysis, data science, cloud computing, DevOps, UI/UX, quality assurance, software, AI, cybersecurity and game development
findings: NITDA and 3MTT explicitly list product management, data analysis and visualisation, data science, cloud computing, DevOps, UI/UX and quality assurance among Nigerian technical-skill tracks.
source_summaries.limitations: A national training track is evidence of a Nigerian skills pathway and ecosystem signal, not a guarantee of employment demand or a universal requirement for each related subgroup.

source_summaries.name: SMEDAN Nigerian founder, MSME, entrepreneurship and business-development training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian MSME capacity building, entrepreneurship training, business development, access to finance, market support and founder development
findings: SMEDAN describes entrepreneurship training, capacity building, finance, markets and founder support for Nigerian nano, micro and small enterprises.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports entrepreneurial and business-development foundations; it does not establish a universal founder credential, company-registration outcome or demand ranking for every management role.

Nigerian energy planning, efficiency and sustainable-energy context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian energy policy, planning, statistics, renewable energy, energy efficiency, electricity, fossil fuels and sustainable-energy development
findings: The Energy Commission of Nigeria identifies national energy planning and policy implementation, energy statistics, energy information systems, electricity and fossil-fuel functions, renewable-energy research and energy-efficiency or sustainable-development work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian energy-sector and planning context, not a universal building-assessor licence, project-vacancy count or qualification for every hydropower, pipeline, energy or conservation title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian public-service administration, integrity, privacy and compliance context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian public administration, policy, planning, public-sector compliance, anti-corruption, ethics, data protection and government records or programme work
findings: OHCSF publishes Nigerian public-service rules, policy and civil-service resources; ICPC describes review of public-body systems, anti-corruption transparency units, monitoring, reporting, ethics and compliance work in MDAs; NDPC documents data-protection compliance, audits, data-protection officers and licensed compliance organisations in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian public-service and compliance functions; they are not evidence that every global public-office title exists locally, nor a universal qualification or vacancy count for each role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian procurement, freight and supply-chain professional context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian procurement, purchasing, stores, logistics, supply-chain management, freight forwarding, cargo and professional capacity
findings: CIPSMN identifies procurement, stores, purchasing, supply, logistics and supply-chain management professionals across public and private sectors and describes Nigerian professional certification and training; CRFFN regulates freight forwarding and promotes competence, conduct and supply-chain capacity in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian professional and regulatory pathways; they do not establish one universal certificate or current demand ranking for every procurement, logistics or supply-chain role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian project-management professional and regulatory pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian project management, PMO, programme delivery, project consulting, professional development, certification and practice standards
findings: PMI Nigeria describes a Nigerian project-management professional community, learning, job and networking pathways; CIPMN describes Nigerian training, examination, certification, licensing, supervision and standards for project managers and PMO or consulting practitioners.
source_summaries.limitations: The bodies establish professional and training pathways, not a national vacancy count or a universal requirement that every project or programme worker hold a particular credential.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Management professional standards and pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian management, leadership, administration, organisational development, professional membership and management-practice standards
findings: The Nigerian Institute of Management (Chartered) states that its charter empowers it to control and regulate management practice in Nigeria, build management and leadership capacity and support members in managerial and executive positions across public and private sectors.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes management-profession context and a professional pathway; it is not a vacancy count or proof that every management, executive or business role requires NIM membership.

source_summaries.name: NITDA 3MTT Nigerian product, data, cloud, DevOps and digital-skills pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian technical-talent pathways in product management, data analysis, data science, cloud computing, DevOps, UI/UX, quality assurance, software, AI, cybersecurity and game development
findings: NITDA and 3MTT explicitly list product management, data analysis and visualisation, data science, cloud computing, DevOps, UI/UX and quality assurance among Nigerian technical-skill tracks.
source_summaries.limitations: A national training track is evidence of a Nigerian skills pathway and ecosystem signal, not a guarantee of employment demand or a universal requirement for each related subgroup.

source_summaries.name: SMEDAN Nigerian founder, MSME, entrepreneurship and business-development training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian MSME capacity building, entrepreneurship training, business development, access to finance, market support and founder development
findings: SMEDAN describes entrepreneurship training, capacity building, finance, markets and founder support for Nigerian nano, micro and small enterprises.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports entrepreneurial and business-development foundations; it does not establish a universal founder credential, company-registration outcome or demand ranking for every management role.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian human-resource management, labour law, employment relations, talent, training, compensation, workforce development, HR practitioner licensing and professional education
findings: CIPM identifies Nigerian HR membership, examination and professional routes and covers labour law, employment relations, HR management and labour-market analysis.
The Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment describes staff development, welfare, workforce training and labour-governance responsibilities.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian HR and labour-practice context; it does not establish a vacancy count, one qualification or one licence for every people, learning, coaching, public-service or organisational-development title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian public-service administration, integrity, privacy and compliance context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian public administration, policy, planning, public-sector compliance, anti-corruption, ethics, data protection and government records or programme work
findings: OHCSF publishes Nigerian public-service rules, policy and civil-service resources; ICPC describes review of public-body systems, anti-corruption transparency units, monitoring, reporting, ethics and compliance work in MDAs; NDPC documents data-protection compliance, audits, data-protection officers and licensed compliance organisations in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian public-service and compliance functions; they are not evidence that every global public-office title exists locally, nor a universal qualification or vacancy count for each role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Management professional standards and pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian management, leadership, administration, organisational development, professional membership and management-practice standards
findings: The Nigerian Institute of Management (Chartered) states that its charter empowers it to control and regulate management practice in Nigeria, build management and leadership capacity and support members in managerial and executive positions across public and private sectors.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes management-profession context and a professional pathway; it is not a vacancy count or proof that every management, executive or business role requires NIM membership.

source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian sales and customer-facing practice context, not a vacancy count or a universal certification requirement for every sales, retail, trading, service or commercial title.

source_summaries.limitations: This is a Nigerian occupational and vacancy signal, not a national demand total or a universal certification requirement for every product, business-analysis or innovation role.

Nigerian hospitality, catering, travel and tourism training and regulation context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian hotels, restaurants, catering, accommodation, front office, housekeeping, food and beverage, travel, tours, events, recreation, tourism promotion and hospitality standards
findings: The Federal Ministry describes NIHOTOUR as Nigeria's hospitality and tourism training arm with professional and technical programmes; NTDA describes national tourism development, regulation, promotion, capacity building and accreditation of hotels, restaurants, travel agencies, tour operators and related enterprises; official sector sources identify hotel, catering, recreation, tourism safety and tourism-ethics functions.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian hospitality and tourism role-family context, not a vacancy count or a universal certification for every service, food, travel or entertainment title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian sales, customer relationship and consumer-market practice context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian sales management, customer relationship management, account management, customer experience, commercial execution, consumer information and fair marketing
findings: Nigerian sales and customer-facing professional bodies and training programmes identify sales planning, prospecting, consultative selling, negotiation, pipeline and performance management, account development, customer experience and service recovery; FCCPC identifies Nigerian consumer-information, fair-marketing, sales-record, product-safety and sales-promotion obligations; NIMN provides related marketing-professional context.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian sales and customer-facing practice context, not a vacancy count or a universal certification requirement for every sales, retail, trading, service or commercial title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian procurement, freight and supply-chain professional context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian procurement, purchasing, stores, logistics, supply-chain management, freight forwarding, cargo and professional capacity
findings: CIPSMN identifies procurement, stores, purchasing, supply, logistics and supply-chain management professionals across public and private sectors and describes Nigerian professional certification and training; CRFFN regulates freight forwarding and promotes competence, conduct and supply-chain capacity in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian professional and regulatory pathways; they do not establish one universal certificate or current demand ranking for every procurement, logistics or supply-chain role.

findings: The Federal Ministry describes NIHOTOUR as Nigeria's hospitality and tourism training arm with professional and technical programmes; NTDA describes national tourism development, regulation, promotion, capacity building and accreditation of hotels, restaurants, travel agencies, tour operators and related enterprises; official sector sources identify hotel, catering, recreation, tourism safety and tourism-ethics functions.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian hospitality and tourism role-family context, not a vacancy count or a universal certification for every service, food, travel or entertainment title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian sales, customer relationship and consumer-market practice context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian sales management, customer relationship management, account management, customer experience, commercial execution, consumer information and fair marketing
findings: Nigerian sales and customer-facing professional bodies and training programmes identify sales planning, prospecting, consultative selling, negotiation, pipeline and performance management, account development, customer experience and service recovery; FCCPC identifies Nigerian consumer-information, fair-marketing, sales-record, product-safety and sales-promotion obligations; NIMN provides related marketing-professional context.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian sales and customer-facing practice context, not a vacancy count or a universal certification requirement for every sales, retail, trading, service or commercial title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian procurement, freight and supply-chain professional context

source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian professional and regulatory pathways; they do not establish one universal certificate or current demand ranking for every procurement, logistics or supply-chain role.

Nigerian customs, tariff, trade facilitation and border-compliance context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian customs clearance, tariff and valuation, import/export documentation, trade facilitation, authorised economic operators, enforcement, border security and customs digital systems
findings: Nigeria Customs Service identifies revenue collection, trade facilitation, border security, enforcement, compliance and digital customs services as core functions.
The Nigeria Trade Portal exposes tariff search, trader guidance, manifests, declarations, licences, permits and a single-window workflow for trade actors.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian customs and trade-work context; it does not establish a vacancy count, one customs-agent licence or the requirements for every import, export, logistics or policy title.

source_summaries.name: EU-funded project delivery and international-development role signal in Nigeria
source_summaries.scope: EU-funded and ECOWAS-linked project delivery roles based in Abuja, Nigeria
findings: A 2026 Abuja project-officer vacancy describes an EU-funded ECOWAS-linked project and project-management responsibilities in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a dated vacancy signal, not proof of a permanent Nigerian occupation, universal requirement or demand ranking for EU-funds managers.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian marketing, advertising, journalism and media-training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing, advertising, public relations, journalism, mass communication, graphic and digital media practice and training
findings: NIMN identifies marketing as a chartered Nigerian profession with standards, certification, ethics and continuing development; APCON identifies statutory regulation, registration, advertising standards and advert-vetting functions; NIJ documents practical training in print, broadcast, online journalism, public relations, advertising, photojournalism, news writing, editing and radio/television production; NBTE lists Nigerian mass-communication and graphic-design curricula.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian professional, training and regulatory context; they are not a vacancy count and do not make one credential mandatory for every communications, creative or commercial role.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria procurement and purchasing vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based procurement, purchasing, sourcing, supplier, contract and supply-chain work
findings: Nigeria-focused vacancy pages identify Procurement Manager and Purchasing Manager roles across agriculture, oil and gas, manufacturing, construction, hospitality, pharmaceuticals and other sectors, with sourcing, vendor management, negotiation and supply-chain responsibilities.
source_summaries.limitations: The listings demonstrate a local procurement role family; they do not establish one universal certification, procurement system, sector requirement or national demand total.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian public-service administration, integrity, privacy and compliance context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian public administration, policy, planning, public-sector compliance, anti-corruption, ethics, data protection and government records or programme work
findings: OHCSF publishes Nigerian public-service rules, policy and civil-service resources; ICPC describes review of public-body systems, anti-corruption transparency units, monitoring, reporting, ethics and compliance work in MDAs; NDPC documents data-protection compliance, audits, data-protection officers and licensed compliance organisations in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian public-service and compliance functions; they are not evidence that every global public-office title exists locally, nor a universal qualification or vacancy count for each role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian textile, garment and trade value-chain context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian textile and garment production, wholesale trade, import/export documentation, customs and local-content value chains
findings: CBN describes a Nigerian cotton, textile and garment value-chain resuscitation initiative, while the Nigeria Trade Portal provides textile and garment trader procedures, customs, certificates and cross-border documentation.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes a Nigerian textile-trade context; it does not establish a vacancy count or imply that every wholesale trader needs the same permit or credential.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria warehouse, logistics and supply-chain vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based warehouse management, inventory, logistics, fulfilment and end-to-end supply-chain operations
findings: Nigeria-focused listings identify Warehouse Manager, Logistics Manager, Warehouse/Logistics Manager, Inventory Manager and Operations & Supply Chain Manager work involving receiving, storage, fulfilment, dispatch, inventory accuracy, warehousing and last-mile delivery.
source_summaries.limitations: The listings demonstrate Nigerian warehouse and logistics role families; they do not establish one universal warehouse system, qualification, salary or demand total.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian procurement, freight and supply-chain professional context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian procurement, purchasing, stores, logistics, supply-chain management, freight forwarding, cargo and professional capacity
findings: CIPSMN identifies procurement, stores, purchasing, supply, logistics and supply-chain management professionals across public and private sectors and describes Nigerian professional certification and training; CRFFN regulates freight forwarding and promotes competence, conduct and supply-chain capacity in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian professional and regulatory pathways; they do not establish one universal certificate or current demand ranking for every procurement, logistics or supply-chain role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian project-management professional and regulatory pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian project management, PMO, programme delivery, project consulting, professional development, certification and practice standards
findings: PMI Nigeria describes a Nigerian project-management professional community, learning, job and networking pathways; CIPMN describes Nigerian training, examination, certification, licensing, supervision and standards for project managers and PMO or consulting practitioners.
source_summaries.limitations: The bodies establish professional and training pathways, not a national vacancy count or a universal requirement that every project or programme worker hold a particular credential.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Management professional standards and pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian management, leadership, administration, organisational development, professional membership and management-practice standards
findings: The Nigerian Institute of Management (Chartered) states that its charter empowers it to control and regulate management practice in Nigeria, build management and leadership capacity and support members in managerial and executive positions across public and private sectors.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes management-profession context and a professional pathway; it is not a vacancy count or proof that every management, executive or business role requires NIM membership.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Procurement Certification Programme
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian public and private procurement practitioners
findings: The programme describes four Nigerian procurement-certification tiers and skills including communication, teamwork, time management, deadlines, ethics and risk management, with prerequisites varying by tier.
source_summaries.limitations: The pathway is for procurement practice and does not apply to every purchasing, logistics, project or administrative role.

source_summaries.name: Project Managers Development Association of Nigeria
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian project-management professional development and IPMA-aligned certification levels
findings: PMDAN identifies itself as Nigeria's IPMA member association, describes four certification levels and publishes project-execution and project-management learning activities.
source_summaries.limitations: Professional-body certification is a pathway, not a universal employer requirement for every project-support or coordination role.
