source_summaries.name: COREN engineering registration and biomedical-engineering development context
COREN 2026 engineering regulation and public-safety reforms
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian engineering practice, registration, public safety, project monitoring and anti-quackery context
findings: COREN's 2026 reforms emphasise qualified and registered practitioners, public safety, project monitoring and enforcement against unqualified engineering practice.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports regulated-engineering context; it is not a personal registration requirement for every technician or non-engineering role in an engineering organisation.

source_summaries.name: CPN 2021 Examination Syllabus
NUC, NCCE and Nigerian education standards
Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy and Microsoft 3MTT workforce programme
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian digital-skills pathways in AI, cybersecurity, data science and software development
findings: The ministry described 3MTT pathways for AI, cybersecurity, data science and software development and a Microsoft-backed AI skilling programme targeting Nigerian learners.
source_summaries.limitations: A government skilling programme is ecosystem and pathway evidence, not proof that every Nigerian employer requires the programme or its tools.

source_summaries.name: Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare hospital-services policy resources
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian health-facility, laboratory quality, biosafety, patient-safety, eye-health and oxygen-care guidance
findings: The ministry lists a 2024 guideline on integration of medical laboratory services, a 2025 guideline on medical-laboratory quality management, and a 2026 guideline on laboratory biosafety and biosecurity.
The same policy resource lists patient-safety and care-quality guidance and an eye-health strategic plan for 2024-2028.
source_summaries.limitations: These are system and practice guidance documents; they do not by themselves establish an individual licence or a vacancy for every health occupation.

source_summaries.name: HotNigerianJobs metallurgical and materials engineering vacancy snapshot
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian metallurgical, materials, steel and welding-related vacancies
findings: The Nigerian discipline page listed metallurgical and materials engineering vacancies, including steel melt-shop and mechanical/metallurgical engineering roles, with welding and fabrication qualifications appearing in requirements.
source_summaries.limitations: Job listings are time-bound and title conventions vary; this is an observed market signal, not a national demand estimate or universal qualification requirement.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria physicist vacancy signal
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based physical-science employment
findings: A Nigeria-focused physical-sciences jobs page identified a Physicist vacancy in Ikeja, Lagos, with relevant training or certification requirements.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a single dated vacancy signal; it is not a national demand count, universal qualification route or evidence for every scientific-research speciality.

source_summaries.name: Jobberman Nigeria jobs
MDCN and MLSCN Nigerian medical, dental and laboratory registration and training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian medical and dental education, housemanship, professional registration, annual practice licensing, medical laboratory training, laboratory registration and continuing professional development
findings: MDCN publishes medical and dental education, accreditation, registration, practising-licence and CPD services.
MLSCN publishes medical-laboratory training, registration, licensure, laboratory accreditation and CPD services, including the 2025 ND curriculum.
source_summaries.limitations: The regulations apply to defined health professions and facilities; they do not establish a universal licence for every health-support, research, technology or administrative role.

source_summaries.name: MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
NBRDA genetics, genomics and bioinformatics workshop
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian molecular biology, genetics, genomics, bioinformatics and public research infrastructure
findings: NBRDA reported a practical workshop through its Genetics, Genomics and Bioinformatics Department and connected it to Nigeria BioGenome and national genomics/bioinformatics data infrastructure goals.
source_summaries.limitations: The workshop supports Nigerian research and skills context; it does not establish broad private-sector demand or a universal certificate.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications list
Nigerian agricultural research, horticulture, crop, livestock and extension context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian crop production, horticulture, livestock, plant genetics, biotechnology, agricultural training, extension and production improvement
findings: ARCN coordinates agricultural research, training and extension through national institutes and colleges across Nigeria's agro-ecological zones; its plant-resources work covers crop improvement, seed production, irrigation, pest and disease management, genetics and biotechnology; NIHORT covers fruits, vegetables, spices, ornamentals, post-harvest processing and sustainable horticultural production; NBTE lists Nigerian crop-production and livestock-production technical pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian agricultural role-family and training context, not a universal farm system, commodity, equipment stack, licence or vacancy count for every agricultural occupation.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria analytical-chemist vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based analytical chemistry, laboratory quality-control and pharmaceutical or manufacturing testing work
findings: Nigeria-focused job pages identify Analytical Chemist roles involving chemical analysis, laboratory instrumentation, method validation, quality control, calibration and reporting in Lagos, Warri, Onitsha, Akure, Minna and other locations.
source_summaries.limitations: The listings demonstrate Nigerian analytical-chemistry work; they do not establish one universal laboratory credential, instrument stack or requirement for every chemist speciality.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria environmental-scientist vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based environmental monitoring, assessment, compliance, remediation and field-science work
findings: Nigeria-based listings identify Environmental Scientist roles involving environmental data collection, sampling, analysis, impact or compliance work, reporting and field health, safety and environmental requirements.
source_summaries.limitations: The listings demonstrate a Nigerian environmental-science role family; they do not establish one universal environmental licence, certification, employer requirement or software stack.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria microbiologist vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based microbiology, laboratory testing, quality control, food, pharmaceutical, environmental and research work
findings: Nigeria-focused biological-sciences vacancy pages identify Microbiologist roles in Port Harcourt and Lagos involving laboratory testing, experimental protocols, quality control, food, pharmaceutical and environmental applications.
source_summaries.limitations: The listings demonstrate a Nigerian microbiology role family; they do not establish one universal laboratory credential, instrument stack or regulator for every microbiology setting.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria statistician and mathematician vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based statistics, mathematics, data and quantitative-analysis employment
findings: Nigeria-focused vacancy pages identify Statistician, Statistics Graduate and combined Statistician/Mathematician roles in Lagos, including National Bureau of Statistics and private-sector signals.
source_summaries.limitations: These are vacancy and institutional title signals, not a national demand count or a universal qualification route for every quantitative role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian biomedical, biotechnology, pharmaceutical and epidemiology research context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian biomedical research, molecular biology, biotechnology, immunology, epidemiology, toxicology, pharmacology, diagnostics, vaccines and pharmaceutical development
findings: NIMR describes Nigerian molecular epidemiology, food-safety, immunogenetics, theranostics, microbiome and molecular-technique laboratories; NABDA describes Nigerian biomedical biotechnology work in immunology, vaccinology, antibody generation, DNA, biobanking and diagnostics; NIPRD describes pharmaceutical, biological-product, toxicology, quality-assurance and environmental-science research.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian research and institutional role families, not a vacancy count, personal licence or universal academic route for every biomedical or scientific occupation.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian environmental science, biodiversity, water-quality and environmental-health context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian environmental science, environmental health, biodiversity conservation, water and air quality, pollution control, environmental audit, natural resources and sustainability
findings: NESREA describes Nigerian environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, water-quality and pollution standards, environmental audits, environmental data, ecosystem conservation and research; EHCON regulates and licenses environmental-health specialists, officers, technicians and assistants; the Federal Ministry of Environment identifies chemical, waste, sewage, air-emissions and environmental-health functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian environmental and environmental-health practice context; it is not a national vacancy count and environmental-health registration should not be applied to every environmental scientist or ecologist.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian fisheries, aquaculture and aquatic-research context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fisheries, aquaculture development, aquatic research, training, extension, marine and inland-water resources and sustainable production
findings: The Agricultural Research Council of Nigeria identifies a Fisheries and Aquaculture department responsible for coordinating, supervising and regulating research and training, policy, facilities, industry collaboration, sustainable practices and productivity across Nigerian fisheries and aquaculture institutions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian fisheries and aquaculture institutional context, not a vacancy count or one universal qualification, species, production system or equipment stack.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority radiation-safety training for mining
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian solid-mineral mining and processing radiation-safety roles and adjacent technical occupations
findings: NNRA announced a 2026 national course for current or prospective Radiation Safety Officers in mining and mineral processing, covering NORM/TE-NORM, monitoring, dose assessment, radiation protection, handling, transport, waste management and regulatory compliance.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a specialised radiation-safety pathway and does not apply to every mining or geology role.

source_summaries.name: National Universities Commission CCMAS and standards
National Universities Commission guidelines for e-learning in Nigerian universities
Office of the Head of the Civil Service ICT scheme-of-service circular
source_summaries.scope: Federal Nigerian public-service ICT role classification and professional benchmark context
findings: The 2026 circular reports review and harmonisation of federal ICT schemes of service and describes professional benchmarks involving COREN for computer engineers and CPN registration for other IT specialists in the specified public-service progression context.
source_summaries.limitations: The circular applies to the stated public-service scheme and must not be rendered as a blanket private-sector licence requirement.

source_summaries.name: University of Ibadan AFRIGENE genomics and computational-skills programme
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian genomics, bioinformatics, computational biology, evolutionary biology and biodiversity research skills
findings: The University of Ibadan described AFRIGENE 2026 hands-on learning focused on computational tools and approaches for genomics, evolutionary biology and biodiversity conservation.
source_summaries.limitations: University training is research and capacity-building evidence, not a role-specific vacancy or licence requirement.

findings: NUC describes Nigerian university accreditation, minimum academic standards, academic planning, inspection, student services, research and institutional quality assurance; TETFund TERAS describes Nigerian tertiary research repositories and services for researchers, students and institutions; NBTE documents technical-tertiary admissions and academic-board responsibilities.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian public-service administration, integrity, privacy and compliance context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian public administration, policy, planning, public-sector compliance, anti-corruption, ethics, data protection and government records or programme work
findings: OHCSF publishes Nigerian public-service rules, policy and civil-service resources; ICPC describes review of public-body systems, anti-corruption transparency units, monitoring, reporting, ethics and compliance work in MDAs; NDPC documents data-protection compliance, audits, data-protection officers and licensed compliance organisations in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian public-service and compliance functions; they are not evidence that every global public-office title exists locally, nor a universal qualification or vacancy count for each role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian social-work, child-care, safeguarding and psychosocial pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social work, child and family welfare, childcare, safeguarding, community development, psychosocial support, counselling and correctional or rehabilitation services
findings: NASoW identifies social work across Nigerian schools, hospitals, NGOs, ministries, rehabilitation centres, old people's homes, correctional centres and government levels; the Nigerian social-work curriculum identifies child, family, youth, mental-health, counselling, community, criminal-justice and correctional practice; NBTE lists Children's Care, Learning and Development; NCoS describes counselling, psychosocial support, rehabilitation, probation and non-custodial services.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian practice, service and training pathways; they do not establish a national vacancy count or imply that every caregiver, mentor, nanny or support worker is a regulated social worker.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian sports development, athlete support, coaching and administration context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian athlete development, coaching, sports administration, competition, facilities, sports science, support staff and national or international sports participation
findings: The Federal Ministry of Sports Development describes sports policy, monitoring, athlete training and life skills, competition participation, coach and technical-support development and performance improvement; the Nigeria Olympic Committee describes training, entering and funding Nigerian Olympic and Paralympic teams, national governing bodies, coaching education, athlete support and career services.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian sports role and institutional context, not a vacancy count, universal coaching licence or local counterpart for every sport-specific or winter/outdoor title.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria stand-up comedy and live-performance ecosystem signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based stand-up comedy, live performance, hosting and entertainment work
findings: Nigeria's State House describes stand-up comedy as part of a significant entertainment ecosystem, and a Nigerian talent platform lists verified stand-up comedians and event-booking pathways in Lagos and Port Harcourt.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian creative-industry and talent-market context, not a vacancy count, guaranteed income, universal qualification or formal personal licence.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria video-technician and audiovisual vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based video, audiovisual, filming, production and technical-media work
findings: Nigeria-focused job listings identify Video Technician and related videography and video-production work in Lagos, Ekiti, Kaduna and other Nigerian locations.
source_summaries.limitations: The listings demonstrate a local audiovisual role family; they do not establish one universal production tool stack or a national demand total for every video-specialist title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Management professional standards and pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian management, leadership, administration, organisational development, professional membership and management-practice standards
findings: The Nigerian Institute of Management (Chartered) states that its charter empowers it to control and regulate management practice in Nigeria, build management and leadership capacity and support members in managerial and executive positions across public and private sectors.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes management-profession context and a professional pathway; it is not a vacancy count or proof that every management, executive or business role requires NIM membership.

source_summaries.name: National Institute of Marketing of Nigeria
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing professional standards, training, certification and continuing development
findings: NIMN describes itself as the chartered regulatory body for marketing professionals in Nigeria and identifies training, certification, professional standards and ethics as part of its mandate.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports marketing-profession context; it does not establish a required certification for every marketing, sales, communications or brand role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Professional Administrators and Office Technology and Management
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian office administration, secretarial administration and office-technology professional training/certification
findings: NIPAS publishes professional certification and examination procedures for office administration and office-technology candidates.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a professional training/membership route, not a universal statutory licence for every office administrator.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission creative-economy sector map
source_summaries.scope: Film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming, XR, arts and cultural tourism in Nigeria
findings: The NIPC sector page identifies film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming and XR among Nigeria's creative-economy activities.
source_summaries.limitations: Sector mapping shows an established Nigerian sector context; it does not establish role-level hiring volume or a required tool stack.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Translators and Interpreters accreditation and membership examination
Nigerian Press Council journalism ethics and training accreditation
Quantity Surveyors Registration Board of Nigeria 2024 newsletter
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian quantity-surveying practice and professional registration context
findings: The QSRBN newsletter supplies Nigerian quantity-surveying professional-body context and practice material.
source_summaries.limitations: The newsletter supports professional context; specific registration gates must be shown only where the applicable rule is explicit.

source_summaries.name: SMEDAN Nigerian founder, MSME, entrepreneurship and business-development training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian MSME capacity building, entrepreneurship training, business development, access to finance, market support and founder development
findings: SMEDAN describes entrepreneurship training, capacity building, finance, markets and founder support for Nigerian nano, micro and small enterprises.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports entrepreneurial and business-development foundations; it does not establish a universal founder credential, company-registration outcome or demand ranking for every management role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian XR and immersive-technology ecosystem signals
source_summaries.scope: Lagos and Nigerian AR/VR/XR training, immersive media, education, healthcare and construction use cases
findings: Lagos XR ecosystem sources describe skills including 360 video, Unity, Unreal Engine, event planning and team leadership; local reporting also describes VR training and Nigerian immersive-technology education and emergency-services use cases.
source_summaries.limitations: These are ecosystem and training signals, not evidence of a national vacancy count or universal tool requirement.

findings: A Nigeria-based CNBC Africa posting identified a News Editor role in Lagos and described newsroom agenda-setting, editorial quality, production and team direction responsibilities.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a dated vacancy signal for broadcast news editing in Nigeria; it is not an esports-specific vacancy, national demand count or universal qualification requirement.

Directors Guild of Nigeria Academy
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film and television directing, screenwriting, cinematography and production management
findings: DGN Academy describes practical and theoretical training for directors, filmmakers, students and emerging creatives, including directing, screenwriting, cinematography and production management.
source_summaries.limitations: Guild training is a pathway signal and does not establish a universal licence or employment guarantee.

source_summaries.name: Esports Federation of Nigeria national esports programmes
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian competitive gaming, schools and university esports, broadcasting, refereeing, tournament operations and team programmes
findings: The federation described a National Esports Championship, Team Nigeria programme, schools and university league, and training for referees, broadcasters and tournament officials.
The federation's career-pathway language identifies athletes, content creators, event managers, analysts and game developers as roles within the Nigerian esports ecosystem.
EFN's current about page identifies players, coaches, referees and support staff as participants in Nigeria's organised esports pathway and describes national representation and player development.
source_summaries.limitations: Federation programmes demonstrate ecosystem and role-family context; they do not establish national job volume or a mandatory credential.

source_summaries.name: Federal Ministry of Arts, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy gaming sector context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria gaming, game development, esports and immersive creative economy
findings: Government identifies game development, esports and immersive experiences as a Nigerian creative-economy growth area.
The ministry describes local talent support, digital-skills development and job creation as sector objectives.
source_summaries.limitations: Sector policy context is not a count of vacancies and does not establish an individual licence or credential requirement.

MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
National Theatre production and technical-theatre ecosystem
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian stage production, technical theatre, performance and cultural programming
findings: The National Theatre identifies production and technical-theatre services and operates as a Nigerian hub for artistic expression and cultural production.
source_summaries.limitations: Institutional context does not establish a role-specific vacancy, salary or credential requirement.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE Creative Content Production curriculum
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian audio-visual content, cinematography, sound, editing and scriptwriting
findings: The curriculum includes background music and sound effects, cinematography, shot lists, storyboarding, lighting, screen directing and introductory scriptwriting.
source_summaries.limitations: Curriculum evidence supports skills and learning routes, not role-level demand or a universal credential requirement.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian creative-media and performing-production standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film and media production, cinematography, lighting, sound, editing, production design, performance, special effects and stage/creative production
findings: The Nigerian NBTE Creative Media Production standard covers storytelling, cinematography, sound, production design, editing, performance, special effects, video-camera operation, lighting and casting; National Theatre materials identify stage performances, film shows, exhibitions, cultural shows, circus shows and related production facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian training and production ecosystems, not a national vacancy count or direct evidence for every highly specialised performance title; role-specific gaps remain explicit where the source does not support the title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications list
NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Copyright Commission music and creative-economy rights framework
Nigerian Film Corporation creative-media National Occupational Standards workshop
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian creative-media trades including film, audio, content, photography, animation, graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies
findings: The Nigerian Film Corporation reported a July 2026 critique and validation workshop intended to develop National Occupational Standards for creative-media trades, including film production, audio production, content creation, digital photography, animation, digital graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies.
source_summaries.limitations: The workshop demonstrates Nigerian standardisation activity and named trade families; it does not mean final standards or a personal certificate already exist for every listed role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Film Corporation film, sound, camera and audiovisual training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film production, camera, sound, video, editing, audiovisual training, archives and National Film Institute pathways
findings: NFC describes its film-industry development, National Film Institute courses, training, film production, archiving and National Film Video and Sound Archive responsibilities.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports Nigerian audiovisual training and sector context, not one universal commercial camera, audio or editing stack.

source_summaries.name: National Film and Video Censors Board film classification and distribution licensing
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film/video classification, legal distribution and exhibition
findings: NFVCB states that films and video works must be classified before distribution or exhibition and provides online, national, regional and community distributor-licence categories.
source_summaries.limitations: These requirements apply to film works, distributors and exhibition activity; they are not automatically a personal licence for actors, editors, camera operators or technicians.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria disc-jockey vacancy and professional-body signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based disc-jockey, live-event, club, mobile-DJ and music-entertainment work
findings: Nigeria-focused listings identify Disc Jockey roles in Lagos, Benin City and event settings, while the Deejays Association of Nigeria presents a national professional body offering development, networking and certification-oriented support.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources demonstrate a Nigerian DJ role and ecosystem; they do not establish one universal certification, income level, equipment stack or national demand total.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian marketing, advertising, journalism and media-training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing, advertising, public relations, journalism, mass communication, graphic and digital media practice and training
findings: NIMN identifies marketing as a chartered Nigerian profession with standards, certification, ethics and continuing development; APCON identifies statutory regulation, registration, advertising standards and advert-vetting functions; NIJ documents practical training in print, broadcast, online journalism, public relations, advertising, photojournalism, news writing, editing and radio/television production; NBTE lists Nigerian mass-communication and graphic-design curricula.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian professional, training and regulatory context; they are not a vacancy count and do not make one credential mandatory for every communications, creative or commercial role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian sports development, athlete support, coaching and administration context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian athlete development, coaching, sports administration, competition, facilities, sports science, support staff and national or international sports participation
findings: The Federal Ministry of Sports Development describes sports policy, monitoring, athlete training and life skills, competition participation, coach and technical-support development and performance improvement; the Nigeria Olympic Committee describes training, entering and funding Nigerian Olympic and Paralympic teams, national governing bodies, coaching education, athlete support and career services.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian sports role and institutional context, not a vacancy count, universal coaching licence or local counterpart for every sport-specific or winter/outdoor title.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria stand-up comedy and live-performance ecosystem signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based stand-up comedy, live performance, hosting and entertainment work
findings: Nigeria's State House describes stand-up comedy as part of a significant entertainment ecosystem, and a Nigerian talent platform lists verified stand-up comedians and event-booking pathways in Lagos and Port Harcourt.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian creative-industry and talent-market context, not a vacancy count, guaranteed income, universal qualification or formal personal licence.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria video-technician and audiovisual vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based video, audiovisual, filming, production and technical-media work
findings: Nigeria-focused job listings identify Video Technician and related videography and video-production work in Lagos, Ekiti, Kaduna and other Nigerian locations.
source_summaries.limitations: The listings demonstrate a local audiovisual role family; they do not establish one universal production tool stack or a national demand total for every video-specialist title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Management professional standards and pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian management, leadership, administration, organisational development, professional membership and management-practice standards
findings: The Nigerian Institute of Management (Chartered) states that its charter empowers it to control and regulate management practice in Nigeria, build management and leadership capacity and support members in managerial and executive positions across public and private sectors.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes management-profession context and a professional pathway; it is not a vacancy count or proof that every management, executive or business role requires NIM membership.

source_summaries.name: National Institute of Marketing of Nigeria
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing professional standards, training, certification and continuing development
findings: NIMN describes itself as the chartered regulatory body for marketing professionals in Nigeria and identifies training, certification, professional standards and ethics as part of its mandate.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports marketing-profession context; it does not establish a required certification for every marketing, sales, communications or brand role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Professional Administrators and Office Technology and Management
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian office administration, secretarial administration and office-technology professional training/certification
findings: NIPAS publishes professional certification and examination procedures for office administration and office-technology candidates.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a professional training/membership route, not a universal statutory licence for every office administrator.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission creative-economy sector map
source_summaries.scope: Film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming, XR, arts and cultural tourism in Nigeria
findings: The NIPC sector page identifies film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming and XR among Nigeria's creative-economy activities.
source_summaries.limitations: Sector mapping shows an established Nigerian sector context; it does not establish role-level hiring volume or a required tool stack.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian MSME capacity building, entrepreneurship training, business development, access to finance, market support and founder development

findings: NIMN describes itself as the chartered regulatory body for marketing professionals in Nigeria and identifies training, certification, professional standards and ethics as part of its mandate.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports marketing-profession context; it does not establish a required certification for every marketing, sales, communications or brand role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Professional Administrators and Office Technology and Management
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian office administration, secretarial administration and office-technology professional training/certification
findings: NIPAS publishes professional certification and examination procedures for office administration and office-technology candidates.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a professional training/membership route, not a universal statutory licence for every office administrator.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission creative-economy sector map
source_summaries.scope: Film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming, XR, arts and cultural tourism in Nigeria
findings: The NIPC sector page identifies film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming and XR among Nigeria's creative-economy activities.
source_summaries.limitations: Sector mapping shows an established Nigerian sector context; it does not establish role-level hiring volume or a required tool stack.

source_summaries.limitations: The newsletter supports professional context; specific registration gates must be shown only where the applicable rule is explicit.

source_summaries.name: SMEDAN Nigerian founder, MSME, entrepreneurship and business-development training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian MSME capacity building, entrepreneurship training, business development, access to finance, market support and founder development

source_summaries.limitations: This supports entrepreneurial and business-development foundations; it does not establish a universal founder credential, company-registration outcome or demand ranking for every management role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian XR and immersive-technology ecosystem signals

source_summaries.limitations: These are ecosystem and training signals, not evidence of a national vacancy count or universal tool requirement.

Nigeria-based broadcast news editor vacancy signal
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based broadcast-media news-editing work
findings: A Nigeria-based CNBC Africa posting identified a News Editor role in Lagos and described newsroom agenda-setting, editorial quality, production and team direction responsibilities.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a dated vacancy signal for broadcast news editing in Nigeria; it is not an esports-specific vacancy, national demand count or universal qualification requirement.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian creative-industry and media sources
Directors Guild of Nigeria Academy
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film and television directing, screenwriting, cinematography and production management
findings: DGN Academy describes practical and theoretical training for directors, filmmakers, students and emerging creatives, including directing, screenwriting, cinematography and production management.
source_summaries.limitations: Guild training is a pathway signal and does not establish a universal licence or employment guarantee.

source_summaries.name: Esports Federation of Nigeria national esports programmes
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian competitive gaming, schools and university esports, broadcasting, refereeing, tournament operations and team programmes
findings: The federation described a National Esports Championship, Team Nigeria programme, schools and university league, and training for referees, broadcasters and tournament officials.
The federation's career-pathway language identifies athletes, content creators, event managers, analysts and game developers as roles within the Nigerian esports ecosystem.
EFN's current about page identifies players, coaches, referees and support staff as participants in Nigeria's organised esports pathway and describes national representation and player development.
source_summaries.limitations: Federation programmes demonstrate ecosystem and role-family context; they do not establish national job volume or a mandatory credential.

source_summaries.name: Federal Ministry of Arts, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy gaming sector context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria gaming, game development, esports and immersive creative economy
findings: Government identifies game development, esports and immersive experiences as a Nigerian creative-economy growth area.
The ministry describes local talent support, digital-skills development and job creation as sector objectives.
source_summaries.limitations: Sector policy context is not a count of vacancies and does not establish an individual licence or credential requirement.

MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
National Theatre production and technical-theatre ecosystem
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian stage production, technical theatre, performance and cultural programming
findings: The National Theatre identifies production and technical-theatre services and operates as a Nigerian hub for artistic expression and cultural production.
source_summaries.limitations: Institutional context does not establish a role-specific vacancy, salary or credential requirement.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE Creative Content Production curriculum
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian audio-visual content, cinematography, sound, editing and scriptwriting
findings: The curriculum includes background music and sound effects, cinematography, shot lists, storyboarding, lighting, screen directing and introductory scriptwriting.
source_summaries.limitations: Curriculum evidence supports skills and learning routes, not role-level demand or a universal credential requirement.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian creative-media and performing-production standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film and media production, cinematography, lighting, sound, editing, production design, performance, special effects and stage/creative production
findings: The Nigerian NBTE Creative Media Production standard covers storytelling, cinematography, sound, production design, editing, performance, special effects, video-camera operation, lighting and casting; National Theatre materials identify stage performances, film shows, exhibitions, cultural shows, circus shows and related production facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian training and production ecosystems, not a national vacancy count or direct evidence for every highly specialised performance title; role-specific gaps remain explicit where the source does not support the title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications list
NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Copyright Commission music and creative-economy rights framework
Nigerian Film Corporation creative-media National Occupational Standards workshop
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian creative-media trades including film, audio, content, photography, animation, graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies
findings: The Nigerian Film Corporation reported a July 2026 critique and validation workshop intended to develop National Occupational Standards for creative-media trades, including film production, audio production, content creation, digital photography, animation, digital graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies.
source_summaries.limitations: The workshop demonstrates Nigerian standardisation activity and named trade families; it does not mean final standards or a personal certificate already exist for every listed role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Film Corporation film, sound, camera and audiovisual training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film production, camera, sound, video, editing, audiovisual training, archives and National Film Institute pathways
findings: NFC describes its film-industry development, National Film Institute courses, training, film production, archiving and National Film Video and Sound Archive responsibilities.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports Nigerian audiovisual training and sector context, not one universal commercial camera, audio or editing stack.

source_summaries.name: National Film and Video Censors Board film classification and distribution licensing
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film/video classification, legal distribution and exhibition
findings: NFVCB states that films and video works must be classified before distribution or exhibition and provides online, national, regional and community distributor-licence categories.
source_summaries.limitations: These requirements apply to film works, distributors and exhibition activity; they are not automatically a personal licence for actors, editors, camera operators or technicians.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria disc-jockey vacancy and professional-body signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based disc-jockey, live-event, club, mobile-DJ and music-entertainment work
findings: Nigeria-focused listings identify Disc Jockey roles in Lagos, Benin City and event settings, while the Deejays Association of Nigeria presents a national professional body offering development, networking and certification-oriented support.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources demonstrate a Nigerian DJ role and ecosystem; they do not establish one universal certification, income level, equipment stack or national demand total.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian marketing, advertising, journalism and media-training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing, advertising, public relations, journalism, mass communication, graphic and digital media practice and training
findings: NIMN identifies marketing as a chartered Nigerian profession with standards, certification, ethics and continuing development; APCON identifies statutory regulation, registration, advertising standards and advert-vetting functions; NIJ documents practical training in print, broadcast, online journalism, public relations, advertising, photojournalism, news writing, editing and radio/television production; NBTE lists Nigerian mass-communication and graphic-design curricula.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian professional, training and regulatory context; they are not a vacancy count and do not make one credential mandatory for every communications, creative or commercial role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian sports development, athlete support, coaching and administration context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian athlete development, coaching, sports administration, competition, facilities, sports science, support staff and national or international sports participation
findings: The Federal Ministry of Sports Development describes sports policy, monitoring, athlete training and life skills, competition participation, coach and technical-support development and performance improvement; the Nigeria Olympic Committee describes training, entering and funding Nigerian Olympic and Paralympic teams, national governing bodies, coaching education, athlete support and career services.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian sports role and institutional context, not a vacancy count, universal coaching licence or local counterpart for every sport-specific or winter/outdoor title.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria stand-up comedy and live-performance ecosystem signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based stand-up comedy, live performance, hosting and entertainment work
findings: Nigeria's State House describes stand-up comedy as part of a significant entertainment ecosystem, and a Nigerian talent platform lists verified stand-up comedians and event-booking pathways in Lagos and Port Harcourt.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian creative-industry and talent-market context, not a vacancy count, guaranteed income, universal qualification or formal personal licence.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria video-technician and audiovisual vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based video, audiovisual, filming, production and technical-media work
findings: Nigeria-focused job listings identify Video Technician and related videography and video-production work in Lagos, Ekiti, Kaduna and other Nigerian locations.
source_summaries.limitations: The listings demonstrate a local audiovisual role family; they do not establish one universal production tool stack or a national demand total for every video-specialist title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Management professional standards and pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian management, leadership, administration, organisational development, professional membership and management-practice standards
findings: The Nigerian Institute of Management (Chartered) states that its charter empowers it to control and regulate management practice in Nigeria, build management and leadership capacity and support members in managerial and executive positions across public and private sectors.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes management-profession context and a professional pathway; it is not a vacancy count or proof that every management, executive or business role requires NIM membership.

source_summaries.name: National Institute of Marketing of Nigeria
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing professional standards, training, certification and continuing development
findings: NIMN describes itself as the chartered regulatory body for marketing professionals in Nigeria and identifies training, certification, professional standards and ethics as part of its mandate.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports marketing-profession context; it does not establish a required certification for every marketing, sales, communications or brand role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Professional Administrators and Office Technology and Management
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian office administration, secretarial administration and office-technology professional training/certification
findings: NIPAS publishes professional certification and examination procedures for office administration and office-technology candidates.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a professional training/membership route, not a universal statutory licence for every office administrator.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission creative-economy sector map
source_summaries.scope: Film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming, XR, arts and cultural tourism in Nigeria
findings: The NIPC sector page identifies film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming and XR among Nigeria's creative-economy activities.
source_summaries.limitations: Sector mapping shows an established Nigerian sector context; it does not establish role-level hiring volume or a required tool stack.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian MSME capacity building, entrepreneurship training, business development, access to finance, market support and founder development

NBTE Creative Content Production curriculum
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian audio-visual content, cinematography, sound, editing and scriptwriting
findings: The curriculum includes background music and sound effects, cinematography, shot lists, storyboarding, lighting, screen directing and introductory scriptwriting.
source_summaries.limitations: Curriculum evidence supports skills and learning routes, not role-level demand or a universal credential requirement.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian creative-media and performing-production standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film and media production, cinematography, lighting, sound, editing, production design, performance, special effects and stage/creative production
findings: The Nigerian NBTE Creative Media Production standard covers storytelling, cinematography, sound, production design, editing, performance, special effects, video-camera operation, lighting and casting; National Theatre materials identify stage performances, film shows, exhibitions, cultural shows, circus shows and related production facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian training and production ecosystems, not a national vacancy count or direct evidence for every highly specialised performance title; role-specific gaps remain explicit where the source does not support the title.

source_summaries.name: National Film and Video Censors Board film classification and distribution licensing
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film/video classification, legal distribution and exhibition
findings: NFVCB states that films and video works must be classified before distribution or exhibition and provides online, national, regional and community distributor-licence categories.
source_summaries.limitations: These requirements apply to film works, distributors and exhibition activity; they are not automatically a personal licence for actors, editors, camera operators or technicians.

source_summaries.limitations: Curriculum evidence supports skills and learning routes, not role-level demand or a universal credential requirement.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian creative-media and performing-production standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film and media production, cinematography, lighting, sound, editing, production design, performance, special effects and stage/creative production
findings: The Nigerian NBTE Creative Media Production standard covers storytelling, cinematography, sound, production design, editing, performance, special effects, video-camera operation, lighting and casting; National Theatre materials identify stage performances, film shows, exhibitions, cultural shows, circus shows and related production facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian training and production ecosystems, not a national vacancy count or direct evidence for every highly specialised performance title; role-specific gaps remain explicit where the source does not support the title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications list
NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Copyright Commission music and creative-economy rights framework
Nigerian Film Corporation creative-media National Occupational Standards workshop
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian creative-media trades including film, audio, content, photography, animation, graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies
findings: The Nigerian Film Corporation reported a July 2026 critique and validation workshop intended to develop National Occupational Standards for creative-media trades, including film production, audio production, content creation, digital photography, animation, digital graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies.
source_summaries.limitations: The workshop demonstrates Nigerian standardisation activity and named trade families; it does not mean final standards or a personal certificate already exist for every listed role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Film Corporation film, sound, camera and audiovisual training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film production, camera, sound, video, editing, audiovisual training, archives and National Film Institute pathways
findings: NFC describes its film-industry development, National Film Institute courses, training, film production, archiving and National Film Video and Sound Archive responsibilities.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports Nigerian audiovisual training and sector context, not one universal commercial camera, audio or editing stack.

source_summaries.name: National Film and Video Censors Board film classification and distribution licensing
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film/video classification, legal distribution and exhibition
findings: NFVCB states that films and video works must be classified before distribution or exhibition and provides online, national, regional and community distributor-licence categories.
source_summaries.limitations: These requirements apply to film works, distributors and exhibition activity; they are not automatically a personal licence for actors, editors, camera operators or technicians.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria disc-jockey vacancy and professional-body signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based disc-jockey, live-event, club, mobile-DJ and music-entertainment work
findings: Nigeria-focused listings identify Disc Jockey roles in Lagos, Benin City and event settings, while the Deejays Association of Nigeria presents a national professional body offering development, networking and certification-oriented support.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources demonstrate a Nigerian DJ role and ecosystem; they do not establish one universal certification, income level, equipment stack or national demand total.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian marketing, advertising, journalism and media-training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing, advertising, public relations, journalism, mass communication, graphic and digital media practice and training
findings: NIMN identifies marketing as a chartered Nigerian profession with standards, certification, ethics and continuing development; APCON identifies statutory regulation, registration, advertising standards and advert-vetting functions; NIJ documents practical training in print, broadcast, online journalism, public relations, advertising, photojournalism, news writing, editing and radio/television production; NBTE lists Nigerian mass-communication and graphic-design curricula.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian professional, training and regulatory context; they are not a vacancy count and do not make one credential mandatory for every communications, creative or commercial role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian sports development, athlete support, coaching and administration context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian athlete development, coaching, sports administration, competition, facilities, sports science, support staff and national or international sports participation
findings: The Federal Ministry of Sports Development describes sports policy, monitoring, athlete training and life skills, competition participation, coach and technical-support development and performance improvement; the Nigeria Olympic Committee describes training, entering and funding Nigerian Olympic and Paralympic teams, national governing bodies, coaching education, athlete support and career services.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian sports role and institutional context, not a vacancy count, universal coaching licence or local counterpart for every sport-specific or winter/outdoor title.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria stand-up comedy and live-performance ecosystem signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based stand-up comedy, live performance, hosting and entertainment work
findings: Nigeria's State House describes stand-up comedy as part of a significant entertainment ecosystem, and a Nigerian talent platform lists verified stand-up comedians and event-booking pathways in Lagos and Port Harcourt.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian creative-industry and talent-market context, not a vacancy count, guaranteed income, universal qualification or formal personal licence.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria video-technician and audiovisual vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based video, audiovisual, filming, production and technical-media work
findings: Nigeria-focused job listings identify Video Technician and related videography and video-production work in Lagos, Ekiti, Kaduna and other Nigerian locations.
source_summaries.limitations: The listings demonstrate a local audiovisual role family; they do not establish one universal production tool stack or a national demand total for every video-specialist title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Management professional standards and pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian management, leadership, administration, organisational development, professional membership and management-practice standards
findings: The Nigerian Institute of Management (Chartered) states that its charter empowers it to control and regulate management practice in Nigeria, build management and leadership capacity and support members in managerial and executive positions across public and private sectors.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes management-profession context and a professional pathway; it is not a vacancy count or proof that every management, executive or business role requires NIM membership.

source_summaries.name: National Institute of Marketing of Nigeria
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing professional standards, training, certification and continuing development
findings: NIMN describes itself as the chartered regulatory body for marketing professionals in Nigeria and identifies training, certification, professional standards and ethics as part of its mandate.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports marketing-profession context; it does not establish a required certification for every marketing, sales, communications or brand role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Professional Administrators and Office Technology and Management
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian office administration, secretarial administration and office-technology professional training/certification
findings: NIPAS publishes professional certification and examination procedures for office administration and office-technology candidates.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a professional training/membership route, not a universal statutory licence for every office administrator.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission creative-economy sector map
source_summaries.scope: Film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming, XR, arts and cultural tourism in Nigeria
findings: The NIPC sector page identifies film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming and XR among Nigeria's creative-economy activities.
source_summaries.limitations: Sector mapping shows an established Nigerian sector context; it does not establish role-level hiring volume or a required tool stack.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Translators and Interpreters accreditation and membership examination
Nigerian Press Council journalism ethics and training accreditation
Quantity Surveyors Registration Board of Nigeria 2024 newsletter
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian quantity-surveying practice and professional registration context
findings: The QSRBN newsletter supplies Nigerian quantity-surveying professional-body context and practice material.
source_summaries.limitations: The newsletter supports professional context; specific registration gates must be shown only where the applicable rule is explicit.

source_summaries.name: SMEDAN Nigerian founder, MSME, entrepreneurship and business-development training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian MSME capacity building, entrepreneurship training, business development, access to finance, market support and founder development
findings: SMEDAN describes entrepreneurship training, capacity building, finance, markets and founder support for Nigerian nano, micro and small enterprises.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports entrepreneurial and business-development foundations; it does not establish a universal founder credential, company-registration outcome or demand ranking for every management role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian XR and immersive-technology ecosystem signals
source_summaries.scope: Lagos and Nigerian AR/VR/XR training, immersive media, education, healthcare and construction use cases
findings: Lagos XR ecosystem sources describe skills including 360 video, Unity, Unreal Engine, event planning and team leadership; local reporting also describes VR training and Nigerian immersive-technology education and emergency-services use cases.
source_summaries.limitations: These are ecosystem and training signals, not evidence of a national vacancy count or universal tool requirement.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film and television directing, screenwriting, cinematography and production management
findings: DGN Academy describes practical and theoretical training for directors, filmmakers, students and emerging creatives, including directing, screenwriting, cinematography and production management.
source_summaries.limitations: Guild training is a pathway signal and does not establish a universal licence or employment guarantee.

MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
National Theatre production and technical-theatre ecosystem
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian stage production, technical theatre, performance and cultural programming
findings: The National Theatre identifies production and technical-theatre services and operates as a Nigerian hub for artistic expression and cultural production.
source_summaries.limitations: Institutional context does not establish a role-specific vacancy, salary or credential requirement.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE Creative Content Production curriculum
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian audio-visual content, cinematography, sound, editing and scriptwriting
findings: The curriculum includes background music and sound effects, cinematography, shot lists, storyboarding, lighting, screen directing and introductory scriptwriting.
source_summaries.limitations: Curriculum evidence supports skills and learning routes, not role-level demand or a universal credential requirement.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian creative-media and performing-production standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film and media production, cinematography, lighting, sound, editing, production design, performance, special effects and stage/creative production
findings: The Nigerian NBTE Creative Media Production standard covers storytelling, cinematography, sound, production design, editing, performance, special effects, video-camera operation, lighting and casting; National Theatre materials identify stage performances, film shows, exhibitions, cultural shows, circus shows and related production facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian training and production ecosystems, not a national vacancy count or direct evidence for every highly specialised performance title; role-specific gaps remain explicit where the source does not support the title.

source_summaries.name: National Film and Video Censors Board film classification and distribution licensing
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film/video classification, legal distribution and exhibition
findings: NFVCB states that films and video works must be classified before distribution or exhibition and provides online, national, regional and community distributor-licence categories.
source_summaries.limitations: These requirements apply to film works, distributors and exhibition activity; they are not automatically a personal licence for actors, editors, camera operators or technicians.

findings: The federation described a National Esports Championship, Team Nigeria programme, schools and university league, and training for referees, broadcasters and tournament officials.
The federation's career-pathway language identifies athletes, content creators, event managers, analysts and game developers as roles within the Nigerian esports ecosystem.
EFN's current about page identifies players, coaches, referees and support staff as participants in Nigeria's organised esports pathway and describes national representation and player development.
source_summaries.limitations: Federation programmes demonstrate ecosystem and role-family context; they do not establish national job volume or a mandatory credential.

source_summaries.scope: Nigeria gaming, game development, esports and immersive creative economy
findings: Government identifies game development, esports and immersive experiences as a Nigerian creative-economy growth area.
The ministry describes local talent support, digital-skills development and job creation as sector objectives.
source_summaries.limitations: Sector policy context is not a count of vacancies and does not establish an individual licence or credential requirement.

NBTE Creative Content Production curriculum
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian audio-visual content, cinematography, sound, editing and scriptwriting
findings: The curriculum includes background music and sound effects, cinematography, shot lists, storyboarding, lighting, screen directing and introductory scriptwriting.
source_summaries.limitations: Curriculum evidence supports skills and learning routes, not role-level demand or a universal credential requirement.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian creative-media and performing-production standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film and media production, cinematography, lighting, sound, editing, production design, performance, special effects and stage/creative production
findings: The Nigerian NBTE Creative Media Production standard covers storytelling, cinematography, sound, production design, editing, performance, special effects, video-camera operation, lighting and casting; National Theatre materials identify stage performances, film shows, exhibitions, cultural shows, circus shows and related production facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian training and production ecosystems, not a national vacancy count or direct evidence for every highly specialised performance title; role-specific gaps remain explicit where the source does not support the title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications list
NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Copyright Commission music and creative-economy rights framework

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian creative-media trades including film, audio, content, photography, animation, graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies
findings: The Nigerian Film Corporation reported a July 2026 critique and validation workshop intended to develop National Occupational Standards for creative-media trades, including film production, audio production, content creation, digital photography, animation, digital graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies.
source_summaries.limitations: The workshop demonstrates Nigerian standardisation activity and named trade families; it does not mean final standards or a personal certificate already exist for every listed role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Film Corporation film, sound, camera and audiovisual training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film production, camera, sound, video, editing, audiovisual training, archives and National Film Institute pathways

source_summaries.limitations: The source supports Nigerian audiovisual training and sector context, not one universal commercial camera, audio or editing stack.

source_summaries.name: National Film and Video Censors Board film classification and distribution licensing
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film/video classification, legal distribution and exhibition
findings: NFVCB states that films and video works must be classified before distribution or exhibition and provides online, national, regional and community distributor-licence categories.
source_summaries.limitations: These requirements apply to film works, distributors and exhibition activity; they are not automatically a personal licence for actors, editors, camera operators or technicians.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria disc-jockey vacancy and professional-body signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based disc-jockey, live-event, club, mobile-DJ and music-entertainment work
findings: Nigeria-focused listings identify Disc Jockey roles in Lagos, Benin City and event settings, while the Deejays Association of Nigeria presents a national professional body offering development, networking and certification-oriented support.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources demonstrate a Nigerian DJ role and ecosystem; they do not establish one universal certification, income level, equipment stack or national demand total.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian marketing, advertising, journalism and media-training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing, advertising, public relations, journalism, mass communication, graphic and digital media practice and training
findings: NIMN identifies marketing as a chartered Nigerian profession with standards, certification, ethics and continuing development; APCON identifies statutory regulation, registration, advertising standards and advert-vetting functions; NIJ documents practical training in print, broadcast, online journalism, public relations, advertising, photojournalism, news writing, editing and radio/television production; NBTE lists Nigerian mass-communication and graphic-design curricula.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian professional, training and regulatory context; they are not a vacancy count and do not make one credential mandatory for every communications, creative or commercial role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian sports development, athlete support, coaching and administration context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian athlete development, coaching, sports administration, competition, facilities, sports science, support staff and national or international sports participation
findings: The Federal Ministry of Sports Development describes sports policy, monitoring, athlete training and life skills, competition participation, coach and technical-support development and performance improvement; the Nigeria Olympic Committee describes training, entering and funding Nigerian Olympic and Paralympic teams, national governing bodies, coaching education, athlete support and career services.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian sports role and institutional context, not a vacancy count, universal coaching licence or local counterpart for every sport-specific or winter/outdoor title.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria stand-up comedy and live-performance ecosystem signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based stand-up comedy, live performance, hosting and entertainment work
findings: Nigeria's State House describes stand-up comedy as part of a significant entertainment ecosystem, and a Nigerian talent platform lists verified stand-up comedians and event-booking pathways in Lagos and Port Harcourt.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian creative-industry and talent-market context, not a vacancy count, guaranteed income, universal qualification or formal personal licence.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria video-technician and audiovisual vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based video, audiovisual, filming, production and technical-media work
findings: Nigeria-focused job listings identify Video Technician and related videography and video-production work in Lagos, Ekiti, Kaduna and other Nigerian locations.
source_summaries.limitations: The listings demonstrate a local audiovisual role family; they do not establish one universal production tool stack or a national demand total for every video-specialist title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Management professional standards and pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian management, leadership, administration, organisational development, professional membership and management-practice standards
findings: The Nigerian Institute of Management (Chartered) states that its charter empowers it to control and regulate management practice in Nigeria, build management and leadership capacity and support members in managerial and executive positions across public and private sectors.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes management-profession context and a professional pathway; it is not a vacancy count or proof that every management, executive or business role requires NIM membership.

source_summaries.name: National Institute of Marketing of Nigeria
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing professional standards, training, certification and continuing development
findings: NIMN describes itself as the chartered regulatory body for marketing professionals in Nigeria and identifies training, certification, professional standards and ethics as part of its mandate.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports marketing-profession context; it does not establish a required certification for every marketing, sales, communications or brand role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Professional Administrators and Office Technology and Management
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian office administration, secretarial administration and office-technology professional training/certification
findings: NIPAS publishes professional certification and examination procedures for office administration and office-technology candidates.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a professional training/membership route, not a universal statutory licence for every office administrator.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission creative-economy sector map

source_summaries.limitations: Sector mapping shows an established Nigerian sector context; it does not establish role-level hiring volume or a required tool stack.
