source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.limitations: The workshop demonstrates Nigerian standardisation activity and named trade families; it does not mean final standards or a personal certificate already exist for every listed role.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian journalism context; it does not establish a vacancy count or a licence for every language, media or communication title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian marketing, advertising, journalism and media-training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing, advertising, public relations, journalism, mass communication, graphic and digital media practice and training
findings: NIMN identifies marketing as a chartered Nigerian profession with standards, certification, ethics and continuing development; APCON identifies statutory regulation, registration, advertising standards and advert-vetting functions; NIJ documents practical training in print, broadcast, online journalism, public relations, advertising, photojournalism, news writing, editing and radio/television production; NBTE lists Nigerian mass-communication and graphic-design curricula.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian professional, training and regulatory context; they are not a vacancy count and do not make one credential mandatory for every communications, creative or commercial role.

source_summaries.limitations: The source supports marketing-profession context; it does not establish a required certification for every marketing, sales, communications or brand role.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film and media production, cinematography, lighting, sound, editing, production design, performance, special effects and stage/creative production
findings: The Nigerian NBTE Creative Media Production standard covers storytelling, cinematography, sound, production design, editing, performance, special effects, video-camera operation, lighting and casting; National Theatre materials identify stage performances, film shows, exhibitions, cultural shows, circus shows and related production facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian training and production ecosystems, not a national vacancy count or direct evidence for every highly specialised performance title; role-specific gaps remain explicit where the source does not support the title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Copyright Commission music and creative-economy rights framework
Nigerian Film Corporation creative-media National Occupational Standards workshop
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian creative-media trades including film, audio, content, photography, animation, graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies
findings: The Nigerian Film Corporation reported a July 2026 critique and validation workshop intended to develop National Occupational Standards for creative-media trades, including film production, audio production, content creation, digital photography, animation, digital graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies.
source_summaries.limitations: The workshop demonstrates Nigerian standardisation activity and named trade families; it does not mean final standards or a personal certificate already exist for every listed role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian marketing, advertising, journalism and media-training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing, advertising, public relations, journalism, mass communication, graphic and digital media practice and training
findings: NIMN identifies marketing as a chartered Nigerian profession with standards, certification, ethics and continuing development; APCON identifies statutory regulation, registration, advertising standards and advert-vetting functions; NIJ documents practical training in print, broadcast, online journalism, public relations, advertising, photojournalism, news writing, editing and radio/television production; NBTE lists Nigerian mass-communication and graphic-design curricula.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian professional, training and regulatory context; they are not a vacancy count and do not make one credential mandatory for every communications, creative or commercial role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Fashion Council and fashion-sector skills context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fashion, garment, textile, leather, design, manufacturing, craft, innovation and fashion-value-chain work
findings: The Nigerian Fashion Council describes itself as a Federal Government-mandated Sector Skills Council inaugurated through NBTE and identifies a fashion value chain involving designers, craftsmen, manufacturers, innovators and associations; NBTE lists Nigerian pathways for garment making, Adire, embellishment, fashion/textile machine repair and leather work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes a Nigerian fashion-sector and training ecosystem; it is not a vacancy count, universal client demand ranking or single qualification requirement for every fashion or textile title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian luxury, jewellery, leather and craft enterprise context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian luxury and craft enterprise including fashion, leather, jewellery, accessories, furniture and creative-product work
findings: Nigeria's fashion and creative-sector institutions identify fashion, leather and creative enterprises as an active value chain; the 2026 UNDP Nigeria and Lagos State MSME spotlight specifically covers fashion, leather and creative enterprises, while government-linked creative-economy initiatives include fashion and related cultural production.
source_summaries.limitations: This is Nigerian ecosystem and enterprise evidence, not a direct vacancy signal or proof that every jewellery, luxury, furniture or accessory title has a distinct local employer market.

source_summaries.name: National Institute of Marketing of Nigeria
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing professional standards, training, certification and continuing development
findings: NIMN describes itself as the chartered regulatory body for marketing professionals in Nigeria and identifies training, certification, professional standards and ethics as part of its mandate.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports marketing-profession context; it does not establish a required certification for every marketing, sales, communications or brand role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission creative-economy sector map
source_summaries.scope: Film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming, XR, arts and cultural tourism in Nigeria
findings: The NIPC sector page identifies film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming and XR among Nigeria's creative-economy activities.
source_summaries.limitations: Sector mapping shows an established Nigerian sector context; it does not establish role-level hiring volume or a required tool stack.

source_summaries.name: NITDA 3MTT Nigerian product, data, cloud, DevOps and digital-skills pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian technical-talent pathways in product management, data analysis, data science, cloud computing, DevOps, UI/UX, quality assurance, software, AI, cybersecurity and game development
findings: NITDA and 3MTT explicitly list product management, data analysis and visualisation, data science, cloud computing, DevOps, UI/UX and quality assurance among Nigerian technical-skill tracks.
source_summaries.limitations: A national training track is evidence of a Nigerian skills pathway and ecosystem signal, not a guarantee of employment demand or a universal requirement for each related subgroup.

findings: The Nigerian Fashion Council describes itself as a Federal Government-mandated Sector Skills Council inaugurated through NBTE and identifies a fashion value chain involving designers, craftsmen, manufacturers, innovators and associations; NBTE lists Nigerian pathways for garment making, Adire, embellishment, fashion/textile machine repair and leather work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes a Nigerian fashion-sector and training ecosystem; it is not a vacancy count, universal client demand ranking or single qualification requirement for every fashion or textile title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian luxury, jewellery, leather and craft enterprise context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian luxury and craft enterprise including fashion, leather, jewellery, accessories, furniture and creative-product work
findings: Nigeria's fashion and creative-sector institutions identify fashion, leather and creative enterprises as an active value chain; the 2026 UNDP Nigeria and Lagos State MSME spotlight specifically covers fashion, leather and creative enterprises, while government-linked creative-economy initiatives include fashion and related cultural production.
source_summaries.limitations: This is Nigerian ecosystem and enterprise evidence, not a direct vacancy signal or proof that every jewellery, luxury, furniture or accessory title has a distinct local employer market.

source_summaries.name: National Institute of Marketing of Nigeria
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing professional standards, training, certification and continuing development
findings: NIMN describes itself as the chartered regulatory body for marketing professionals in Nigeria and identifies training, certification, professional standards and ethics as part of its mandate.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports marketing-profession context; it does not establish a required certification for every marketing, sales, communications or brand role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission creative-economy sector map
source_summaries.scope: Film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming, XR, arts and cultural tourism in Nigeria
findings: The NIPC sector page identifies film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming and XR among Nigeria's creative-economy activities.
source_summaries.limitations: Sector mapping shows an established Nigerian sector context; it does not establish role-level hiring volume or a required tool stack.

source_summaries.name: NITDA 3MTT Nigerian product, data, cloud, DevOps and digital-skills pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian technical-talent pathways in product management, data analysis, data science, cloud computing, DevOps, UI/UX, quality assurance, software, AI, cybersecurity and game development
findings: NITDA and 3MTT explicitly list product management, data analysis and visualisation, data science, cloud computing, DevOps, UI/UX and quality assurance among Nigerian technical-skill tracks.
source_summaries.limitations: A national training track is evidence of a Nigerian skills pathway and ecosystem signal, not a guarantee of employment demand or a universal requirement for each related subgroup.

Nigerian creative-media and performing-production standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film and media production, cinematography, lighting, sound, editing, production design, performance, special effects and stage/creative production
findings: The Nigerian NBTE Creative Media Production standard covers storytelling, cinematography, sound, production design, editing, performance, special effects, video-camera operation, lighting and casting; National Theatre materials identify stage performances, film shows, exhibitions, cultural shows, circus shows and related production facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian training and production ecosystems, not a national vacancy count or direct evidence for every highly specialised performance title; role-specific gaps remain explicit where the source does not support the title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Copyright Commission music and creative-economy rights framework
Nigerian Film Corporation creative-media National Occupational Standards workshop
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian creative-media trades including film, audio, content, photography, animation, graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies
findings: The Nigerian Film Corporation reported a July 2026 critique and validation workshop intended to develop National Occupational Standards for creative-media trades, including film production, audio production, content creation, digital photography, animation, digital graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies.
source_summaries.limitations: The workshop demonstrates Nigerian standardisation activity and named trade families; it does not mean final standards or a personal certificate already exist for every listed role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian marketing, advertising, journalism and media-training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing, advertising, public relations, journalism, mass communication, graphic and digital media practice and training
findings: NIMN identifies marketing as a chartered Nigerian profession with standards, certification, ethics and continuing development; APCON identifies statutory regulation, registration, advertising standards and advert-vetting functions; NIJ documents practical training in print, broadcast, online journalism, public relations, advertising, photojournalism, news writing, editing and radio/television production; NBTE lists Nigerian mass-communication and graphic-design curricula.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian professional, training and regulatory context; they are not a vacancy count and do not make one credential mandatory for every communications, creative or commercial role.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film and media production, cinematography, lighting, sound, editing, production design, performance, special effects and stage/creative production
findings: The Nigerian NBTE Creative Media Production standard covers storytelling, cinematography, sound, production design, editing, performance, special effects, video-camera operation, lighting and casting; National Theatre materials identify stage performances, film shows, exhibitions, cultural shows, circus shows and related production facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian training and production ecosystems, not a national vacancy count or direct evidence for every highly specialised performance title; role-specific gaps remain explicit where the source does not support the title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian creative-media trades including film, audio, content, photography, animation, graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies
findings: The Nigerian Film Corporation reported a July 2026 critique and validation workshop intended to develop National Occupational Standards for creative-media trades, including film production, audio production, content creation, digital photography, animation, digital graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies.
source_summaries.limitations: The workshop demonstrates Nigerian standardisation activity and named trade families; it does not mean final standards or a personal certificate already exist for every listed role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian marketing, advertising, journalism and media-training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing, advertising, public relations, journalism, mass communication, graphic and digital media practice and training
findings: NIMN identifies marketing as a chartered Nigerian profession with standards, certification, ethics and continuing development; APCON identifies statutory regulation, registration, advertising standards and advert-vetting functions; NIJ documents practical training in print, broadcast, online journalism, public relations, advertising, photojournalism, news writing, editing and radio/television production; NBTE lists Nigerian mass-communication and graphic-design curricula.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian professional, training and regulatory context; they are not a vacancy count and do not make one credential mandatory for every communications, creative or commercial role.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes a Nigerian fashion-sector and training ecosystem; it is not a vacancy count, universal client demand ranking or single qualification requirement for every fashion or textile title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian luxury, jewellery, leather and craft enterprise context

Nigerian creative-media and performing-production standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film and media production, cinematography, lighting, sound, editing, production design, performance, special effects and stage/creative production
findings: The Nigerian NBTE Creative Media Production standard covers storytelling, cinematography, sound, production design, editing, performance, special effects, video-camera operation, lighting and casting; National Theatre materials identify stage performances, film shows, exhibitions, cultural shows, circus shows and related production facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian training and production ecosystems, not a national vacancy count or direct evidence for every highly specialised performance title; role-specific gaps remain explicit where the source does not support the title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications catalogue
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian trade, technician, craft, agricultural, hospitality, ICT, automotive, construction, fashion and technical occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current catalogue names validated or current NOS/NSQ routes for masonry, electrical installation, carpentry, fashion and garment making, leather, food and beverage, automotive, agricultural equipment, interior-decoration-related craft and many other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS/NSQ route is a skills/qualification pathway; it is not automatically a separate licence to practise every trade or operate every business.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian marketing, advertising, journalism and media-training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing, advertising, public relations, journalism, mass communication, graphic and digital media practice and training
findings: NIMN identifies marketing as a chartered Nigerian profession with standards, certification, ethics and continuing development; APCON identifies statutory regulation, registration, advertising standards and advert-vetting functions; NIJ documents practical training in print, broadcast, online journalism, public relations, advertising, photojournalism, news writing, editing and radio/television production; NBTE lists Nigerian mass-communication and graphic-design curricula.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian professional, training and regulatory context; they are not a vacancy count and do not make one credential mandatory for every communications, creative or commercial role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Fashion Council and fashion-sector skills context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fashion, garment, textile, leather, design, manufacturing, craft, innovation and fashion-value-chain work
findings: The Nigerian Fashion Council describes itself as a Federal Government-mandated Sector Skills Council inaugurated through NBTE and identifies a fashion value chain involving designers, craftsmen, manufacturers, innovators and associations; NBTE lists Nigerian pathways for garment making, Adire, embellishment, fashion/textile machine repair and leather work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes a Nigerian fashion-sector and training ecosystem; it is not a vacancy count, universal client demand ranking or single qualification requirement for every fashion or textile title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian luxury, jewellery, leather and craft enterprise context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian luxury and craft enterprise including fashion, leather, jewellery, accessories, furniture and creative-product work
findings: Nigeria's fashion and creative-sector institutions identify fashion, leather and creative enterprises as an active value chain; the 2026 UNDP Nigeria and Lagos State MSME spotlight specifically covers fashion, leather and creative enterprises, while government-linked creative-economy initiatives include fashion and related cultural production.
source_summaries.limitations: This is Nigerian ecosystem and enterprise evidence, not a direct vacancy signal or proof that every jewellery, luxury, furniture or accessory title has a distinct local employer market.

findings: NBTE's current catalogue names validated or current NOS/NSQ routes for masonry, electrical installation, carpentry, fashion and garment making, leather, food and beverage, automotive, agricultural equipment, interior-decoration-related craft and many other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS/NSQ route is a skills/qualification pathway; it is not automatically a separate licence to practise every trade or operate every business.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian marketing, advertising, journalism and media-training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marketing, advertising, public relations, journalism, mass communication, graphic and digital media practice and training
findings: NIMN identifies marketing as a chartered Nigerian profession with standards, certification, ethics and continuing development; APCON identifies statutory regulation, registration, advertising standards and advert-vetting functions; NIJ documents practical training in print, broadcast, online journalism, public relations, advertising, photojournalism, news writing, editing and radio/television production; NBTE lists Nigerian mass-communication and graphic-design curricula.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian professional, training and regulatory context; they are not a vacancy count and do not make one credential mandatory for every communications, creative or commercial role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Fashion Council and fashion-sector skills context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fashion, garment, textile, leather, design, manufacturing, craft, innovation and fashion-value-chain work
findings: The Nigerian Fashion Council describes itself as a Federal Government-mandated Sector Skills Council inaugurated through NBTE and identifies a fashion value chain involving designers, craftsmen, manufacturers, innovators and associations; NBTE lists Nigerian pathways for garment making, Adire, embellishment, fashion/textile machine repair and leather work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes a Nigerian fashion-sector and training ecosystem; it is not a vacancy count, universal client demand ranking or single qualification requirement for every fashion or textile title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian luxury, jewellery, leather and craft enterprise context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian luxury and craft enterprise including fashion, leather, jewellery, accessories, furniture and creative-product work
findings: Nigeria's fashion and creative-sector institutions identify fashion, leather and creative enterprises as an active value chain; the 2026 UNDP Nigeria and Lagos State MSME spotlight specifically covers fashion, leather and creative enterprises, while government-linked creative-economy initiatives include fashion and related cultural production.
source_summaries.limitations: This is Nigerian ecosystem and enterprise evidence, not a direct vacancy signal or proof that every jewellery, luxury, furniture or accessory title has a distinct local employer market.

Nigerian archives, records, museum collections and digitisation context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian records management, archives, museum collections, cataloguing, conservation, digitisation, audio-visual preservation and public access
findings: The National Archives describes preservation, records-management training, digitisation and training collaborations for archivists and records officers.
National museum and film-archive sources describe collection documentation, cataloguing, imaging, conservation and audio-visual preservation.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources support records and collections practice but do not establish one universal museum, archive or commercial software stack.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE National Occupational Standards and Federal TVET trade pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian vocational and technical pathways including garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web, health and safety and other occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current NOS catalogue names occupational standards and levels for garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web and other trades.
The Federal TVET initiative describes accredited centres, practical skills, employment and entrepreneurship pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS or TVET pathway is evidence of a Nigerian training route, not a claim that every employer requires the listed level or that one trade credential is interchangeable with a degree or professional licence.

source_summaries.name: National Commission for Museums and Monuments functions and museum-practice standards
Nigerian library, archive, museum and documentary-heritage context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian archives, records management, documentary heritage, preservation, access, cultural collections and information services
findings: The National Archives of Nigeria preserves documentary records and advises public institutions on records handling, transfer and preservation.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian archives and records context; exact professional requirements depend on institution, collection and title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian energy planning, efficiency and sustainable-energy context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian energy policy, planning, statistics, renewable energy, energy efficiency, electricity, fossil fuels and sustainable-energy development
findings: The Energy Commission of Nigeria identifies national energy planning and policy implementation, energy statistics, energy information systems, electricity and fossil-fuel functions, renewable-energy research and energy-efficiency or sustainable-development work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian energy-sector and planning context, not a universal building-assessor licence, project-vacancy count or qualification for every hydropower, pipeline, energy or conservation title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian higher-education teaching, administration, research and quality-assurance context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian university and tertiary education accreditation, academic planning, admissions, quality assurance, research, student support, curriculum and institutional administration
findings: NUC describes Nigerian university accreditation, minimum academic standards, academic planning, inspection, student services, research and institutional quality assurance; TETFund TERAS describes Nigerian tertiary research repositories and services for researchers, students and institutions; NBTE documents technical-tertiary admissions and academic-board responsibilities.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian higher-education functions and regulatory context, not a universal appointment route, academic rank or credential for every teaching, coaching or training title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian tourism, travel, hospitality accreditation and training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian destination development, tour operations, travel consultancy, guiding, hospitality standards, tourism marketing, research, accreditation and practitioner certification
findings: NTDA describes regulation, accreditation, classification, marketing, research, capacity building and tour-operation services across Nigeria's tourism value chain.
NIHOTOUR's registration portal describes certification and verification of hospitality, travel and tourism practitioners through a national registry.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian tourism and hospitality context; it does not establish a vacancy count, one certificate for every travel title or a universal requirement across all employers and states.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian automotive repair, vehicle engineering, EV and motorsport training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian automobile repair and maintenance, electric and CNG vehicle training, automotive engineering design tools, vehicle inspection and motorsport officials and engineering pathways
findings: Government and NADDC sources describe nationwide automobile-maintenance, electric-vehicle, CNG and automotive software-capacity training.
ATCN describes Nigerian motorsport governance, driver/official training and an FIA engineering scholarship pathway.
source_summaries.limitations: These are sector training and ecosystem signals; they do not establish one universal automotive tool stack or a licence for every vehicle, motorsport or engineering role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian environmental science, biodiversity, water-quality and environmental-health context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian environmental science, environmental health, biodiversity conservation, water and air quality, pollution control, environmental audit, natural resources and sustainability
findings: NESREA describes Nigerian environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, water-quality and pollution standards, environmental audits, environmental data, ecosystem conservation and research; EHCON regulates and licenses environmental-health specialists, officers, technicians and assistants; the Federal Ministry of Environment identifies chemical, waste, sewage, air-emissions and environmental-health functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian environmental and environmental-health practice context; it is not a national vacancy count and environmental-health registration should not be applied to every environmental scientist or ecologist.

source_summaries.name: NIHOTOUR and Nigerian Tourism Development Authority practitioner registration and accreditation
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian hospitality, travel and tourism practitioner registration/certification and enterprise accreditation
findings: NIHOTOUR describes registration, certification and verification of practitioners; NTDA describes accreditation and classification of hospitality and tourism enterprises.
source_summaries.limitations: Practitioner and enterprise routes differ; neither is a universal credential for every tourism or retail role.

source_summaries.name: University of Ilorin museum and archival certificate/diploma pathway
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian museum, archival, cultural and heritage certificate and diploma education
findings: The University of Ilorin announced 2025/2026 certificate and diploma programmes in museum and archival studies, cultural studies and creative arts.
source_summaries.limitations: An education certificate/diploma route is not a universal statutory licence or proof of demand for every heritage role.

source_summaries.name: WIPO Nigeria and Music Business Academy professional training
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian music and entertainment business training, intellectual property and employability capacity building
findings: WIPO Nigeria described a 2024/2025 Music Business Academy scholarship and a nine-month vocational programme for African music-industry professionals.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports a sector training route, not a universal music-production certification or licence.

findings: NTDA describes regulation, accreditation, classification, marketing, research, capacity building and tour-operation services across Nigeria's tourism value chain.
NIHOTOUR's registration portal describes certification and verification of hospitality, travel and tourism practitioners through a national registry.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian tourism and hospitality context; it does not establish a vacancy count, one certificate for every travel title or a universal requirement across all employers and states.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian automotive repair, vehicle engineering, EV and motorsport training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian automobile repair and maintenance, electric and CNG vehicle training, automotive engineering design tools, vehicle inspection and motorsport officials and engineering pathways
findings: Government and NADDC sources describe nationwide automobile-maintenance, electric-vehicle, CNG and automotive software-capacity training.
ATCN describes Nigerian motorsport governance, driver/official training and an FIA engineering scholarship pathway.
source_summaries.limitations: These are sector training and ecosystem signals; they do not establish one universal automotive tool stack or a licence for every vehicle, motorsport or engineering role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian environmental science, biodiversity, water-quality and environmental-health context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian environmental science, environmental health, biodiversity conservation, water and air quality, pollution control, environmental audit, natural resources and sustainability
findings: NESREA describes Nigerian environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, water-quality and pollution standards, environmental audits, environmental data, ecosystem conservation and research; EHCON regulates and licenses environmental-health specialists, officers, technicians and assistants; the Federal Ministry of Environment identifies chemical, waste, sewage, air-emissions and environmental-health functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian environmental and environmental-health practice context; it is not a national vacancy count and environmental-health registration should not be applied to every environmental scientist or ecologist.

source_summaries.name: NIHOTOUR and Nigerian Tourism Development Authority practitioner registration and accreditation
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian hospitality, travel and tourism practitioner registration/certification and enterprise accreditation
findings: NIHOTOUR describes registration, certification and verification of practitioners; NTDA describes accreditation and classification of hospitality and tourism enterprises.
source_summaries.limitations: Practitioner and enterprise routes differ; neither is a universal credential for every tourism or retail role.

source_summaries.name: University of Ilorin museum and archival certificate/diploma pathway
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian museum, archival, cultural and heritage certificate and diploma education
findings: The University of Ilorin announced 2025/2026 certificate and diploma programmes in museum and archival studies, cultural studies and creative arts.
source_summaries.limitations: An education certificate/diploma route is not a universal statutory licence or proof of demand for every heritage role.

source_summaries.name: WIPO Nigeria and Music Business Academy professional training
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian music and entertainment business training, intellectual property and employability capacity building
findings: WIPO Nigeria described a 2024/2025 Music Business Academy scholarship and a nine-month vocational programme for African music-industry professionals.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports a sector training route, not a universal music-production certification or licence.

National museum and film-archive sources describe collection documentation, cataloguing, imaging, conservation and audio-visual preservation.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources support records and collections practice but do not establish one universal museum, archive or commercial software stack.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE National Occupational Standards and Federal TVET trade pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian vocational and technical pathways including garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web, health and safety and other occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current NOS catalogue names occupational standards and levels for garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web and other trades.
The Federal TVET initiative describes accredited centres, practical skills, employment and entrepreneurship pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS or TVET pathway is evidence of a Nigerian training route, not a claim that every employer requires the listed level or that one trade credential is interchangeable with a degree or professional licence.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian archives and records context; exact professional requirements depend on institution, collection and title.

findings: The Nigerian Fashion Council describes itself as a Federal Government-mandated Sector Skills Council inaugurated through NBTE and identifies a fashion value chain involving designers, craftsmen, manufacturers, innovators and associations; NBTE lists Nigerian pathways for garment making, Adire, embellishment, fashion/textile machine repair and leather work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes a Nigerian fashion-sector and training ecosystem; it is not a vacancy count, universal client demand ranking or single qualification requirement for every fashion or textile title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian luxury, jewellery, leather and craft enterprise context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian luxury and craft enterprise including fashion, leather, jewellery, accessories, furniture and creative-product work
findings: Nigeria's fashion and creative-sector institutions identify fashion, leather and creative enterprises as an active value chain; the 2026 UNDP Nigeria and Lagos State MSME spotlight specifically covers fashion, leather and creative enterprises, while government-linked creative-economy initiatives include fashion and related cultural production.
source_summaries.limitations: This is Nigerian ecosystem and enterprise evidence, not a direct vacancy signal or proof that every jewellery, luxury, furniture or accessory title has a distinct local employer market.

source_summaries.name: NIHOTOUR and Nigerian Tourism Development Authority practitioner registration and accreditation
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian hospitality, travel and tourism practitioner registration/certification and enterprise accreditation
findings: NIHOTOUR describes registration, certification and verification of practitioners; NTDA describes accreditation and classification of hospitality and tourism enterprises.
source_summaries.limitations: Practitioner and enterprise routes differ; neither is a universal credential for every tourism or retail role.

source_summaries.name: Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria teacher standards and PQE
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian teacher education, accreditation, registration, professional qualifying examination and competency assessment
findings: TRCN describes its responsibility for teacher-education standards, programme accreditation, qualification approval, professional registration and competency assessment; its 2026 updates include PQE results and school-accreditation policy implementation.
source_summaries.limitations: TRCN applies to teaching practice within its mandate, not to every education, training, research or childcare role.

source_summaries.name: Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria PQE and registration framework
University of Ilorin museum and archival certificate/diploma pathway
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian museum, archival, cultural and heritage certificate and diploma education
findings: The University of Ilorin announced 2025/2026 certificate and diploma programmes in museum and archival studies, cultural studies and creative arts.
source_summaries.limitations: An education certificate/diploma route is not a universal statutory licence or proof of demand for every heritage role.

source_summaries.name: WIPO Nigeria and Music Business Academy professional training
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian music and entertainment business training, intellectual property and employability capacity building
findings: WIPO Nigeria described a 2024/2025 Music Business Academy scholarship and a nine-month vocational programme for African music-industry professionals.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports a sector training route, not a universal music-production certification or licence.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian diplomatic missions, consular work, ambassadorial appointments and Foreign Affairs Officer cadres
findings: Nigeria's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists embassies, high commissions, consulates and permanent missions and its current communications identify ambassadorial and consular functions.

The Nigerian Public Service Rules describe Foreign Affairs Officer grades including Third Secretary, Second Secretary, First Secretary, Counsellor and Minister Counsellor, and distinguish diplomatic and non-diplomatic Foreign Service branches.
source_summaries.limitations: This is official public-service and diplomatic role evidence, not a current vacancy count or guarantee that a student can enter a diplomatic rank without the applicable public-service appointment, training and eligibility route.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian public-service administration, integrity, privacy and compliance context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian public administration, policy, planning, public-sector compliance, anti-corruption, ethics, data protection and government records or programme work
findings: OHCSF publishes Nigerian public-service rules, policy and civil-service resources; ICPC describes review of public-body systems, anti-corruption transparency units, monitoring, reporting, ethics and compliance work in MDAs; NDPC documents data-protection compliance, audits, data-protection officers and licensed compliance organisations in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian public-service and compliance functions; they are not evidence that every global public-office title exists locally, nor a universal qualification or vacancy count for each role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian security, fire, border and correctional-service context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fire prevention and rescue, emergency response, border security, immigration control, policing, correctional custody, probation, rehabilitation and public safety
findings: The Federal Fire Service describes fire prevention, mitigation, rescue, life and property protection, training and emergency response; NIS describes border control, surveillance, immigration compliance, airport, seaport, intelligence and cybersecurity functions; NCoS describes secure and humane custody, risk and needs assessment, rehabilitation, probation, parole and non-custodial measures; PSC/NPF materials establish Nigerian police recruitment and service context.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources support the named public-service families and functions; they do not establish a counterpart, private-security licence or vacancy count for every global guard, transport, animal, gaming or specialist rescue title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian state and local-government office context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian state governors, local-government chairmen and councilors/councillors, local-government executive and legislative functions
findings: A Nigerian state local-government law describes the Local Government Executive Council, its Chairman as chief executive and accounting officer, Vice Chairman, Supervisors and the Legislative Council with elected or appointed councilor roles; it also refers to the Governor in the state oath and oversight context.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports Nigerian public-office counterparts and institutional functions, not a vacancy count or a universal professional qualification; 'mayor' is not treated as the canonical Nigerian title here.

Nigeria Immigration Service operational and service context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian immigration, border-management, passport, visa and residence-permit functions
findings: The Nigeria Immigration Service identifies border-management, passport, visa, ECOWAS travel and residence-permit services, while the Ministry of Interior describes immigration and expatriate-work-permit administration as part of the national service environment.
source_summaries.limitations: Official service functions establish the Nigerian role family and institutional context; they do not establish a current vacancy, rank-equivalence or universal qualification for every immigration or passport role.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Procurement Certification Programme
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian public and private procurement practitioners
findings: The programme describes four Nigerian procurement-certification tiers and skills including communication, teamwork, time management, deadlines, ethics and risk management, with prerequisites varying by tier.
source_summaries.limitations: The pathway is for procurement practice and does not apply to every purchasing, logistics, project or administrative role.

source_summaries.name: OHCSF Personnel Audit and Skills Gap Analysis project
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian federal civil-service skills identification, development and gap analysis
findings: The OHCSF PASGA portal describes a project to identify and develop the skills of Nigerian public servants and build a data-driven, globally competitive civil service.
source_summaries.limitations: The portal is public-service skills context and does not establish a private-sector requirement or a single certification.

source_summaries.name: Project Managers Development Association of Nigeria
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian project-management professional development and IPMA-aligned certification levels
findings: PMDAN identifies itself as Nigeria's IPMA member association, describes four certification levels and publishes project-execution and project-management learning activities.
source_summaries.limitations: Professional-body certification is a pathway, not a universal employer requirement for every project-support or coordination role.

source_summaries.name: Project Management Institute Nigeria Chapter professional development and certification pathway
Nigeria Police Service Commission recruitment and inspector context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian police recruitment, inspector and specialist appointment, detective training and law-enforcement work
findings: The Police Service Commission identifies recruitment of constables, appointment of cadet ASPs and Inspectors and specialist appointments; Nigeria Police Academy materials describe cadet Inspector training including police duties, law, detective courses and practical attachment.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes an official Nigerian policing pathway and training context, not a current vacancy for every police rank or a claim that civilian criminal-investigator titles map directly to a police appointment.

source_summaries.name: Federal Government social-work professionalisation and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice, professionalisation, standards and capacity-building context
findings: The Federal Government described work to strengthen social-work practice in Nigeria, including professionalisation and standards challenges under the Social Work Practitioners Act 2022 context.
source_summaries.limitations: The article supports Nigerian practice context but does not establish one compulsory credential for every care, counselling or social-service role.

source_summaries.name: TRCN safeguarding resources for Nigerian schools
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian child protection, learner safety, violence-free schools and safeguarding practice
findings: TRCN provides resources on child protection, safety, security and violence-free schools and describes protocols and standards for protecting children and learners.
source_summaries.limitations: Safeguarding resources support education and child-facing practice; they do not create one universal certificate for all social-service or childcare roles.

source_summaries.name: Bureau of Public Service Reforms National Strategy for Public Service Reform
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian civil-service administration, competency, performance, accountability and professionalisation
findings: The strategy describes a professional, results-oriented, competent, accountable and citizen-centred Nigerian public service, including merit-based recruitment, performance management, job evaluation and professionalisation of core cadres.
source_summaries.limitations: A reform strategy supplies public-service capability context, not a universal qualification for every public or private-sector role.

source_summaries.name: Central Bank of Nigeria Governor institutional role
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria's central-bank governance, monetary-policy, financial-system and public-sector leadership role
findings: The official Central Bank of Nigeria biography identifies the Governor of the CBN as a Nigerian public leadership role and records the current officeholder's banking, public-sector, economics, finance and governance background.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes the Nigerian office and institutional context, not a recurring vacancy, a universal career route or a claim that every central-bank employee needs the Governor's qualifications.

Jobberman Nigeria jobs
MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
National Assembly of Nigeria legislative roles
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian Senate, House of Representatives, legislative representation, lawmaking and public oversight
findings: The official National Assembly describes the Senate as one chamber of Nigeria's bicameral legislature, made up of elected Senators, with lawmaking, representation, public-institution scrutiny and committee responsibilities; the site also identifies House Members as the other parliamentary membership pathway.
source_summaries.limitations: This is elected public-office context rather than an ordinary employment vacancy or a guaranteed career pathway; nomination, election, constitutional eligibility and political processes are distinct from skills training.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Bar Association annual practising list, MCPD and practice certificate requirements
National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE Operational Guidelines for Sector Skills Councils
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian sector-skills governance and occupational-standard development across ICT, engineering, transport/logistics and other sectors
findings: The guidelines describe sector-skills-council structures used to coordinate occupational standards, industry participation and skills development in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: The guidelines support skills-governance context and do not establish a credential or demand signal for an individual role.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Customs Service recruitment and cadre context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian Customs Service officer recruitment, cadres, revenue, border and anti-smuggling functions
findings: The Nigeria Customs Service recruitment portal describes Superintendent, Inspectorate and Customs Assistant cadres and identifies revenue collection, trade and anti-smuggling functions; an official 2025 update reported 3,927 declared vacancies across those cadres.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes an official Nigerian Customs pathway and service context, not a current open vacancy, guaranteed appointment or one universal qualification for every customs-related role.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Council for Theological Studies and Christian Education and Nigerian theological training
Nigeria Foreign Service and Ministry of Foreign Affairs role context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian diplomatic missions, consular work, ambassadorial appointments and Foreign Affairs Officer cadres
findings: Nigeria's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists embassies, high commissions, consulates and permanent missions and its current communications identify ambassadorial and consular functions.

The Nigerian Public Service Rules describe Foreign Affairs Officer grades including Third Secretary, Second Secretary, First Secretary, Counsellor and Minister Counsellor, and distinguish diplomatic and non-diplomatic Foreign Service branches.
source_summaries.limitations: This is official public-service and diplomatic role evidence, not a current vacancy count or guarantee that a student can enter a diplomatic rank without the applicable public-service appointment, training and eligibility route.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian public-service administration, integrity, privacy and compliance context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian public administration, policy, planning, public-sector compliance, anti-corruption, ethics, data protection and government records or programme work
findings: OHCSF publishes Nigerian public-service rules, policy and civil-service resources; ICPC describes review of public-body systems, anti-corruption transparency units, monitoring, reporting, ethics and compliance work in MDAs; NDPC documents data-protection compliance, audits, data-protection officers and licensed compliance organisations in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian public-service and compliance functions; they are not evidence that every global public-office title exists locally, nor a universal qualification or vacancy count for each role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian security, fire, border and correctional-service context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fire prevention and rescue, emergency response, border security, immigration control, policing, correctional custody, probation, rehabilitation and public safety
findings: The Federal Fire Service describes fire prevention, mitigation, rescue, life and property protection, training and emergency response; NIS describes border control, surveillance, immigration compliance, airport, seaport, intelligence and cybersecurity functions; NCoS describes secure and humane custody, risk and needs assessment, rehabilitation, probation, parole and non-custodial measures; PSC/NPF materials establish Nigerian police recruitment and service context.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources support the named public-service families and functions; they do not establish a counterpart, private-security licence or vacancy count for every global guard, transport, animal, gaming or specialist rescue title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian state and local-government office context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian state governors, local-government chairmen and councilors/councillors, local-government executive and legislative functions
findings: A Nigerian state local-government law describes the Local Government Executive Council, its Chairman as chief executive and accounting officer, Vice Chairman, Supervisors and the Legislative Council with elected or appointed councilor roles; it also refers to the Governor in the state oath and oversight context.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports Nigerian public-office counterparts and institutional functions, not a vacancy count or a universal professional qualification; 'mayor' is not treated as the canonical Nigerian title here.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of International Affairs and Foreign Affairs diplomatic-training context
NIMASA port-state and marine inspection context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian port-state control, marine surveying, ship inspection, cargo-related safety documentation and maritime compliance
findings: NIMASA describes port-state-control inspections, marine surveyors boarding ships, checking certificates and documentation, examining vessels and crews, recording deficiencies and applying Nigerian and IMO-aligned inspection procedures.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports a Nigerian marine and port-inspection function that is adjacent to the canonical marine cargo inspector title; it does not establish one universal job title, vacancy count or personal certification requirement for every cargo-inspection role.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Immigration Service mandate, travel-document operations and enlistment requirements
Nigeria Immigration Service operational and service context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian immigration, border-management, passport, visa and residence-permit functions
findings: The Nigeria Immigration Service identifies border-management, passport, visa, ECOWAS travel and residence-permit services, while the Ministry of Interior describes immigration and expatriate-work-permit administration as part of the national service environment.
source_summaries.limitations: Official service functions establish the Nigerian role family and institutional context; they do not establish a current vacancy, rank-equivalence or universal qualification for every immigration or passport role.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Procurement Certification Programme
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian public and private procurement practitioners
findings: The programme describes four Nigerian procurement-certification tiers and skills including communication, teamwork, time management, deadlines, ethics and risk management, with prerequisites varying by tier.
source_summaries.limitations: The pathway is for procurement practice and does not apply to every purchasing, logistics, project or administrative role.

source_summaries.name: OHCSF Personnel Audit and Skills Gap Analysis project
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian federal civil-service skills identification, development and gap analysis
findings: The OHCSF PASGA portal describes a project to identify and develop the skills of Nigerian public servants and build a data-driven, globally competitive civil service.
source_summaries.limitations: The portal is public-service skills context and does not establish a private-sector requirement or a single certification.

source_summaries.name: Project Managers Development Association of Nigeria
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian project-management professional development and IPMA-aligned certification levels
findings: PMDAN identifies itself as Nigeria's IPMA member association, describes four certification levels and publishes project-execution and project-management learning activities.
source_summaries.limitations: Professional-body certification is a pathway, not a universal employer requirement for every project-support or coordination role.

source_summaries.name: Project Management Institute Nigeria Chapter professional development and certification pathway
Nigeria Police Service Commission recruitment and inspector context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian police recruitment, inspector and specialist appointment, detective training and law-enforcement work
findings: The Police Service Commission identifies recruitment of constables, appointment of cadet ASPs and Inspectors and specialist appointments; Nigeria Police Academy materials describe cadet Inspector training including police duties, law, detective courses and practical attachment.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes an official Nigerian policing pathway and training context, not a current vacancy for every police rank or a claim that civilian criminal-investigator titles map directly to a police appointment.

source_summaries.name: Federal Government social-work professionalisation and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice, professionalisation, standards and capacity-building context
findings: The Federal Government described work to strengthen social-work practice in Nigeria, including professionalisation and standards challenges under the Social Work Practitioners Act 2022 context.
source_summaries.limitations: The article supports Nigerian practice context but does not establish one compulsory credential for every care, counselling or social-service role.

source_summaries.name: TRCN safeguarding resources for Nigerian schools
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian child protection, learner safety, violence-free schools and safeguarding practice
findings: TRCN provides resources on child protection, safety, security and violence-free schools and describes protocols and standards for protecting children and learners.
source_summaries.limitations: Safeguarding resources support education and child-facing practice; they do not create one universal certificate for all social-service or childcare roles.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian diplomatic missions, consular work, ambassadorial appointments and Foreign Affairs Officer cadres
findings: Nigeria's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists embassies, high commissions, consulates and permanent missions and its current communications identify ambassadorial and consular functions.

The Nigerian Public Service Rules describe Foreign Affairs Officer grades including Third Secretary, Second Secretary, First Secretary, Counsellor and Minister Counsellor, and distinguish diplomatic and non-diplomatic Foreign Service branches.
source_summaries.limitations: This is official public-service and diplomatic role evidence, not a current vacancy count or guarantee that a student can enter a diplomatic rank without the applicable public-service appointment, training and eligibility route.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian public-service administration, integrity, privacy and compliance context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian public administration, policy, planning, public-sector compliance, anti-corruption, ethics, data protection and government records or programme work
findings: OHCSF publishes Nigerian public-service rules, policy and civil-service resources; ICPC describes review of public-body systems, anti-corruption transparency units, monitoring, reporting, ethics and compliance work in MDAs; NDPC documents data-protection compliance, audits, data-protection officers and licensed compliance organisations in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian public-service and compliance functions; they are not evidence that every global public-office title exists locally, nor a universal qualification or vacancy count for each role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian security, fire, border and correctional-service context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fire prevention and rescue, emergency response, border security, immigration control, policing, correctional custody, probation, rehabilitation and public safety
findings: The Federal Fire Service describes fire prevention, mitigation, rescue, life and property protection, training and emergency response; NIS describes border control, surveillance, immigration compliance, airport, seaport, intelligence and cybersecurity functions; NCoS describes secure and humane custody, risk and needs assessment, rehabilitation, probation, parole and non-custodial measures; PSC/NPF materials establish Nigerian police recruitment and service context.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources support the named public-service families and functions; they do not establish a counterpart, private-security licence or vacancy count for every global guard, transport, animal, gaming or specialist rescue title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian state and local-government office context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian state governors, local-government chairmen and councilors/councillors, local-government executive and legislative functions
findings: A Nigerian state local-government law describes the Local Government Executive Council, its Chairman as chief executive and accounting officer, Vice Chairman, Supervisors and the Legislative Council with elected or appointed councilor roles; it also refers to the Governor in the state oath and oversight context.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports Nigerian public-office counterparts and institutional functions, not a vacancy count or a universal professional qualification; 'mayor' is not treated as the canonical Nigerian title here.

findings: NIMASA describes port-state-control inspections, marine surveyors boarding ships, checking certificates and documentation, examining vessels and crews, recording deficiencies and applying Nigerian and IMO-aligned inspection procedures.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports a Nigerian marine and port-inspection function that is adjacent to the canonical marine cargo inspector title; it does not establish one universal job title, vacancy count or personal certification requirement for every cargo-inspection role.

source_summaries.name: OHCSF Personnel Audit and Skills Gap Analysis project
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian federal civil-service skills identification, development and gap analysis
findings: The OHCSF PASGA portal describes a project to identify and develop the skills of Nigerian public servants and build a data-driven, globally competitive civil service.
source_summaries.limitations: The portal is public-service skills context and does not establish a private-sector requirement or a single certification.

source_summaries.name: Project Managers Development Association of Nigeria
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian project-management professional development and IPMA-aligned certification levels
findings: PMDAN identifies itself as Nigeria's IPMA member association, describes four certification levels and publishes project-execution and project-management learning activities.
source_summaries.limitations: Professional-body certification is a pathway, not a universal employer requirement for every project-support or coordination role.

source_summaries.name: Project Management Institute Nigeria Chapter professional development and certification pathway
Nigeria Police Service Commission recruitment and inspector context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian police recruitment, inspector and specialist appointment, detective training and law-enforcement work
findings: The Police Service Commission identifies recruitment of constables, appointment of cadet ASPs and Inspectors and specialist appointments; Nigeria Police Academy materials describe cadet Inspector training including police duties, law, detective courses and practical attachment.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes an official Nigerian policing pathway and training context, not a current vacancy for every police rank or a claim that civilian criminal-investigator titles map directly to a police appointment.

source_summaries.name: Federal Government social-work professionalisation and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice, professionalisation, standards and capacity-building context
findings: The Federal Government described work to strengthen social-work practice in Nigeria, including professionalisation and standards challenges under the Social Work Practitioners Act 2022 context.
source_summaries.limitations: The article supports Nigerian practice context but does not establish one compulsory credential for every care, counselling or social-service role.

source_summaries.name: TRCN safeguarding resources for Nigerian schools
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian child protection, learner safety, violence-free schools and safeguarding practice
findings: TRCN provides resources on child protection, safety, security and violence-free schools and describes protocols and standards for protecting children and learners.
source_summaries.limitations: Safeguarding resources support education and child-facing practice; they do not create one universal certificate for all social-service or childcare roles.

source_summaries.name: Bureau of Public Service Reforms National Strategy for Public Service Reform
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian civil-service administration, competency, performance, accountability and professionalisation
findings: The strategy describes a professional, results-oriented, competent, accountable and citizen-centred Nigerian public service, including merit-based recruitment, performance management, job evaluation and professionalisation of core cadres.
source_summaries.limitations: A reform strategy supplies public-service capability context, not a universal qualification for every public or private-sector role.

source_summaries.name: Central Bank of Nigeria Governor institutional role
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria's central-bank governance, monetary-policy, financial-system and public-sector leadership role
findings: The official Central Bank of Nigeria biography identifies the Governor of the CBN as a Nigerian public leadership role and records the current officeholder's banking, public-sector, economics, finance and governance background.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes the Nigerian office and institutional context, not a recurring vacancy, a universal career route or a claim that every central-bank employee needs the Governor's qualifications.
