Jobberman Nigeria jobs
MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
National Assembly of Nigeria legislative roles
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian Senate, House of Representatives, legislative representation, lawmaking and public oversight
findings: The official National Assembly describes the Senate as one chamber of Nigeria's bicameral legislature, made up of elected Senators, with lawmaking, representation, public-institution scrutiny and committee responsibilities; the site also identifies House Members as the other parliamentary membership pathway.
source_summaries.limitations: This is elected public-office context rather than an ordinary employment vacancy or a guaranteed career pathway; nomination, election, constitutional eligibility and political processes are distinct from skills training.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Bar Association annual practising list, MCPD and practice certificate requirements
National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE Operational Guidelines for Sector Skills Councils
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian sector-skills governance and occupational-standard development across ICT, engineering, transport/logistics and other sectors
findings: The guidelines describe sector-skills-council structures used to coordinate occupational standards, industry participation and skills development in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: The guidelines support skills-governance context and do not establish a credential or demand signal for an individual role.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Customs Service recruitment and cadre context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian Customs Service officer recruitment, cadres, revenue, border and anti-smuggling functions
findings: The Nigeria Customs Service recruitment portal describes Superintendent, Inspectorate and Customs Assistant cadres and identifies revenue collection, trade and anti-smuggling functions; an official 2025 update reported 3,927 declared vacancies across those cadres.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes an official Nigerian Customs pathway and service context, not a current open vacancy, guaranteed appointment or one universal qualification for every customs-related role.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Council for Theological Studies and Christian Education and Nigerian theological training
Nigeria Foreign Service and Ministry of Foreign Affairs role context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian diplomatic missions, consular work, ambassadorial appointments and Foreign Affairs Officer cadres
findings: Nigeria's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists embassies, high commissions, consulates and permanent missions and its current communications identify ambassadorial and consular functions.

The Nigerian Public Service Rules describe Foreign Affairs Officer grades including Third Secretary, Second Secretary, First Secretary, Counsellor and Minister Counsellor, and distinguish diplomatic and non-diplomatic Foreign Service branches.
source_summaries.limitations: This is official public-service and diplomatic role evidence, not a current vacancy count or guarantee that a student can enter a diplomatic rank without the applicable public-service appointment, training and eligibility route.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian public-service administration, integrity, privacy and compliance context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian public administration, policy, planning, public-sector compliance, anti-corruption, ethics, data protection and government records or programme work
findings: OHCSF publishes Nigerian public-service rules, policy and civil-service resources; ICPC describes review of public-body systems, anti-corruption transparency units, monitoring, reporting, ethics and compliance work in MDAs; NDPC documents data-protection compliance, audits, data-protection officers and licensed compliance organisations in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian public-service and compliance functions; they are not evidence that every global public-office title exists locally, nor a universal qualification or vacancy count for each role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian security, fire, border and correctional-service context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fire prevention and rescue, emergency response, border security, immigration control, policing, correctional custody, probation, rehabilitation and public safety
findings: The Federal Fire Service describes fire prevention, mitigation, rescue, life and property protection, training and emergency response; NIS describes border control, surveillance, immigration compliance, airport, seaport, intelligence and cybersecurity functions; NCoS describes secure and humane custody, risk and needs assessment, rehabilitation, probation, parole and non-custodial measures; PSC/NPF materials establish Nigerian police recruitment and service context.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources support the named public-service families and functions; they do not establish a counterpart, private-security licence or vacancy count for every global guard, transport, animal, gaming or specialist rescue title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian state and local-government office context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian state governors, local-government chairmen and councilors/councillors, local-government executive and legislative functions
findings: A Nigerian state local-government law describes the Local Government Executive Council, its Chairman as chief executive and accounting officer, Vice Chairman, Supervisors and the Legislative Council with elected or appointed councilor roles; it also refers to the Governor in the state oath and oversight context.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports Nigerian public-office counterparts and institutional functions, not a vacancy count or a universal professional qualification; 'mayor' is not treated as the canonical Nigerian title here.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of International Affairs and Foreign Affairs diplomatic-training context
NIMASA port-state and marine inspection context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian port-state control, marine surveying, ship inspection, cargo-related safety documentation and maritime compliance
findings: NIMASA describes port-state-control inspections, marine surveyors boarding ships, checking certificates and documentation, examining vessels and crews, recording deficiencies and applying Nigerian and IMO-aligned inspection procedures.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports a Nigerian marine and port-inspection function that is adjacent to the canonical marine cargo inspector title; it does not establish one universal job title, vacancy count or personal certification requirement for every cargo-inspection role.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Immigration Service mandate, travel-document operations and enlistment requirements
Nigeria Immigration Service operational and service context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian immigration, border-management, passport, visa and residence-permit functions
findings: The Nigeria Immigration Service identifies border-management, passport, visa, ECOWAS travel and residence-permit services, while the Ministry of Interior describes immigration and expatriate-work-permit administration as part of the national service environment.
source_summaries.limitations: Official service functions establish the Nigerian role family and institutional context; they do not establish a current vacancy, rank-equivalence or universal qualification for every immigration or passport role.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Procurement Certification Programme
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian public and private procurement practitioners
findings: The programme describes four Nigerian procurement-certification tiers and skills including communication, teamwork, time management, deadlines, ethics and risk management, with prerequisites varying by tier.
source_summaries.limitations: The pathway is for procurement practice and does not apply to every purchasing, logistics, project or administrative role.

source_summaries.name: OHCSF Personnel Audit and Skills Gap Analysis project
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian federal civil-service skills identification, development and gap analysis
findings: The OHCSF PASGA portal describes a project to identify and develop the skills of Nigerian public servants and build a data-driven, globally competitive civil service.
source_summaries.limitations: The portal is public-service skills context and does not establish a private-sector requirement or a single certification.

source_summaries.name: Project Managers Development Association of Nigeria
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian project-management professional development and IPMA-aligned certification levels
findings: PMDAN identifies itself as Nigeria's IPMA member association, describes four certification levels and publishes project-execution and project-management learning activities.
source_summaries.limitations: Professional-body certification is a pathway, not a universal employer requirement for every project-support or coordination role.

source_summaries.name: Project Management Institute Nigeria Chapter professional development and certification pathway
Nigeria Police Service Commission recruitment and inspector context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian police recruitment, inspector and specialist appointment, detective training and law-enforcement work
findings: The Police Service Commission identifies recruitment of constables, appointment of cadet ASPs and Inspectors and specialist appointments; Nigeria Police Academy materials describe cadet Inspector training including police duties, law, detective courses and practical attachment.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes an official Nigerian policing pathway and training context, not a current vacancy for every police rank or a claim that civilian criminal-investigator titles map directly to a police appointment.

source_summaries.name: Federal Government social-work professionalisation and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice, professionalisation, standards and capacity-building context
findings: The Federal Government described work to strengthen social-work practice in Nigeria, including professionalisation and standards challenges under the Social Work Practitioners Act 2022 context.
source_summaries.limitations: The article supports Nigerian practice context but does not establish one compulsory credential for every care, counselling or social-service role.

source_summaries.name: TRCN safeguarding resources for Nigerian schools
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian child protection, learner safety, violence-free schools and safeguarding practice
findings: TRCN provides resources on child protection, safety, security and violence-free schools and describes protocols and standards for protecting children and learners.
source_summaries.limitations: Safeguarding resources support education and child-facing practice; they do not create one universal certificate for all social-service or childcare roles.

source_summaries.name: Bureau of Public Service Reforms National Strategy for Public Service Reform
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian civil-service administration, competency, performance, accountability and professionalisation
findings: The strategy describes a professional, results-oriented, competent, accountable and citizen-centred Nigerian public service, including merit-based recruitment, performance management, job evaluation and professionalisation of core cadres.
source_summaries.limitations: A reform strategy supplies public-service capability context, not a universal qualification for every public or private-sector role.

source_summaries.name: Central Bank of Nigeria Governor institutional role
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria's central-bank governance, monetary-policy, financial-system and public-sector leadership role
findings: The official Central Bank of Nigeria biography identifies the Governor of the CBN as a Nigerian public leadership role and records the current officeholder's banking, public-sector, economics, finance and governance background.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes the Nigerian office and institutional context, not a recurring vacancy, a universal career route or a claim that every central-bank employee needs the Governor's qualifications.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian Senate, House of Representatives, legislative representation, lawmaking and public oversight
findings: The official National Assembly describes the Senate as one chamber of Nigeria's bicameral legislature, made up of elected Senators, with lawmaking, representation, public-institution scrutiny and committee responsibilities; the site also identifies House Members as the other parliamentary membership pathway.
source_summaries.limitations: This is elected public-office context rather than an ordinary employment vacancy or a guaranteed career pathway; nomination, election, constitutional eligibility and political processes are distinct from skills training.

findings: The guidelines describe sector-skills-council structures used to coordinate occupational standards, industry participation and skills development in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: The guidelines support skills-governance context and do not establish a credential or demand signal for an individual role.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Customs Service recruitment and cadre context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian Customs Service officer recruitment, cadres, revenue, border and anti-smuggling functions
findings: The Nigeria Customs Service recruitment portal describes Superintendent, Inspectorate and Customs Assistant cadres and identifies revenue collection, trade and anti-smuggling functions; an official 2025 update reported 3,927 declared vacancies across those cadres.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes an official Nigerian Customs pathway and service context, not a current open vacancy, guaranteed appointment or one universal qualification for every customs-related role.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Council for Theological Studies and Christian Education and Nigerian theological training
Nigeria Foreign Service and Ministry of Foreign Affairs role context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian diplomatic missions, consular work, ambassadorial appointments and Foreign Affairs Officer cadres
findings: Nigeria's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists embassies, high commissions, consulates and permanent missions and its current communications identify ambassadorial and consular functions.

The Nigerian Public Service Rules describe Foreign Affairs Officer grades including Third Secretary, Second Secretary, First Secretary, Counsellor and Minister Counsellor, and distinguish diplomatic and non-diplomatic Foreign Service branches.
source_summaries.limitations: This is official public-service and diplomatic role evidence, not a current vacancy count or guarantee that a student can enter a diplomatic rank without the applicable public-service appointment, training and eligibility route.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian public-service administration, integrity, privacy and compliance context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian public administration, policy, planning, public-sector compliance, anti-corruption, ethics, data protection and government records or programme work
findings: OHCSF publishes Nigerian public-service rules, policy and civil-service resources; ICPC describes review of public-body systems, anti-corruption transparency units, monitoring, reporting, ethics and compliance work in MDAs; NDPC documents data-protection compliance, audits, data-protection officers and licensed compliance organisations in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian public-service and compliance functions; they are not evidence that every global public-office title exists locally, nor a universal qualification or vacancy count for each role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian security, fire, border and correctional-service context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fire prevention and rescue, emergency response, border security, immigration control, policing, correctional custody, probation, rehabilitation and public safety
findings: The Federal Fire Service describes fire prevention, mitigation, rescue, life and property protection, training and emergency response; NIS describes border control, surveillance, immigration compliance, airport, seaport, intelligence and cybersecurity functions; NCoS describes secure and humane custody, risk and needs assessment, rehabilitation, probation, parole and non-custodial measures; PSC/NPF materials establish Nigerian police recruitment and service context.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources support the named public-service families and functions; they do not establish a counterpart, private-security licence or vacancy count for every global guard, transport, animal, gaming or specialist rescue title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian state and local-government office context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian state governors, local-government chairmen and councilors/councillors, local-government executive and legislative functions
findings: A Nigerian state local-government law describes the Local Government Executive Council, its Chairman as chief executive and accounting officer, Vice Chairman, Supervisors and the Legislative Council with elected or appointed councilor roles; it also refers to the Governor in the state oath and oversight context.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports Nigerian public-office counterparts and institutional functions, not a vacancy count or a universal professional qualification; 'mayor' is not treated as the canonical Nigerian title here.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of International Affairs and Foreign Affairs diplomatic-training context
NIMASA port-state and marine inspection context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian port-state control, marine surveying, ship inspection, cargo-related safety documentation and maritime compliance
findings: NIMASA describes port-state-control inspections, marine surveyors boarding ships, checking certificates and documentation, examining vessels and crews, recording deficiencies and applying Nigerian and IMO-aligned inspection procedures.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports a Nigerian marine and port-inspection function that is adjacent to the canonical marine cargo inspector title; it does not establish one universal job title, vacancy count or personal certification requirement for every cargo-inspection role.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Immigration Service mandate, travel-document operations and enlistment requirements
Nigeria Immigration Service operational and service context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian immigration, border-management, passport, visa and residence-permit functions
findings: The Nigeria Immigration Service identifies border-management, passport, visa, ECOWAS travel and residence-permit services, while the Ministry of Interior describes immigration and expatriate-work-permit administration as part of the national service environment.
source_summaries.limitations: Official service functions establish the Nigerian role family and institutional context; they do not establish a current vacancy, rank-equivalence or universal qualification for every immigration or passport role.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Procurement Certification Programme
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian public and private procurement practitioners
findings: The programme describes four Nigerian procurement-certification tiers and skills including communication, teamwork, time management, deadlines, ethics and risk management, with prerequisites varying by tier.
source_summaries.limitations: The pathway is for procurement practice and does not apply to every purchasing, logistics, project or administrative role.

source_summaries.name: OHCSF Personnel Audit and Skills Gap Analysis project
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian federal civil-service skills identification, development and gap analysis
findings: The OHCSF PASGA portal describes a project to identify and develop the skills of Nigerian public servants and build a data-driven, globally competitive civil service.
source_summaries.limitations: The portal is public-service skills context and does not establish a private-sector requirement or a single certification.

source_summaries.name: Project Managers Development Association of Nigeria
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian project-management professional development and IPMA-aligned certification levels
findings: PMDAN identifies itself as Nigeria's IPMA member association, describes four certification levels and publishes project-execution and project-management learning activities.
source_summaries.limitations: Professional-body certification is a pathway, not a universal employer requirement for every project-support or coordination role.

source_summaries.name: Project Management Institute Nigeria Chapter professional development and certification pathway
Nigeria Police Service Commission recruitment and inspector context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian police recruitment, inspector and specialist appointment, detective training and law-enforcement work
findings: The Police Service Commission identifies recruitment of constables, appointment of cadet ASPs and Inspectors and specialist appointments; Nigeria Police Academy materials describe cadet Inspector training including police duties, law, detective courses and practical attachment.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes an official Nigerian policing pathway and training context, not a current vacancy for every police rank or a claim that civilian criminal-investigator titles map directly to a police appointment.

source_summaries.name: Federal Government social-work professionalisation and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice, professionalisation, standards and capacity-building context
findings: The Federal Government described work to strengthen social-work practice in Nigeria, including professionalisation and standards challenges under the Social Work Practitioners Act 2022 context.
source_summaries.limitations: The article supports Nigerian practice context but does not establish one compulsory credential for every care, counselling or social-service role.

source_summaries.name: TRCN safeguarding resources for Nigerian schools
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian child protection, learner safety, violence-free schools and safeguarding practice
findings: TRCN provides resources on child protection, safety, security and violence-free schools and describes protocols and standards for protecting children and learners.
source_summaries.limitations: Safeguarding resources support education and child-facing practice; they do not create one universal certificate for all social-service or childcare roles.

source_summaries.name: Bureau of Public Service Reforms National Strategy for Public Service Reform
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian civil-service administration, competency, performance, accountability and professionalisation
findings: The strategy describes a professional, results-oriented, competent, accountable and citizen-centred Nigerian public service, including merit-based recruitment, performance management, job evaluation and professionalisation of core cadres.
source_summaries.limitations: A reform strategy supplies public-service capability context, not a universal qualification for every public or private-sector role.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice across public services, community development, teaching hospitals, NGOs, rehabilitation, care and correctional settings
findings: NASoW identifies social workers across schools, teaching hospitals, NGOs, ministries, rehabilitation centres, old people's homes, correctional centres and local, state and federal institutions.

NASoW Lagos names public-sector social welfare officers, community development officers, medical social workers, social-work educators, independent social workers and NGO social workers among its professional community.
source_summaries.limitations: Professional-body role-family context demonstrates Nigerian practice settings; it is not a vacancy count, universal title equivalence or proof that every specialised social-care occupation is established in every Nigerian setting.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian sector-skills governance and occupational-standard development across ICT, engineering, transport/logistics and other sectors
findings: The guidelines describe sector-skills-council structures used to coordinate occupational standards, industry participation and skills development in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: The guidelines support skills-governance context and do not establish a credential or demand signal for an individual role.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Council for Theological Studies and Christian Education and Nigerian theological training
Nigerian allied-health, radiography, rehabilitation and optometry context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian radiography, nuclear and diagnostic imaging, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, chiropractic, osteopathy, prosthetics and orthotics, optometry and allied-health education
findings: RRBN regulates radiography and related diagnostic or therapeutic radiography practice; MRTB regulates and licenses rehabilitation professions including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, prosthetics/orthotics, chiropractic and osteopathic practice; ODORBN regulates Nigerian optometrists and dispensing opticians; NUC allied-health standards identify Nigerian allied-health degree pathways and professional information practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian early-childhood care, primary education and childcare training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian early-childhood care and education, primary education, childcare settings, NCE minimum standards and learner safeguarding
findings: NCCE minimum standards identify Early Childhood Care and Primary Education as a specialised NCE pathway for early-years and primary teachers.
Federal education sources publish national minimum standards for ECCDE centres.
source_summaries.limitations: Education standards support institution and educator foundations; they do not establish one universal private childcare credential for every nanny, caregiver or family setting.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian clinical psychology professional context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian clinical psychology regulation, training, practice, supervision and mental-health delivery
findings: The Nigeria Association of Clinical Psychologists describes standardisation, practice regulation, training, continuing education and clinical-psychology services in Nigerian health and community settings; a Nigerian clinical initiative also identifies licensed clinical psychologists and supervised clinical roles.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish a Nigerian clinical-psychology role and professional pathway; they do not establish a national vacancy count or a single universal route for every psychology-adjacent role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Correctional Service probation and rehabilitation context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria non-custodial measures, probation, parole, rehabilitation, counselling and correctional support
findings: The Nigerian Correctional Service describes non-custodial measures including probation, parole, community service and restorative justice, together with rehabilitation, counselling and psychosocial support functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes official Nigerian probation and correctional-service functions; it does not establish a current vacancy, one civilian job title or a universal qualification outside the service pathway.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian psychology professional-body context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian psychology education, membership, psychosocial service and professional-development context
findings: The Nigerian Psychological Association describes psychology practice, education, research and psychosocial services in the public interest and lists Nigerian membership pathways for students, graduates, associates and full members.
source_summaries.limitations: The professional-body page establishes Nigerian psychology practice context; it is not a vacancy count and does not by itself settle every licensing or specialty requirement.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian social-work, child-care, safeguarding and psychosocial pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social work, child and family welfare, childcare, safeguarding, community development, psychosocial support, counselling and correctional or rehabilitation services
findings: NASoW identifies social work across Nigerian schools, hospitals, NGOs, ministries, rehabilitation centres, old people's homes, correctional centres and government levels; the Nigerian social-work curriculum identifies child, family, youth, mental-health, counselling, community, criminal-justice and correctional practice; NBTE lists Children's Care, Learning and Development; NCoS describes counselling, psychosocial support, rehabilitation, probation and non-custodial services.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian practice, service and training pathways; they do not establish a national vacancy count or imply that every caregiver, mentor, nanny or support worker is a regulated social worker.

source_summaries.name: OHCSF Personnel Audit and Skills Gap Analysis project
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian federal civil-service skills identification, development and gap analysis
findings: The OHCSF PASGA portal describes a project to identify and develop the skills of Nigerian public servants and build a data-driven, globally competitive civil service.
source_summaries.limitations: The portal is public-service skills context and does not establish a private-sector requirement or a single certification.

source_summaries.name: Federal Government social-work professionalisation and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice, professionalisation, standards and capacity-building context
findings: The Federal Government described work to strengthen social-work practice in Nigeria, including professionalisation and standards challenges under the Social Work Practitioners Act 2022 context.
source_summaries.limitations: The article supports Nigerian practice context but does not establish one compulsory credential for every care, counselling or social-service role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian social-work registration and professional-practice framework
TRCN safeguarding resources for Nigerian schools
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian child protection, learner safety, violence-free schools and safeguarding practice
findings: TRCN provides resources on child protection, safety, security and violence-free schools and describes protocols and standards for protecting children and learners.
source_summaries.limitations: Safeguarding resources support education and child-facing practice; they do not create one universal certificate for all social-service or childcare roles.

source_summaries.name: Bureau of Public Service Reforms National Strategy for Public Service Reform
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian civil-service administration, competency, performance, accountability and professionalisation
findings: The strategy describes a professional, results-oriented, competent, accountable and citizen-centred Nigerian public service, including merit-based recruitment, performance management, job evaluation and professionalisation of core cadres.
source_summaries.limitations: A reform strategy supplies public-service capability context, not a universal qualification for every public or private-sector role.

source_summaries.name: Chartered Institute of Administration professional qualifying course and public-administration faculty
Jobberman Nigeria jobs
MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
Nigeria Association of Social Workers role-family context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice across public services, community development, teaching hospitals, NGOs, rehabilitation, care and correctional settings
findings: NASoW identifies social workers across schools, teaching hospitals, NGOs, ministries, rehabilitation centres, old people's homes, correctional centres and local, state and federal institutions.

NASoW Lagos names public-sector social welfare officers, community development officers, medical social workers, social-work educators, independent social workers and NGO social workers among its professional community.
source_summaries.limitations: Professional-body role-family context demonstrates Nigerian practice settings; it is not a vacancy count, universal title equivalence or proof that every specialised social-care occupation is established in every Nigerian setting.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE Operational Guidelines for Sector Skills Councils
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian sector-skills governance and occupational-standard development across ICT, engineering, transport/logistics and other sectors
findings: The guidelines describe sector-skills-council structures used to coordinate occupational standards, industry participation and skills development in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: The guidelines support skills-governance context and do not establish a credential or demand signal for an individual role.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Council for Theological Studies and Christian Education and Nigerian theological training
Nigerian allied-health, radiography, rehabilitation and optometry context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian radiography, nuclear and diagnostic imaging, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, chiropractic, osteopathy, prosthetics and orthotics, optometry and allied-health education
findings: RRBN regulates radiography and related diagnostic or therapeutic radiography practice; MRTB regulates and licenses rehabilitation professions including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, prosthetics/orthotics, chiropractic and osteopathic practice; ODORBN regulates Nigerian optometrists and dispensing opticians; NUC allied-health standards identify Nigerian allied-health degree pathways and professional information practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian early-childhood care, primary education and childcare training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian early-childhood care and education, primary education, childcare settings, NCE minimum standards and learner safeguarding
findings: NCCE minimum standards identify Early Childhood Care and Primary Education as a specialised NCE pathway for early-years and primary teachers.
Federal education sources publish national minimum standards for ECCDE centres.
source_summaries.limitations: Education standards support institution and educator foundations; they do not establish one universal private childcare credential for every nanny, caregiver or family setting.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian clinical psychology professional context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian clinical psychology regulation, training, practice, supervision and mental-health delivery
findings: The Nigeria Association of Clinical Psychologists describes standardisation, practice regulation, training, continuing education and clinical-psychology services in Nigerian health and community settings; a Nigerian clinical initiative also identifies licensed clinical psychologists and supervised clinical roles.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish a Nigerian clinical-psychology role and professional pathway; they do not establish a national vacancy count or a single universal route for every psychology-adjacent role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Correctional Service probation and rehabilitation context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria non-custodial measures, probation, parole, rehabilitation, counselling and correctional support
findings: The Nigerian Correctional Service describes non-custodial measures including probation, parole, community service and restorative justice, together with rehabilitation, counselling and psychosocial support functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes official Nigerian probation and correctional-service functions; it does not establish a current vacancy, one civilian job title or a universal qualification outside the service pathway.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian psychology professional-body context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian psychology education, membership, psychosocial service and professional-development context
findings: The Nigerian Psychological Association describes psychology practice, education, research and psychosocial services in the public interest and lists Nigerian membership pathways for students, graduates, associates and full members.
source_summaries.limitations: The professional-body page establishes Nigerian psychology practice context; it is not a vacancy count and does not by itself settle every licensing or specialty requirement.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian social-work, child-care, safeguarding and psychosocial pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social work, child and family welfare, childcare, safeguarding, community development, psychosocial support, counselling and correctional or rehabilitation services
findings: NASoW identifies social work across Nigerian schools, hospitals, NGOs, ministries, rehabilitation centres, old people's homes, correctional centres and government levels; the Nigerian social-work curriculum identifies child, family, youth, mental-health, counselling, community, criminal-justice and correctional practice; NBTE lists Children's Care, Learning and Development; NCoS describes counselling, psychosocial support, rehabilitation, probation and non-custodial services.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian practice, service and training pathways; they do not establish a national vacancy count or imply that every caregiver, mentor, nanny or support worker is a regulated social worker.

source_summaries.name: OHCSF Personnel Audit and Skills Gap Analysis project
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian federal civil-service skills identification, development and gap analysis
findings: The OHCSF PASGA portal describes a project to identify and develop the skills of Nigerian public servants and build a data-driven, globally competitive civil service.
source_summaries.limitations: The portal is public-service skills context and does not establish a private-sector requirement or a single certification.

source_summaries.name: Federal Government social-work professionalisation and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice, professionalisation, standards and capacity-building context
findings: The Federal Government described work to strengthen social-work practice in Nigeria, including professionalisation and standards challenges under the Social Work Practitioners Act 2022 context.
source_summaries.limitations: The article supports Nigerian practice context but does not establish one compulsory credential for every care, counselling or social-service role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian social-work registration and professional-practice framework
TRCN safeguarding resources for Nigerian schools
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian child protection, learner safety, violence-free schools and safeguarding practice
findings: TRCN provides resources on child protection, safety, security and violence-free schools and describes protocols and standards for protecting children and learners.
source_summaries.limitations: Safeguarding resources support education and child-facing practice; they do not create one universal certificate for all social-service or childcare roles.

findings: NASoW identifies social workers across schools, teaching hospitals, NGOs, ministries, rehabilitation centres, old people's homes, correctional centres and local, state and federal institutions.

NASoW Lagos names public-sector social welfare officers, community development officers, medical social workers, social-work educators, independent social workers and NGO social workers among its professional community.

Nigerian allied-health, radiography, rehabilitation and optometry context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian radiography, nuclear and diagnostic imaging, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, chiropractic, osteopathy, prosthetics and orthotics, optometry and allied-health education
findings: RRBN regulates radiography and related diagnostic or therapeutic radiography practice; MRTB regulates and licenses rehabilitation professions including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, prosthetics/orthotics, chiropractic and osteopathic practice; ODORBN regulates Nigerian optometrists and dispensing opticians; NUC allied-health standards identify Nigerian allied-health degree pathways and professional information practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian early-childhood care and education, primary education, childcare settings, NCE minimum standards and learner safeguarding
findings: NCCE minimum standards identify Early Childhood Care and Primary Education as a specialised NCE pathway for early-years and primary teachers.
Federal education sources publish national minimum standards for ECCDE centres.
source_summaries.limitations: Education standards support institution and educator foundations; they do not establish one universal private childcare credential for every nanny, caregiver or family setting.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian clinical psychology professional context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian clinical psychology regulation, training, practice, supervision and mental-health delivery
findings: The Nigeria Association of Clinical Psychologists describes standardisation, practice regulation, training, continuing education and clinical-psychology services in Nigerian health and community settings; a Nigerian clinical initiative also identifies licensed clinical psychologists and supervised clinical roles.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish a Nigerian clinical-psychology role and professional pathway; they do not establish a national vacancy count or a single universal route for every psychology-adjacent role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Correctional Service probation and rehabilitation context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria non-custodial measures, probation, parole, rehabilitation, counselling and correctional support
findings: The Nigerian Correctional Service describes non-custodial measures including probation, parole, community service and restorative justice, together with rehabilitation, counselling and psychosocial support functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes official Nigerian probation and correctional-service functions; it does not establish a current vacancy, one civilian job title or a universal qualification outside the service pathway.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian psychology professional-body context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian psychology education, membership, psychosocial service and professional-development context
findings: The Nigerian Psychological Association describes psychology practice, education, research and psychosocial services in the public interest and lists Nigerian membership pathways for students, graduates, associates and full members.
source_summaries.limitations: The professional-body page establishes Nigerian psychology practice context; it is not a vacancy count and does not by itself settle every licensing or specialty requirement.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian social-work, child-care, safeguarding and psychosocial pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social work, child and family welfare, childcare, safeguarding, community development, psychosocial support, counselling and correctional or rehabilitation services
findings: NASoW identifies social work across Nigerian schools, hospitals, NGOs, ministries, rehabilitation centres, old people's homes, correctional centres and government levels; the Nigerian social-work curriculum identifies child, family, youth, mental-health, counselling, community, criminal-justice and correctional practice; NBTE lists Children's Care, Learning and Development; NCoS describes counselling, psychosocial support, rehabilitation, probation and non-custodial services.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian practice, service and training pathways; they do not establish a national vacancy count or imply that every caregiver, mentor, nanny or support worker is a regulated social worker.

source_summaries.name: OHCSF Personnel Audit and Skills Gap Analysis project
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian federal civil-service skills identification, development and gap analysis
findings: The OHCSF PASGA portal describes a project to identify and develop the skills of Nigerian public servants and build a data-driven, globally competitive civil service.
source_summaries.limitations: The portal is public-service skills context and does not establish a private-sector requirement or a single certification.

source_summaries.name: Federal Government social-work professionalisation and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice, professionalisation, standards and capacity-building context
findings: The Federal Government described work to strengthen social-work practice in Nigeria, including professionalisation and standards challenges under the Social Work Practitioners Act 2022 context.
source_summaries.limitations: The article supports Nigerian practice context but does not establish one compulsory credential for every care, counselling or social-service role.

source_summaries.limitations: Safeguarding resources support education and child-facing practice; they do not create one universal certificate for all social-service or childcare roles.

findings: NASoW identifies social workers across schools, teaching hospitals, NGOs, ministries, rehabilitation centres, old people's homes, correctional centres and local, state and federal institutions.

NASoW Lagos names public-sector social welfare officers, community development officers, medical social workers, social-work educators, independent social workers and NGO social workers among its professional community.

Nigerian allied-health, radiography, rehabilitation and optometry context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian radiography, nuclear and diagnostic imaging, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, chiropractic, osteopathy, prosthetics and orthotics, optometry and allied-health education
findings: RRBN regulates radiography and related diagnostic or therapeutic radiography practice; MRTB regulates and licenses rehabilitation professions including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, prosthetics/orthotics, chiropractic and osteopathic practice; ODORBN regulates Nigerian optometrists and dispensing opticians; NUC allied-health standards identify Nigerian allied-health degree pathways and professional information practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian early-childhood care and education, primary education, childcare settings, NCE minimum standards and learner safeguarding
findings: NCCE minimum standards identify Early Childhood Care and Primary Education as a specialised NCE pathway for early-years and primary teachers.
Federal education sources publish national minimum standards for ECCDE centres.
source_summaries.limitations: Education standards support institution and educator foundations; they do not establish one universal private childcare credential for every nanny, caregiver or family setting.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian clinical psychology professional context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian clinical psychology regulation, training, practice, supervision and mental-health delivery
findings: The Nigeria Association of Clinical Psychologists describes standardisation, practice regulation, training, continuing education and clinical-psychology services in Nigerian health and community settings; a Nigerian clinical initiative also identifies licensed clinical psychologists and supervised clinical roles.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish a Nigerian clinical-psychology role and professional pathway; they do not establish a national vacancy count or a single universal route for every psychology-adjacent role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Correctional Service probation and rehabilitation context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria non-custodial measures, probation, parole, rehabilitation, counselling and correctional support
findings: The Nigerian Correctional Service describes non-custodial measures including probation, parole, community service and restorative justice, together with rehabilitation, counselling and psychosocial support functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes official Nigerian probation and correctional-service functions; it does not establish a current vacancy, one civilian job title or a universal qualification outside the service pathway.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian psychology professional-body context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian psychology education, membership, psychosocial service and professional-development context
findings: The Nigerian Psychological Association describes psychology practice, education, research and psychosocial services in the public interest and lists Nigerian membership pathways for students, graduates, associates and full members.
source_summaries.limitations: The professional-body page establishes Nigerian psychology practice context; it is not a vacancy count and does not by itself settle every licensing or specialty requirement.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian social-work, child-care, safeguarding and psychosocial pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social work, child and family welfare, childcare, safeguarding, community development, psychosocial support, counselling and correctional or rehabilitation services
findings: NASoW identifies social work across Nigerian schools, hospitals, NGOs, ministries, rehabilitation centres, old people's homes, correctional centres and government levels; the Nigerian social-work curriculum identifies child, family, youth, mental-health, counselling, community, criminal-justice and correctional practice; NBTE lists Children's Care, Learning and Development; NCoS describes counselling, psychosocial support, rehabilitation, probation and non-custodial services.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian practice, service and training pathways; they do not establish a national vacancy count or imply that every caregiver, mentor, nanny or support worker is a regulated social worker.

source_summaries.name: OHCSF Personnel Audit and Skills Gap Analysis project
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian federal civil-service skills identification, development and gap analysis
findings: The OHCSF PASGA portal describes a project to identify and develop the skills of Nigerian public servants and build a data-driven, globally competitive civil service.
source_summaries.limitations: The portal is public-service skills context and does not establish a private-sector requirement or a single certification.

source_summaries.name: Federal Government social-work professionalisation and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice, professionalisation, standards and capacity-building context
findings: The Federal Government described work to strengthen social-work practice in Nigeria, including professionalisation and standards challenges under the Social Work Practitioners Act 2022 context.
source_summaries.limitations: The article supports Nigerian practice context but does not establish one compulsory credential for every care, counselling or social-service role.

findings: TRCN provides resources on child protection, safety, security and violence-free schools and describes protocols and standards for protecting children and learners.
source_summaries.limitations: Safeguarding resources support education and child-facing practice; they do not create one universal certificate for all social-service or childcare roles.

findings: The Nigerian Correctional Service describes non-custodial measures including probation, parole, community service and restorative justice, together with rehabilitation, counselling and psychosocial support functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes official Nigerian probation and correctional-service functions; it does not establish a current vacancy, one civilian job title or a universal qualification outside the service pathway.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Immigration Service mandate, travel-document operations and enlistment requirements
Nigeria Immigration Service operational and service context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian immigration, border-management, passport, visa and residence-permit functions
findings: The Nigeria Immigration Service identifies border-management, passport, visa, ECOWAS travel and residence-permit services, while the Ministry of Interior describes immigration and expatriate-work-permit administration as part of the national service environment.
source_summaries.limitations: Official service functions establish the Nigerian role family and institutional context; they do not establish a current vacancy, rank-equivalence or universal qualification for every immigration or passport role.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria Police Academy and Police training and development framework
Nigeria Police Service Commission recruitment and inspector context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian police recruitment, inspector and specialist appointment, detective training and law-enforcement work
findings: The Police Service Commission identifies recruitment of constables, appointment of cadet ASPs and Inspectors and specialist appointments; Nigeria Police Academy materials describe cadet Inspector training including police duties, law, detective courses and practical attachment.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes an official Nigerian policing pathway and training context, not a current vacancy for every police rank or a claim that civilian criminal-investigator titles map directly to a police appointment.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria private-guard company licensing and security-sector reform sources
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian private-guard-company registration/licensing, training and security-company operational requirements
findings: NSCDC describes private guard company licensing, supervision and monitoring; the Federal Government reported a 2024 reform and categorisation process for private-security-company licences and training.
source_summaries.limitations: Company licensing is not the same as a universal personal security-guard licence; role and company requirements must be kept separate.

source_summaries.name: Bureau of Public Service Reforms National Strategy for Public Service Reform
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian civil-service administration, competency, performance, accountability and professionalisation
findings: The strategy describes a professional, results-oriented, competent, accountable and citizen-centred Nigerian public service, including merit-based recruitment, performance management, job evaluation and professionalisation of core cadres.
source_summaries.limitations: A reform strategy supplies public-service capability context, not a universal qualification for every public or private-sector role.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian cosmetology, beauty therapy, personal care, salon practice, hygiene, client service and vocational training
findings: NBTE lists Cosmetology and Beauty Therapy NOS/NSQ levels and current vocational pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: The occupational standard supports training context; it is not a universal licence or proof that every personal-service worker follows the same route.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: National Electronic Labour Exchange Nigerian customer-service and administrative vacancy
Nigerian real-estate, valuation, property-management and land-practice context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian estate surveying and valuation, property management, development, land and property agency, housing and real-estate practice
findings: ESVARBON regulates estate surveying and valuation practice in Nigeria and maintains practitioner registration and professional requirements.
NIESV describes valuation, property management, property development and land-related services as parts of the Nigerian profession.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes professional and regulatory context; it does not establish a vacancy count or a licence requirement for every property, housing or agency title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian security, fire, border and correctional-service context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fire prevention and rescue, emergency response, border security, immigration control, policing, correctional custody, probation, rehabilitation and public safety
findings: The Federal Fire Service describes fire prevention, mitigation, rescue, life and property protection, training and emergency response; NIS describes border control, surveillance, immigration compliance, airport, seaport, intelligence and cybersecurity functions; NCoS describes secure and humane custody, risk and needs assessment, rehabilitation, probation, parole and non-custodial measures; PSC/NPF materials establish Nigerian police recruitment and service context.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources support the named public-service families and functions; they do not establish a counterpart, private-security licence or vacancy count for every global guard, transport, animal, gaming or specialist rescue title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian social-work, child-care and community-support context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social work, child protection, community development, welfare and early-childhood support
findings: Nigerian social-work education and public-sector sources describe community, welfare, child-care and support work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian social and child-care context; exact professional requirements depend on role, agency and client group.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Correctional Service probation and rehabilitation context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria non-custodial measures, probation, parole, rehabilitation, counselling and correctional support
findings: The Nigerian Correctional Service describes non-custodial measures including probation, parole, community service and restorative justice, together with rehabilitation, counselling and psychosocial support functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes official Nigerian probation and correctional-service functions; it does not establish a current vacancy, one civilian job title or a universal qualification outside the service pathway.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian office administration, secretarial administration and office-technology professional training/certification
findings: NIPAS publishes professional certification and examination procedures for office administration and office-technology candidates.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a professional training/membership route, not a universal statutory licence for every office administrator.

source_summaries.name: OHCSF Personnel Audit and Skills Gap Analysis project
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian federal civil-service skills identification, development and gap analysis
findings: The OHCSF PASGA portal describes a project to identify and develop the skills of Nigerian public servants and build a data-driven, globally competitive civil service.
source_summaries.limitations: The portal is public-service skills context and does not establish a private-sector requirement or a single certification.

source_summaries.name: SMEDAN Nigerian founder, MSME, entrepreneurship and business-development training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian MSME capacity building, entrepreneurship training, business development, access to finance, market support and founder development
findings: SMEDAN describes entrepreneurship training, capacity building, finance, markets and founder support for Nigerian nano, micro and small enterprises.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports entrepreneurial and business-development foundations; it does not establish a universal founder credential, company-registration outcome or demand ranking for every management role.

source_summaries.name: Federal Government social-work professionalisation and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice, professionalisation, standards and capacity-building context
findings: The Federal Government described work to strengthen social-work practice in Nigeria, including professionalisation and standards challenges under the Social Work Practitioners Act 2022 context.
source_summaries.limitations: The article supports Nigerian practice context but does not establish one compulsory credential for every care, counselling or social-service role.

Standards Organisation of Nigeria management-system and food-safety training
TRCN safeguarding resources for Nigerian schools
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian child protection, learner safety, violence-free schools and safeguarding practice
findings: TRCN provides resources on child protection, safety, security and violence-free schools and describes protocols and standards for protecting children and learners.
source_summaries.limitations: Safeguarding resources support education and child-facing practice; they do not create one universal certificate for all social-service or childcare roles.

source_summaries.name: Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria teacher standards and PQE
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian teacher education, accreditation, registration, professional qualifying examination and competency assessment
findings: TRCN describes its responsibility for teacher-education standards, programme accreditation, qualification approval, professional registration and competency assessment; its 2026 updates include PQE results and school-accreditation policy implementation.
source_summaries.limitations: TRCN applies to teaching practice within its mandate, not to every education, training, research or childcare role.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fire prevention and rescue, emergency response, border security, immigration control, policing, correctional custody, probation, rehabilitation and public safety

source_summaries.limitations: These sources support the named public-service families and functions; they do not establish a counterpart, private-security licence or vacancy count for every global guard, transport, animal, gaming or specialist rescue title.

source_summaries.limitations: This supports entrepreneurial and business-development foundations; it does not establish a universal founder credential, company-registration outcome or demand ranking for every management role.

source_summaries.name: Federal Government social-work professionalisation and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice, professionalisation, standards and capacity-building context
findings: The Federal Government described work to strengthen social-work practice in Nigeria, including professionalisation and standards challenges under the Social Work Practitioners Act 2022 context.
source_summaries.limitations: The article supports Nigerian practice context but does not establish one compulsory credential for every care, counselling or social-service role.

source_summaries.limitations: Safeguarding resources support education and child-facing practice; they do not create one universal certificate for all social-service or childcare roles.

source_summaries.name: Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria teacher standards and PQE
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian teacher education, accreditation, registration, professional qualifying examination and competency assessment

source_summaries.limitations: TRCN applies to teaching practice within its mandate, not to every education, training, research or childcare role.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian estate surveying and valuation, property management, development, land and property agency, housing and real-estate practice
findings: ESVARBON regulates estate surveying and valuation practice in Nigeria and maintains practitioner registration and professional requirements.
NIESV describes valuation, property management, property development and land-related services as parts of the Nigerian profession.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes professional and regulatory context; it does not establish a vacancy count or a licence requirement for every property, housing or agency title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian security, fire, border and correctional-service context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fire prevention and rescue, emergency response, border security, immigration control, policing, correctional custody, probation, rehabilitation and public safety
findings: The Federal Fire Service describes fire prevention, mitigation, rescue, life and property protection, training and emergency response; NIS describes border control, surveillance, immigration compliance, airport, seaport, intelligence and cybersecurity functions; NCoS describes secure and humane custody, risk and needs assessment, rehabilitation, probation, parole and non-custodial measures; PSC/NPF materials establish Nigerian police recruitment and service context.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources support the named public-service families and functions; they do not establish a counterpart, private-security licence or vacancy count for every global guard, transport, animal, gaming or specialist rescue title.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian social and child-care context; exact professional requirements depend on role, agency and client group.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian estate surveying and valuation, property management, development, land and property agency, housing and real-estate practice
findings: ESVARBON regulates estate surveying and valuation practice in Nigeria and maintains practitioner registration and professional requirements.
NIESV describes valuation, property management, property development and land-related services as parts of the Nigerian profession.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes professional and regulatory context; it does not establish a vacancy count or a licence requirement for every property, housing or agency title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian security, fire, border and correctional-service context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fire prevention and rescue, emergency response, border security, immigration control, policing, correctional custody, probation, rehabilitation and public safety
findings: The Federal Fire Service describes fire prevention, mitigation, rescue, life and property protection, training and emergency response; NIS describes border control, surveillance, immigration compliance, airport, seaport, intelligence and cybersecurity functions; NCoS describes secure and humane custody, risk and needs assessment, rehabilitation, probation, parole and non-custodial measures; PSC/NPF materials establish Nigerian police recruitment and service context.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources support the named public-service families and functions; they do not establish a counterpart, private-security licence or vacancy count for every global guard, transport, animal, gaming or specialist rescue title.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian social and child-care context; exact professional requirements depend on role, agency and client group.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Correctional Service probation and rehabilitation context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria non-custodial measures, probation, parole, rehabilitation, counselling and correctional support

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes official Nigerian probation and correctional-service functions; it does not establish a current vacancy, one civilian job title or a universal qualification outside the service pathway.

Nigerian digital-forensics and cybercrime-investigation context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian digital evidence acquisition, forensic analysis, cybercrime investigation, incident understanding and law-enforcement support
findings: Nigeria's National Digital Forensic Laboratory describes forensic acquisition, preservation and analysis of digital evidence as a national cybersecurity capability.
The Nigeria Police Force National Cybercrime Centre provides authorised officers with digital-forensics and cybercrime-investigation protocols and legal-framework resources.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian institutional and occupational context; they do not establish a universal private-sector title, vacancy count or one certificate for every forensic or investigation role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian digital technology, software, AI, cybersecurity and data-protection context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian software, web, data, artificial intelligence, networking, cybersecurity, digital services, information systems, privacy and compliance work
findings: NITDA identifies digital skills, software and hardware development, cybersecurity, digital trust, research and an agile technology workforce as Nigerian strategic priorities.
NBTE lists Nigerian programmes and national occupational standards spanning software, web, data, AI, networking, robotics, computer hardware, cybersecurity and digital service operations.
NDPC describes data-protection compliance, information privacy, information audit, data management and information-security evidence relevant to Nigerian privacy and compliance work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technology-sector, training and regulatory context; it does not prove a specific employer requirement, salary, vacancy count or universal certificate for every ICT title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian security, fire, border and correctional-service context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fire prevention and rescue, emergency response, border security, immigration control, policing, correctional custody, probation, rehabilitation and public safety
findings: The Federal Fire Service describes fire prevention, mitigation, rescue, life and property protection, training and emergency response; NIS describes border control, surveillance, immigration compliance, airport, seaport, intelligence and cybersecurity functions; NCoS describes secure and humane custody, risk and needs assessment, rehabilitation, probation, parole and non-custodial measures; PSC/NPF materials establish Nigerian police recruitment and service context.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources support the named public-service families and functions; they do not establish a counterpart, private-security licence or vacancy count for every global guard, transport, animal, gaming or specialist rescue title.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria private-guard company licensing and security-sector reform sources
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian private-guard-company registration/licensing, training and security-company operational requirements
findings: NSCDC describes private guard company licensing, supervision and monitoring; the Federal Government reported a 2024 reform and categorisation process for private-security-company licences and training.
source_summaries.limitations: Company licensing is not the same as a universal personal security-guard licence; role and company requirements must be kept separate.
