source_summaries.scope: Nigerian construction-equipment operation, excavators, bulldozers, graders, loaders, concrete mixers, maintenance, workplace safety and road regulations
findings: NBTE National Skills Qualifications for Nigerian construction-equipment operations identify operator-helper and operator competencies, daily checks, equipment maintenance, health and safety, road and workplace regulations, and specific excavator, bulldozer, grader, loader and concrete-truck-mixer operation units.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian construction-equipment training context, not a vacancy count or a local counterpart for every mining, snow, cable-vehicle, elevator or specialist crane title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian hospitality, catering, travel and tourism training and regulation context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian hotels, restaurants, catering, accommodation, front office, housekeeping, food and beverage, travel, tours, events, recreation, tourism promotion and hospitality standards
findings: The Federal Ministry describes NIHOTOUR as Nigeria's hospitality and tourism training arm with professional and technical programmes; NTDA describes national tourism development, regulation, promotion, capacity building and accreditation of hotels, restaurants, travel agencies, tour operators and related enterprises; official sector sources identify hotel, catering, recreation, tourism safety and tourism-ethics functions.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian hospitality and tourism role-family context, not a vacancy count or a universal certification for every service, food, travel or entertainment title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operations context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian railway stations, rail operations, train safety, signalling, route planning, airport operations, baggage, airspace and air-transport services, aviation fuel and road-transport administration
findings: NRC describes passenger and goods carriage, station management, train safety, control and signalling, route planning, traffic and commercial operations; NCAA regulates air transport, aviation fuel and aerodrome services; FAAN manages Nigerian commercial airports, airport operations, cargo and passenger services; NAMA describes air-traffic-management, communications, navigation and surveillance; the Federal Ministry of Transportation lists rail, road, engineering and transport-planning functions.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operation context, not a vacancy count or a counterpart for every global vehicle, pipeline, event, warehouse or specialist infrastructure title.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian sales management, customer relationship management, account management, customer experience, commercial execution, consumer information and fair marketing
findings: Nigerian sales and customer-facing professional bodies and training programmes identify sales planning, prospecting, consultative selling, negotiation, pipeline and performance management, account development, customer experience and service recovery; FCCPC identifies Nigerian consumer-information, fair-marketing, sales-record, product-safety and sales-promotion obligations; NIMN provides related marketing-professional context.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian sales and customer-facing practice context, not a vacancy count or a universal certification requirement for every sales, retail, trading, service or commercial title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian retail sales consultant vacancy with customer-experience requirements
NIHOTOUR and Nigerian Tourism Development Authority practitioner registration and accreditation
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian hospitality, travel and tourism practitioner registration/certification and enterprise accreditation
findings: NIHOTOUR describes registration, certification and verification of practitioners; NTDA describes accreditation and classification of hospitality and tourism enterprises.
source_summaries.limitations: Practitioner and enterprise routes differ; neither is a universal credential for every tourism or retail role.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian museum, archival, cultural and heritage certificate and diploma education
findings: The University of Ilorin announced 2025/2026 certificate and diploma programmes in museum and archival studies, cultural studies and creative arts.
source_summaries.limitations: An education certificate/diploma route is not a universal statutory licence or proof of demand for every heritage role.

source_summaries.name: WIPO Nigeria and Music Business Academy professional training
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian music and entertainment business training, intellectual property and employability capacity building
findings: WIPO Nigeria described a 2024/2025 Music Business Academy scholarship and a nine-month vocational programme for African music-industry professionals.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports a sector training route, not a universal music-production certification or licence.

findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.

findings: C-LMIS/CORBON identifies construction as a major Nigerian employer and publishes National Occupational Standards for building trades including electrical installation, carpentry and joinery, masonry, painting and decoration, plumbing, tiling and decorative stonework; CORBON describes standards, compliance, safety, sustainability, builder registration and practice-licence verification.
source_summaries.limitations: The sources support the named building-trade and builder families; they do not establish a Nigerian counterpart for every specialist engineering, transport, energy or infrastructure role in the library.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian construction-equipment training context, not a vacancy count or a local counterpart for every mining, snow, cable-vehicle, elevator or specialist crane title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian construction, building trades and builder-standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian building construction, building trades, construction skills, safety, quality, professional standards, masonry, carpentry, joinery, painting, plumbing, electrical installation, tiling and decorative stonework
findings: C-LMIS/CORBON identifies construction as a major Nigerian employer and publishes National Occupational Standards for building trades including electrical installation, carpentry and joinery, masonry, painting and decoration, plumbing, tiling and decorative stonework; CORBON describes standards, compliance, safety, sustainability, builder registration and practice-licence verification.
source_summaries.limitations: The sources support the named building-trade and builder families; they do not establish a Nigerian counterpart for every specialist engineering, transport, energy or infrastructure role in the library.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian construction-equipment operator training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian construction-equipment operation, excavators, bulldozers, graders, loaders, concrete mixers, maintenance, workplace safety and road regulations
findings: NBTE National Skills Qualifications for Nigerian construction-equipment operations identify operator-helper and operator competencies, daily checks, equipment maintenance, health and safety, road and workplace regulations, and specific excavator, bulldozer, grader, loader and concrete-truck-mixer operation units.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian construction-equipment training context, not a vacancy count or a local counterpart for every mining, snow, cable-vehicle, elevator or specialist crane title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian hospitality, catering, travel and tourism training and regulation context

findings: The Federal Ministry describes NIHOTOUR as Nigeria's hospitality and tourism training arm with professional and technical programmes; NTDA describes national tourism development, regulation, promotion, capacity building and accreditation of hotels, restaurants, travel agencies, tour operators and related enterprises; official sector sources identify hotel, catering, recreation, tourism safety and tourism-ethics functions.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian tourism, travel, hospitality accreditation and training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian destination development, tour operations, travel consultancy, guiding, hospitality standards, tourism marketing, research, accreditation and practitioner certification
findings: NTDA describes regulation, accreditation, classification, marketing, research, capacity building and tour-operation services across Nigeria's tourism value chain.
NIHOTOUR's registration portal describes certification and verification of hospitality, travel and tourism practitioners through a national registry.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian tourism and hospitality context; it does not establish a vacancy count, one certificate for every travel title or a universal requirement across all employers and states.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.limitations: The sources support the named building-trade and builder families; they do not establish a Nigerian counterpart for every specialist engineering, transport, energy or infrastructure role in the library.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian construction-equipment training context, not a vacancy count or a local counterpart for every mining, snow, cable-vehicle, elevator or specialist crane title.

source_summaries.name: NEMSA and REAN renewable-energy safety and standards partnership
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian renewable-energy installation safety, standardisation and quality assurance
findings: NEMSA reported collaboration with the Renewable Energy Association of Nigeria to strengthen safety, standardisation and quality assurance and stated that installations should be carried out by certified professionals under national requirements.
source_summaries.limitations: The statement concerns renewable-energy installations and does not impose one certificate on every energy-adjacent role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission generation-licence requirements

source_summaries.limitations: This is a facility/operator licence context, not a personal licence for every energy worker.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian energy-sector and planning context, not a universal building-assessor licence, project-vacancy count or qualification for every hydropower, pipeline, energy or conservation title.

findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications catalogue
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian trade, technician, craft, agricultural, hospitality, ICT, automotive, construction, fashion and technical occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current catalogue names validated or current NOS/NSQ routes for masonry, electrical installation, carpentry, fashion and garment making, leather, food and beverage, automotive, agricultural equipment, interior-decoration-related craft and many other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS/NSQ route is a skills/qualification pathway; it is not automatically a separate licence to practise every trade or operate every business.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian automotive engineering, diagnostics and vehicle-manufacturing context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian vehicle manufacturing, repair, diagnostics, inspection, CNG and electric-vehicle conversion, mechanical and materials engineering
findings: NADDC supports automotive manufacturing, certified CNG conversion workshops, EV transition and automotive design tools and training.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian automotive context; the required certification and supervision depend on vehicle system, workshop and role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian automotive, vehicle mechatronics and component-development context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian automotive maintenance, vehicle mechatronics, automotive engineering, component development, vehicle production, electric or gas vehicles and automotive skills training
findings: NADDC and NBTE identify Nigerian automotive skills development, vehicle mechatronics, component and vehicle production, workshop standards, CNG and electric-vehicle pathways, engineering design, local materials and automotive training centres; the automotive mechatronics curriculum covers vehicle electrical/electronic systems, structured fault-finding, tools, safety, workshop management and environmental practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian automotive and mechatronics context, not a motorsport-specific vacancy count or a counterpart for every aerospace, racing, software or specialist precision-engineering title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian construction-equipment operator training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian construction-equipment operation, excavators, bulldozers, graders, loaders, concrete mixers, maintenance, workplace safety and road regulations
findings: NBTE National Skills Qualifications for Nigerian construction-equipment operations identify operator-helper and operator competencies, daily checks, equipment maintenance, health and safety, road and workplace regulations, and specific excavator, bulldozer, grader, loader and concrete-truck-mixer operation units.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian construction-equipment training context, not a vacancy count or a local counterpart for every mining, snow, cable-vehicle, elevator or specialist crane title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian road-driver licensing, commercial transport and road-safety context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian commercial and private driving, road transport, delivery, passenger services, dangerous goods, vehicle inspection, driver licensing and road safety
findings: The Federal Ministry of Transportation identifies road transport and mass-transit administration, driver licensing and vehicle inspection; the FRSC driver-licence service documents licensing and commercial-licence routes; FRSC materials address safe operation of articulated vehicles and dangerous-goods transport.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian road-driver and road-transport context, not a vacancy count or a universal licence category for every specialist vehicle, emergency, aviation, rail or private-driving title.

source_summaries.name: Standards Organisation of Nigeria conformity assessment, inspection and standards training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian standards development, inspection, testing, certification, market surveillance, conformity-assessment practitioners and ISO management-system training
findings: SON describes conformity-assessment practitioners including auditors, inspectors, laboratories, consultants, inspection and certification bodies and maintains an NRCAP register.
SON training services publish ISO management-system and quality-related training areas.
source_summaries.limitations: Registration or certification depends on the practitioner, organisation and activity; this does not make every compliance, inspection or quality role a SON-licensed profession.

source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications catalogue
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian trade, technician, craft, agricultural, hospitality, ICT, automotive, construction, fashion and technical occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current catalogue names validated or current NOS/NSQ routes for masonry, electrical installation, carpentry, fashion and garment making, leather, food and beverage, automotive, agricultural equipment, interior-decoration-related craft and many other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS/NSQ route is a skills/qualification pathway; it is not automatically a separate licence to practise every trade or operate every business.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian automotive engineering, diagnostics and vehicle-manufacturing context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian vehicle manufacturing, repair, diagnostics, inspection, CNG and electric-vehicle conversion, mechanical and materials engineering
findings: NADDC supports automotive manufacturing, certified CNG conversion workshops, EV transition and automotive design tools and training.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian automotive context; the required certification and supervision depend on vehicle system, workshop and role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian automotive, vehicle mechatronics and component-development context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian automotive maintenance, vehicle mechatronics, automotive engineering, component development, vehicle production, electric or gas vehicles and automotive skills training
findings: NADDC and NBTE identify Nigerian automotive skills development, vehicle mechatronics, component and vehicle production, workshop standards, CNG and electric-vehicle pathways, engineering design, local materials and automotive training centres; the automotive mechatronics curriculum covers vehicle electrical/electronic systems, structured fault-finding, tools, safety, workshop management and environmental practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian automotive and mechatronics context, not a motorsport-specific vacancy count or a counterpart for every aerospace, racing, software or specialist precision-engineering title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian construction-equipment operator training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian construction-equipment operation, excavators, bulldozers, graders, loaders, concrete mixers, maintenance, workplace safety and road regulations
findings: NBTE National Skills Qualifications for Nigerian construction-equipment operations identify operator-helper and operator competencies, daily checks, equipment maintenance, health and safety, road and workplace regulations, and specific excavator, bulldozer, grader, loader and concrete-truck-mixer operation units.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian construction-equipment training context, not a vacancy count or a local counterpart for every mining, snow, cable-vehicle, elevator or specialist crane title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian road-driver licensing, commercial transport and road-safety context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian commercial and private driving, road transport, delivery, passenger services, dangerous goods, vehicle inspection, driver licensing and road safety
findings: The Federal Ministry of Transportation identifies road transport and mass-transit administration, driver licensing and vehicle inspection; the FRSC driver-licence service documents licensing and commercial-licence routes; FRSC materials address safe operation of articulated vehicles and dangerous-goods transport.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian road-driver and road-transport context, not a vacancy count or a universal licence category for every specialist vehicle, emergency, aviation, rail or private-driving title.

source_summaries.name: Standards Organisation of Nigeria conformity assessment, inspection and standards training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian standards development, inspection, testing, certification, market surveillance, conformity-assessment practitioners and ISO management-system training
findings: SON describes conformity-assessment practitioners including auditors, inspectors, laboratories, consultants, inspection and certification bodies and maintains an NRCAP register.
SON training services publish ISO management-system and quality-related training areas.
source_summaries.limitations: Registration or certification depends on the practitioner, organisation and activity; this does not make every compliance, inspection or quality role a SON-licensed profession.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian crop production, horticulture, livestock, plant genetics, biotechnology, agricultural training, extension and production improvement

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian automotive context; the required certification and supervision depend on vehicle system, workshop and role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian automotive, vehicle mechatronics and component-development context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian automotive maintenance, vehicle mechatronics, automotive engineering, component development, vehicle production, electric or gas vehicles and automotive skills training

source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian automotive and mechatronics context, not a motorsport-specific vacancy count or a counterpart for every aerospace, racing, software or specialist precision-engineering title.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian construction-equipment training context, not a vacancy count or a local counterpart for every mining, snow, cable-vehicle, elevator or specialist crane title.

source_summaries.limitations: The official standards establish Nigerian occupational pathways and the job posting is a limited vacancy signal; neither establishes a national demand count or one universal machine, credential or employer requirement for every metalworking title.

source_summaries.name: Construction and Labour Market Information System Nigerian construction National Occupational Standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian construction trades including electrical, carpentry and joinery, masonry, painting, plumbing and tiling
findings: C-LMIS provides Nigerian construction National Occupational Standards across building trades, including electrical, carpentry and joinery, masonry, painting and decorating, plumbing and tiling.
source_summaries.limitations: The standards support construction-trade skills and pathways; they do not establish a licence for every worker or a universal requirement for construction managers and engineers.

source_summaries.name: Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria registration guidance
COREN and Nigerian Society of Engineers
Federal Government Nigerian welding, fabrication, foundry and instrumentation bootcamp
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian youth technical training in welding, fabrication, foundry, metallurgy, instrumentation, control and mechanical maintenance
findings: The Federal Government reported training 535 Nigerian youths in welding and fabrication and related metals, instrumentation, control and mechanical-maintenance areas.
source_summaries.limitations: The bootcamp is a skills-development signal and not a universal certificate or evidence that every metal-trade role is currently hiring.

source_summaries.name: Jobberman Nigeria jobs
MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
Nigeria lathe, milling, drilling and CNC operator vacancy signals
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based machining, lathe, milling, drilling and CNC manufacturing work
findings: A Nigeria-focused MyJobMag role page lists Lathe Machine Operator, Machinist (Lathe and Drill Operator), CNC Lathe Machine Operator and related machine-operation vacancies in Lagos, Ogun and other Nigerian locations.
source_summaries.limitations: The listings demonstrate Nigerian machining role-family and local vacancy signals; they do not establish one employer's universal requirements or a national demand total for every machine-operator variant.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE National Occupational Standards and curricula
Nigerian construction and building-trade occupational standards and curricula
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian masonry, painting and decoration, carpentry and joinery, construction equipment, openings, doors, windows and related building-trade training
findings: NBTE lists validated Nigerian occupational standards for masonry, painting and decoration, tiling, carpentry and joinery and construction-equipment operation; Nigerian curricula describe door and window construction, frames, materials and fixing methods; C-LMIS/CORBON publishes construction-trade standards for masonry works.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources support Nigerian occupational and training families, not a vacancy count or a claim that every named installation or supervisory title is a separate regulated occupation.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing, foundry and machining standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian welding and fabrication, blacksmithing, foundry, fitting, machining, industrial mechanics and related metal-production work
findings: NBTE's current National Occupational Standards catalogue lists Welding and Fabrication, Blacksmithing, Fitting, Machining and Blacksmithing and Foundry pathways, while Nigeria-based job signals include machinist/welder work using lathe, milling, drilling, grinding, welding and fabrication.
source_summaries.limitations: The official standards establish Nigerian occupational pathways and the job posting is a limited vacancy signal; neither establishes a national demand count or one universal machine, credential or employer requirement for every metalworking title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications list
NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria locksmith and smart-security vacancy signal
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based locksmithing, lock-and-key, access-control and smart-security service work
findings: A Lagos-based Nigerian listing identifies a Locksmithing Specialist role covering installation, repair and maintenance of locks, keys, cylinders, door-access and electronic security systems.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a single Nigerian vacancy signal; it does not establish a national demand count, universal certification or one tool stack for locksmithing and security-installation work.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing and metal-production training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing, foundry, metal forming, machining, fitting, assembly, workshop safety and technical production
findings: NBTE publishes Nigerian national curricula and occupational standards for fabrication and welding, fitting, welding and fabrication, blacksmithing and foundry, and related technical pathways; the standards include safety, statutory compliance, marking out, welding, fastening, bending, thermal cutting, sawing and abrasive cutting.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technical-training and occupational-standard context; it does not prove that every specialist metal role has a distinct local vacancy or that one certificate is universally required.

source_summaries.name: Quantity Surveyors Registration Board of Nigeria 2024 newsletter
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian quantity-surveying practice and professional registration context
findings: The QSRBN newsletter supplies Nigerian quantity-surveying professional-body context and practice material.
source_summaries.limitations: The newsletter supports professional context; specific registration gates must be shown only where the applicable rule is explicit.

source_summaries.name: Standards Organisation of Nigeria building and construction conference
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian building construction standards, structural integrity, materials, risk management and sustainable development
findings: SON reported a 2024 national conference emphasizing standards practice, structural integrity, sustainable materials and risk management in Nigeria's building and construction industry.
source_summaries.limitations: Conference and standards context does not assign one tool or credential to every construction role.

findings: NBTE curricula identify Nigerian training in automation and robotics, including relays, switches, contactors, machine programming, automated production lines, numerical control, automated assembly, PLC programming and fault diagnosis, robotics, mechatronics and human-machine interfaces.
source_summaries.limitations: The curricula establish a Nigerian technical-training pathway and competency categories, not evidence that every employer uses the same controller, software, machine or certification.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing and metal-production training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing, foundry, metal forming, machining, fitting, assembly, workshop safety and technical production
findings: NBTE publishes Nigerian national curricula and occupational standards for fabrication and welding, fitting, welding and fabrication, blacksmithing and foundry, and related technical pathways; the standards include safety, statutory compliance, marking out, welding, fastening, bending, thermal cutting, sawing and abrasive cutting.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technical-training and occupational-standard context; it does not prove that every specialist metal role has a distinct local vacancy or that one certificate is universally required.

source_summaries.name: Standards Organisation of Nigeria conformity assessment, inspection and standards training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian standards development, inspection, testing, certification, market surveillance, conformity-assessment practitioners and ISO management-system training
findings: SON describes conformity-assessment practitioners including auditors, inspectors, laboratories, consultants, inspection and certification bodies and maintains an NRCAP register.
SON training services publish ISO management-system and quality-related training areas.
source_summaries.limitations: Registration or certification depends on the practitioner, organisation and activity; this does not make every compliance, inspection or quality role a SON-licensed profession.

NAFDAC's strategy includes safety and quality of regulated products and laboratory capacity.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE National Occupational Standards and curricula
Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing, foundry and machining standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian welding and fabrication, blacksmithing, foundry, fitting, machining, industrial mechanics and related metal-production work
findings: NBTE's current National Occupational Standards catalogue lists Welding and Fabrication, Blacksmithing, Fitting, Machining and Blacksmithing and Foundry pathways, while Nigeria-based job signals include machinist/welder work using lathe, milling, drilling, grinding, welding and fabrication.
source_summaries.limitations: The official standards establish Nigerian occupational pathways and the job posting is a limited vacancy signal; neither establishes a national demand count or one universal machine, credential or employer requirement for every metalworking title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications list
NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications catalogue
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian trade, technician, craft, agricultural, hospitality, ICT, automotive, construction, fashion and technical occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current catalogue names validated or current NOS/NSQ routes for masonry, electrical installation, carpentry, fashion and garment making, leather, food and beverage, automotive, agricultural equipment, interior-decoration-related craft and many other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS/NSQ route is a skills/qualification pathway; it is not automatically a separate licence to practise every trade or operate every business.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work

source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian trade, technician, craft, agricultural, hospitality, ICT, automotive, construction, fashion and technical occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current catalogue names validated or current NOS/NSQ routes for masonry, electrical installation, carpentry, fashion and garment making, leather, food and beverage, automotive, agricultural equipment, interior-decoration-related craft and many other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS/NSQ route is a skills/qualification pathway; it is not automatically a separate licence to practise every trade or operate every business.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing and metal-production training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing, foundry, metal forming, machining, fitting, assembly, workshop safety and technical production
findings: NBTE publishes Nigerian national curricula and occupational standards for fabrication and welding, fitting, welding and fabrication, blacksmithing and foundry, and related technical pathways; the standards include safety, statutory compliance, marking out, welding, fastening, bending, thermal cutting, sawing and abrasive cutting.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technical-training and occupational-standard context; it does not prove that every specialist metal role has a distinct local vacancy or that one certificate is universally required.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian luxury, jewellery, leather and craft enterprise context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian luxury and craft enterprise including fashion, leather, jewellery, accessories, furniture and creative-product work
findings: Nigeria's fashion and creative-sector institutions identify fashion, leather and creative enterprises as an active value chain; the 2026 UNDP Nigeria and Lagos State MSME spotlight specifically covers fashion, leather and creative enterprises, while government-linked creative-economy initiatives include fashion and related cultural production.
source_summaries.limitations: This is Nigerian ecosystem and enterprise evidence, not a direct vacancy signal or proof that every jewellery, luxury, furniture or accessory title has a distinct local employer market.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technical-training and occupational-standard context; it does not prove that every specialist metal role has a distinct local vacancy or that one certificate is universally required.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications catalogue
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian trade, technician, craft, agricultural, hospitality, ICT, automotive, construction, fashion and technical occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current catalogue names validated or current NOS/NSQ routes for masonry, electrical installation, carpentry, fashion and garment making, leather, food and beverage, automotive, agricultural equipment, interior-decoration-related craft and many other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS/NSQ route is a skills/qualification pathway; it is not automatically a separate licence to practise every trade or operate every business.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian sports development, athlete support, coaching and administration context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian athlete development, coaching, sports administration, competition, facilities, sports science, support staff and national or international sports participation
findings: The Federal Ministry of Sports Development describes sports policy, monitoring, athlete training and life skills, competition participation, coach and technical-support development and performance improvement; the Nigeria Olympic Committee describes training, entering and funding Nigerian Olympic and Paralympic teams, national governing bodies, coaching education, athlete support and career services.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian sports role and institutional context, not a vacancy count, universal coaching licence or local counterpart for every sport-specific or winter/outdoor title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian sports-equipment production, quality and maintenance context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian manufacture, inspection, repair and maintenance of sports goods and related production equipment
findings: NARICT describes local sports-goods production, equipment manufacture to specification and quality inspection, while Nigerian research and industrial sources describe equipment maintenance, repair, calibration and fabrication capabilities.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports a sports-equipment technical role family, not a national vacancy count or universal trade certificate.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian chemical, rubber and plastics regulatory and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria chemical technology, rubber and rubber products, plastics, resins, industrial solvents, dangerous materials and occupational exposure controls
findings: The Standards Organisation of Nigeria lists technical committees for rubber, plastics, adhesives and resins, industrial solvents and chemicals, ceramics, glass and dangerous goods; NESREA regulations describe exposure controls, ventilation, isolation and process controls for plastics, rubber and foam manufacturing.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian industrial standards and safety context, not a vacancy count or a direct title-level demand signal for every machine-operator role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian glass and ceramics education and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian glass technology, ceramic technology, ceramic art and the SON glass and ceramics standards families
findings: NBTE's Nigerian programme catalogue includes ND and HND Glass Technology, ND Ceramic Technology and HND Art and Design (Ceramics); SON lists technical committees for ceramics and glass, laboratory glassware and related apparatus.
source_summaries.limitations: The sources establish Nigerian education and standards pathways, not one national vacancy total, universal kiln or equipment stack, or a direct market signal for each specialised production title.

Jobberman Nigeria jobs
MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE National Occupational Standards and curricula
Nigerian creative-media and performing-production standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film and media production, cinematography, lighting, sound, editing, production design, performance, special effects and stage/creative production
findings: The Nigerian NBTE Creative Media Production standard covers storytelling, cinematography, sound, production design, editing, performance, special effects, video-camera operation, lighting and casting; National Theatre materials identify stage performances, film shows, exhibitions, cultural shows, circus shows and related production facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian training and production ecosystems, not a national vacancy count or direct evidence for every highly specialised performance title; role-specific gaps remain explicit where the source does not support the title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications list
NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications catalogue
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian trade, technician, craft, agricultural, hospitality, ICT, automotive, construction, fashion and technical occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current catalogue names validated or current NOS/NSQ routes for masonry, electrical installation, carpentry, fashion and garment making, leather, food and beverage, automotive, agricultural equipment, interior-decoration-related craft and many other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS/NSQ route is a skills/qualification pathway; it is not automatically a separate licence to practise every trade or operate every business.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian carpentry, joinery, furniture and upholstery standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian carpentry, joinery, furniture making, upholstery, woodwork, finishing, installation and related craft work
findings: NBTE and C-LMIS/CORBON publish Nigerian occupational standards and curricula for carpentry and joinery, furniture making and upholstery; the furniture curriculum covers woodworking, finishing, furniture design and construction, upholstery design and construction and the associated tools and equipment.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian trade and training pathways, not a vacancy count or one universal tool, apprenticeship, certification or business model for every wood or furniture role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Fashion Council and fashion-sector skills context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fashion, garment, textile, leather, design, manufacturing, craft, innovation and fashion-value-chain work
findings: The Nigerian Fashion Council describes itself as a Federal Government-mandated Sector Skills Council inaugurated through NBTE and identifies a fashion value chain involving designers, craftsmen, manufacturers, innovators and associations; NBTE lists Nigerian pathways for garment making, Adire, embellishment, fashion/textile machine repair and leather work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes a Nigerian fashion-sector and training ecosystem; it is not a vacancy count, universal client demand ranking or single qualification requirement for every fashion or textile title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian luxury, jewellery, leather and craft enterprise context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian luxury and craft enterprise including fashion, leather, jewellery, accessories, furniture and creative-product work
findings: Nigeria's fashion and creative-sector institutions identify fashion, leather and creative enterprises as an active value chain; the 2026 UNDP Nigeria and Lagos State MSME spotlight specifically covers fashion, leather and creative enterprises, while government-linked creative-economy initiatives include fashion and related cultural production.
source_summaries.limitations: This is Nigerian ecosystem and enterprise evidence, not a direct vacancy signal or proof that every jewellery, luxury, furniture or accessory title has a distinct local employer market.

findings: The Nigerian Fashion Council describes itself as a Federal Government-mandated Sector Skills Council inaugurated through NBTE and identifies a fashion value chain involving designers, craftsmen, manufacturers, innovators and associations; NBTE lists Nigerian pathways for garment making, Adire, embellishment, fashion/textile machine repair and leather work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes a Nigerian fashion-sector and training ecosystem; it is not a vacancy count, universal client demand ranking or single qualification requirement for every fashion or textile title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian luxury, jewellery, leather and craft enterprise context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian luxury and craft enterprise including fashion, leather, jewellery, accessories, furniture and creative-product work
findings: Nigeria's fashion and creative-sector institutions identify fashion, leather and creative enterprises as an active value chain; the 2026 UNDP Nigeria and Lagos State MSME spotlight specifically covers fashion, leather and creative enterprises, while government-linked creative-economy initiatives include fashion and related cultural production.
source_summaries.limitations: This is Nigerian ecosystem and enterprise evidence, not a direct vacancy signal or proof that every jewellery, luxury, furniture or accessory title has a distinct local employer market.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian MSME capacity building, entrepreneurship training, business development, access to finance, market support and founder development

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications catalogue
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian trade, technician, craft, agricultural, hospitality, ICT, automotive, construction, fashion and technical occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current catalogue names validated or current NOS/NSQ routes for masonry, electrical installation, carpentry, fashion and garment making, leather, food and beverage, automotive, agricultural equipment, interior-decoration-related craft and many other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS/NSQ route is a skills/qualification pathway; it is not automatically a separate licence to practise every trade or operate every business.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and Federal TVET trade pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian vocational and technical pathways including garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web, health and safety and other occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current NOS catalogue names occupational standards and levels for garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web and other trades.
The Federal TVET initiative describes accredited centres, practical skills, employment and entrepreneurship pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS or TVET pathway is evidence of a Nigerian training route, not a claim that every employer requires the listed level or that one trade credential is interchangeable with a degree or professional licence.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications catalogue
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian trade, technician, craft, agricultural, hospitality, ICT, automotive, construction, fashion and technical occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current catalogue names validated or current NOS/NSQ routes for masonry, electrical installation, carpentry, fashion and garment making, leather, food and beverage, automotive, agricultural equipment, interior-decoration-related craft and many other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS/NSQ route is a skills/qualification pathway; it is not automatically a separate licence to practise every trade or operate every business.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and Federal TVET trade pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian vocational and technical pathways including garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web, health and safety and other occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current NOS catalogue names occupational standards and levels for garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web and other trades.
The Federal TVET initiative describes accredited centres, practical skills, employment and entrepreneurship pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS or TVET pathway is evidence of a Nigerian training route, not a claim that every employer requires the listed level or that one trade credential is interchangeable with a degree or professional licence.

Nigerian chemical, rubber and plastics regulatory and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria chemical technology, rubber and rubber products, plastics, resins, industrial solvents, dangerous materials and occupational exposure controls
findings: The Standards Organisation of Nigeria lists technical committees for rubber, plastics, adhesives and resins, industrial solvents and chemicals, ceramics, glass and dangerous goods; NESREA regulations describe exposure controls, ventilation, isolation and process controls for plastics, rubber and foam manufacturing.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian industrial standards and safety context, not a vacancy count or a direct title-level demand signal for every machine-operator role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Fashion Council and fashion-sector skills context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fashion, garment, textile, leather, design, manufacturing, craft, innovation and fashion-value-chain work
findings: The Nigerian Fashion Council describes itself as a Federal Government-mandated Sector Skills Council inaugurated through NBTE and identifies a fashion value chain involving designers, craftsmen, manufacturers, innovators and associations; NBTE lists Nigerian pathways for garment making, Adire, embellishment, fashion/textile machine repair and leather work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes a Nigerian fashion-sector and training ecosystem; it is not a vacancy count, universal client demand ranking or single qualification requirement for every fashion or textile title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian luxury, jewellery, leather and craft enterprise context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian luxury and craft enterprise including fashion, leather, jewellery, accessories, furniture and creative-product work
findings: Nigeria's fashion and creative-sector institutions identify fashion, leather and creative enterprises as an active value chain; the 2026 UNDP Nigeria and Lagos State MSME spotlight specifically covers fashion, leather and creative enterprises, while government-linked creative-economy initiatives include fashion and related cultural production.
source_summaries.limitations: This is Nigerian ecosystem and enterprise evidence, not a direct vacancy signal or proof that every jewellery, luxury, furniture or accessory title has a distinct local employer market.

source_summaries.limitations: The curricula establish a Nigerian technical-training pathway and competency categories, not evidence that every employer uses the same controller, software, machine or certification.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing and metal-production training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian welding, fabrication, blacksmithing, foundry, metal forming, machining, fitting, assembly, workshop safety and technical production
findings: NBTE publishes Nigerian national curricula and occupational standards for fabrication and welding, fitting, welding and fabrication, blacksmithing and foundry, and related technical pathways; the standards include safety, statutory compliance, marking out, welding, fastening, bending, thermal cutting, sawing and abrasive cutting.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technical-training and occupational-standard context; it does not prove that every specialist metal role has a distinct local vacancy or that one certificate is universally required.

NBTE curriculum material covers foundry development in Nigeria, casting, alloys, molten-metal behaviour and foundry production fundamentals.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technical-training and industry context; it does not establish a vacancy count, one universal plant process or a professional licence for every operator, technician, artisan or manager title.

source_summaries.name: Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria registration guidance
COREN 2026 engineering regulation and public-safety reforms
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian engineering practice, registration, public safety, project monitoring and anti-quackery context
findings: COREN's 2026 reforms emphasise qualified and registered practitioners, public safety, project monitoring and enforcement against unqualified engineering practice.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports regulated-engineering context; it is not a personal registration requirement for every technician or non-engineering role in an engineering organisation.

source_summaries.name: COREN and Nigerian Society of Engineers
Federal Government Nigerian welding, fabrication, foundry and instrumentation bootcamp
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian youth technical training in welding, fabrication, foundry, metallurgy, instrumentation, control and mechanical maintenance
findings: The Federal Government reported training 535 Nigerian youths in welding and fabrication and related metals, instrumentation, control and mechanical-maintenance areas.
source_summaries.limitations: The bootcamp is a skills-development signal and not a universal certificate or evidence that every metal-trade role is currently hiring.

source_summaries.name: HotNigerianJobs metallurgical and materials engineering vacancy snapshot
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian metallurgical, materials, steel and welding-related vacancies
findings: The Nigerian discipline page listed metallurgical and materials engineering vacancies, including steel melt-shop and mechanical/metallurgical engineering roles, with welding and fabrication qualifications appearing in requirements.
source_summaries.limitations: Job listings are time-bound and title conventions vary; this is an observed market signal, not a national demand estimate or universal qualification requirement.

source_summaries.name: Jobberman Nigeria jobs
MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
NAFDAC production-inspection guidance for chemical manufacturing facilities
Nigerian Association of Metallurgical and Materials Engineers role-context publication
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian metallurgical and materials engineering role families
findings: The publication identifies Nigerian role families including metallurgical engineer, foundry technician and welding/inspection engineer across steel, aluminium, copper, foundry and upstream or midstream settings.
source_summaries.limitations: Professional role context does not establish current vacancy volume or that every role requires professional registration.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE National Occupational Standards and curricula
NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE occupational and technical-education standards for textile, wood, manufacturing and assembly
Nigerian industrial automation, robotics and mechatronics training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian industrial automation, programmable logic controllers, robotics, mechatronics, automated production, assembly, instrumentation and manufacturing technology
findings: NBTE curricula identify Nigerian training in automation and robotics, including relays, switches, contactors, machine programming, automated production lines, numerical control, automated assembly, PLC programming and fault diagnosis, robotics, mechatronics and human-machine interfaces.
source_summaries.limitations: The curricula establish a Nigerian technical-training pathway and competency categories, not evidence that every employer uses the same controller, software, machine or certification.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian chemical, rubber and plastics regulatory and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria chemical technology, rubber and rubber products, plastics, resins, industrial solvents, dangerous materials and occupational exposure controls
findings: The Standards Organisation of Nigeria lists technical committees for rubber, plastics, adhesives and resins, industrial solvents and chemicals, ceramics, glass and dangerous goods; NESREA regulations describe exposure controls, ventilation, isolation and process controls for plastics, rubber and foam manufacturing.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian industrial standards and safety context, not a vacancy count or a direct title-level demand signal for every machine-operator role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian environmental science, biodiversity, water-quality and environmental-health context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian environmental science, environmental health, biodiversity conservation, water and air quality, pollution control, environmental audit, natural resources and sustainability
findings: NESREA describes Nigerian environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, water-quality and pollution standards, environmental audits, environmental data, ecosystem conservation and research; EHCON regulates and licenses environmental-health specialists, officers, technicians and assistants; the Federal Ministry of Environment identifies chemical, waste, sewage, air-emissions and environmental-health functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian environmental and environmental-health practice context; it is not a national vacancy count and environmental-health registration should not be applied to every environmental scientist or ecologist.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority radiation-safety training for mining
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian solid-mineral mining and processing radiation-safety roles and adjacent technical occupations
findings: NNRA announced a 2026 national course for current or prospective Radiation Safety Officers in mining and mineral processing, covering NORM/TE-NORM, monitoring, dose assessment, radiation protection, handling, transport, waste management and regulatory compliance.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a specialised radiation-safety pathway and does not apply to every mining or geology role.

source_summaries.name: Standards Organisation of Nigeria food and agriculture technical committees
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian food, agriculture, animal-feed and veterinary-drug-residue standardisation
findings: SON lists technical committees covering animal feeds and veterinary-drug residues and antimicrobial resistance in food among Nigerian food and agriculture standards work.
source_summaries.limitations: Technical-committee scope supports standards context; it is not by itself an individual certification or demand signal.

findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

NBTE National Occupational Standards and Federal TVET trade pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian vocational and technical pathways including garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web, health and safety and other occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current NOS catalogue names occupational standards and levels for garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web and other trades.
The Federal TVET initiative describes accredited centres, practical skills, employment and entrepreneurship pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS or TVET pathway is evidence of a Nigerian training route, not a claim that every employer requires the listed level or that one trade credential is interchangeable with a degree or professional licence.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian chemical, rubber and plastics regulatory and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria chemical technology, rubber and rubber products, plastics, resins, industrial solvents, dangerous materials and occupational exposure controls
findings: The Standards Organisation of Nigeria lists technical committees for rubber, plastics, adhesives and resins, industrial solvents and chemicals, ceramics, glass and dangerous goods; NESREA regulations describe exposure controls, ventilation, isolation and process controls for plastics, rubber and foam manufacturing.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian industrial standards and safety context, not a vacancy count or a direct title-level demand signal for every machine-operator role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Fashion Council and fashion-sector skills context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fashion, garment, textile, leather, design, manufacturing, craft, innovation and fashion-value-chain work
findings: The Nigerian Fashion Council describes itself as a Federal Government-mandated Sector Skills Council inaugurated through NBTE and identifies a fashion value chain involving designers, craftsmen, manufacturers, innovators and associations; NBTE lists Nigerian pathways for garment making, Adire, embellishment, fashion/textile machine repair and leather work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes a Nigerian fashion-sector and training ecosystem; it is not a vacancy count, universal client demand ranking or single qualification requirement for every fashion or textile title.

findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: NBTE occupational and technical-education standards for textile, wood, manufacturing and assembly
NBTE National Occupational Standards and Federal TVET trade pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian vocational and technical pathways including garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web, health and safety and other occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current NOS catalogue names occupational standards and levels for garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web and other trades.
The Federal TVET initiative describes accredited centres, practical skills, employment and entrepreneurship pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS or TVET pathway is evidence of a Nigerian training route, not a claim that every employer requires the listed level or that one trade credential is interchangeable with a degree or professional licence.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian chemical, rubber and plastics regulatory and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria chemical technology, rubber and rubber products, plastics, resins, industrial solvents, dangerous materials and occupational exposure controls
findings: The Standards Organisation of Nigeria lists technical committees for rubber, plastics, adhesives and resins, industrial solvents and chemicals, ceramics, glass and dangerous goods; NESREA regulations describe exposure controls, ventilation, isolation and process controls for plastics, rubber and foam manufacturing.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian industrial standards and safety context, not a vacancy count or a direct title-level demand signal for every machine-operator role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Fashion Council and fashion-sector skills context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian fashion, garment, textile, leather, design, manufacturing, craft, innovation and fashion-value-chain work
findings: The Nigerian Fashion Council describes itself as a Federal Government-mandated Sector Skills Council inaugurated through NBTE and identifies a fashion value chain involving designers, craftsmen, manufacturers, innovators and associations; NBTE lists Nigerian pathways for garment making, Adire, embellishment, fashion/textile machine repair and leather work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes a Nigerian fashion-sector and training ecosystem; it is not a vacancy count, universal client demand ranking or single qualification requirement for every fashion or textile title.

source_summaries.limitations: The sources support the named building-trade and builder families; they do not establish a Nigerian counterpart for every specialist engineering, transport, energy or infrastructure role in the library.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian construction-equipment training context, not a vacancy count or a local counterpart for every mining, snow, cable-vehicle, elevator or specialist crane title.

source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian hospitality and tourism role-family context, not a vacancy count or a universal certification for every service, food, travel or entertainment title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority personnel licensing and aviation regulation
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian pilots, aircraft maintenance engineers, dispatchers, air traffic controllers, cabin crew and aeronautical personnel
findings: NCAA is Nigeria's civil-aviation regulator and identifies licensing, certification, inspection, monitoring and enforcement functions.
The personnel licensing framework covers pilots, aircraft maintenance engineers, flight dispatchers, air traffic controllers and related aviation personnel.
source_summaries.limitations: Licensing requirements are role- and operation-specific; the presence of a licence pathway does not mean every aeronautical or airport role requires the same licence.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian College of Aviation Technology training programmes
