source_summaries.limitations: Training availability does not by itself grant a licence or establish a vacancy.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian inland-waterway transport, marine safety and operations context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian inland-waterway navigation, vessel operations, cargo handling, warehousing, ferry services, pilotage, safety inspection, traffic management, maritime security and intermodal transport
findings: NIWA describes statutory Nigerian responsibility for inland-waterway development and regulation, vessel operations, ferry services, cargo handling, storage, stevedoring, pilotage, vessel traffic management, safety inspections, search and rescue and maritime security; it also describes training for boat operators and skippers.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian inland-waterway role and operational context; it does not establish a counterpart for every air, rail, pipeline or ocean-shipping title, or one universal licence for every waterway role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operations context

findings: NRC describes passenger and goods carriage, station management, train safety, control and signalling, route planning, traffic and commercial operations; NCAA regulates air transport, aviation fuel and aerodrome services; FAAN manages Nigerian commercial airports, airport operations, cargo and passenger services; NAMA describes air-traffic-management, communications, navigation and surveillance; the Federal Ministry of Transportation lists rail, road, engineering and transport-planning functions.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operation context, not a vacancy count or a counterpart for every global vehicle, pipeline, event, warehouse or specialist infrastructure title.

Government education and TVET sources describe technical-teacher training, accredited centres and practical instruction pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: The sources support education-workforce and instructor foundations; they do not establish a universal licence or exact hiring requirement for every teaching, training or coaching title.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian seafarer education, assessment, certification, revalidation, endorsement and medical fitness

source_summaries.limitations: These standards apply to seafarer roles and do not apply to every maritime, port, logistics or naval-architecture occupation.

source_summaries.limitations: A training course listing supports a Nigerian pathway and named capability areas; it does not establish a universal personal licence or current vacancy count.

findings: NCAA is Nigeria's civil-aviation regulator and identifies licensing, certification, inspection, monitoring and enforcement functions.
The personnel licensing framework covers pilots, aircraft maintenance engineers, flight dispatchers, air traffic controllers and related aviation personnel.
source_summaries.limitations: Licensing requirements are role- and operation-specific; the presence of a licence pathway does not mean every aeronautical or airport role requires the same licence.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian College of Aviation Technology training programmes
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian pilot, air-traffic, aircraft-maintenance, aviation-management and aeronautical-technical training
findings: NCAT lists aircraft-maintenance engineering, aviation management and air-traffic services/communications training and is identified as a national aviation specialist-training institution.
source_summaries.limitations: Training availability does not by itself grant a licence or establish a vacancy.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian inland-waterway transport, marine safety and operations context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian inland-waterway navigation, vessel operations, cargo handling, warehousing, ferry services, pilotage, safety inspection, traffic management, maritime security and intermodal transport
findings: NIWA describes statutory Nigerian responsibility for inland-waterway development and regulation, vessel operations, ferry services, cargo handling, storage, stevedoring, pilotage, vessel traffic management, safety inspections, search and rescue and maritime security; it also describes training for boat operators and skippers.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian inland-waterway role and operational context; it does not establish a counterpart for every air, rail, pipeline or ocean-shipping title, or one universal licence for every waterway role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operations context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian railway stations, rail operations, train safety, signalling, route planning, airport operations, baggage, airspace and air-transport services, aviation fuel and road-transport administration
findings: NRC describes passenger and goods carriage, station management, train safety, control and signalling, route planning, traffic and commercial operations; NCAA regulates air transport, aviation fuel and aerodrome services; FAAN manages Nigerian commercial airports, airport operations, cargo and passenger services; NAMA describes air-traffic-management, communications, navigation and surveillance; the Federal Ministry of Transportation lists rail, road, engineering and transport-planning functions.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operation context, not a vacancy count or a counterpart for every global vehicle, pipeline, event, warehouse or specialist infrastructure title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian teacher, technical-instructor and digital-learning training pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian teacher professional development, digital literacy, classroom practice, technical teacher training and education technology implementation
findings: The Federal Ministry of Education's teacher platform describes structured teaching-methodology and digital-literacy modules.
Government education and TVET sources describe technical-teacher training, accredited centres and practical instruction pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: The sources support education-workforce and instructor foundations; they do not establish a universal licence or exact hiring requirement for every teaching, training or coaching title.

source_summaries.name: NIMASA seafarer education, training, certification and medical-fitness standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian seafarer education, assessment, certification, revalidation, endorsement and medical fitness
findings: NIMASA reported revised standards under Nigeria's 2025 STCW regulations, including education, training, assessment, examination, certification, revalidation, endorsement and medical-fitness requirements, with bridging courses for specified ND/HND holders.
source_summaries.limitations: These standards apply to seafarer roles and do not apply to every maritime, port, logistics or naval-architecture occupation.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Transport Technology 2026 railway training programme
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian railway communication, signalling, networks, control, cargo, governance, safety, track maintenance, infrastructure and rail administration
findings: NITT lists 2026 railway courses covering communication and signalling, ITS, cargo operations, governance, occupational safety, track-quality monitoring, infrastructure and facility management.
source_summaries.limitations: A training course listing supports a Nigerian pathway and named capability areas; it does not establish a universal personal licence or current vacancy count.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Railway Corporation railway technology transfer and manpower pathway
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian railway technology transfer, locomotive engineering, rail management and digital rail technology
findings: NRC describes a 2025 partnership with tertiary institutions to build a skilled manpower pipeline in locomotive engineering, rail management and digital rail technology.
source_summaries.limitations: The partnership is an ecosystem and workforce-development signal, not proof that every railway role is currently recruited or that one credential applies to all roles.

findings: NCAA is Nigeria's civil-aviation regulator and identifies licensing, certification, inspection, monitoring and enforcement functions.

source_summaries.limitations: Training availability does not by itself grant a licence or establish a vacancy.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian inland-waterway transport, marine safety and operations context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian inland-waterway navigation, vessel operations, cargo handling, warehousing, ferry services, pilotage, safety inspection, traffic management, maritime security and intermodal transport
findings: NIWA describes statutory Nigerian responsibility for inland-waterway development and regulation, vessel operations, ferry services, cargo handling, storage, stevedoring, pilotage, vessel traffic management, safety inspections, search and rescue and maritime security; it also describes training for boat operators and skippers.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian inland-waterway role and operational context; it does not establish a counterpart for every air, rail, pipeline or ocean-shipping title, or one universal licence for every waterway role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operations context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian railway stations, rail operations, train safety, signalling, route planning, airport operations, baggage, airspace and air-transport services, aviation fuel and road-transport administration
findings: NRC describes passenger and goods carriage, station management, train safety, control and signalling, route planning, traffic and commercial operations; NCAA regulates air transport, aviation fuel and aerodrome services; FAAN manages Nigerian commercial airports, airport operations, cargo and passenger services; NAMA describes air-traffic-management, communications, navigation and surveillance; the Federal Ministry of Transportation lists rail, road, engineering and transport-planning functions.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operation context, not a vacancy count or a counterpart for every global vehicle, pipeline, event, warehouse or specialist infrastructure title.

findings: NIWA describes statutory Nigerian responsibility for inland-waterway development and regulation, vessel operations, ferry services, cargo handling, storage, stevedoring, pilotage, vessel traffic management, safety inspections, search and rescue and maritime security; it also describes training for boat operators and skippers.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian inland-waterway role and operational context; it does not establish a counterpart for every air, rail, pipeline or ocean-shipping title, or one universal licence for every waterway role.

source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operation context, not a vacancy count or a counterpart for every global vehicle, pipeline, event, warehouse or specialist infrastructure title.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

findings: NIWA describes statutory Nigerian responsibility for inland-waterway development and regulation, vessel operations, ferry services, cargo handling, storage, stevedoring, pilotage, vessel traffic management, safety inspections, search and rescue and maritime security; it also describes training for boat operators and skippers.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian inland-waterway role and operational context; it does not establish a counterpart for every air, rail, pipeline or ocean-shipping title, or one universal licence for every waterway role.

source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operation context, not a vacancy count or a counterpart for every global vehicle, pipeline, event, warehouse or specialist infrastructure title.

findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operation context, not a vacancy count or a counterpart for every global vehicle, pipeline, event, warehouse or specialist infrastructure title.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian tourism and hospitality context; it does not establish a vacancy count, one certificate for every travel title or a universal requirement across all employers and states.

findings: NESREA describes Nigerian environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, water-quality and pollution standards, environmental audits, environmental data, ecosystem conservation and research; EHCON regulates and licenses environmental-health specialists, officers, technicians and assistants; the Federal Ministry of Environment identifies chemical, waste, sewage, air-emissions and environmental-health functions.

Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria registration guidance
COREN 2026 engineering regulation and public-safety reforms
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian engineering practice, registration, public safety, project monitoring and anti-quackery context
findings: COREN's 2026 reforms emphasise qualified and registered practitioners, public safety, project monitoring and enforcement against unqualified engineering practice.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports regulated-engineering context; it is not a personal registration requirement for every technician or non-engineering role in an engineering organisation.

source_summaries.name: NUC, NCCE and Nigerian education standards
Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare hospital-services policy resources
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian health-facility, laboratory quality, biosafety, patient-safety, eye-health and oxygen-care guidance
findings: The ministry lists a 2024 guideline on integration of medical laboratory services, a 2025 guideline on medical-laboratory quality management, and a 2026 guideline on laboratory biosafety and biosecurity.
The same policy resource lists patient-safety and care-quality guidance and an eye-health strategic plan for 2024-2028.
source_summaries.limitations: These are system and practice guidance documents; they do not by themselves establish an individual licence or a vacancy for every health occupation.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian health-profession regulators
Nigerian health records registration and digital health information context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian health records officers, health-information management, registration and licensure, electronic content management, digital health, EMR/EHR, data quality and confidentiality
findings: The Federal Ministry of Health describes HRORBN registration, digital compliance and health-records workforce demand, and describes ECM and national digital-health/EMR direction.
source_summaries.limitations: The regulatory requirement applies to defined health-records practice; digital-health context does not make every medical, data or administrative role a registered health-records profession.

source_summaries.name: Jobberman Nigeria jobs
MDCN and MLSCN Nigerian medical, dental and laboratory registration and training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian medical and dental education, housemanship, professional registration, annual practice licensing, medical laboratory training, laboratory registration and continuing professional development
findings: MDCN publishes medical and dental education, accreditation, registration, practising-licence and CPD services.
MLSCN publishes medical-laboratory training, registration, licensure, laboratory accreditation and CPD services, including the 2025 ND curriculum.
source_summaries.limitations: The regulations apply to defined health professions and facilities; they do not establish a universal licence for every health-support, research, technology or administrative role.

source_summaries.name: Medical Laboratory Science Council of Nigeria
Medical Laboratory Science Council of Nigeria registration, quality and laboratory guidance
source_summaries.scope: Medical laboratory practitioner registration/licensing, laboratory quality, sample management, laboratory design, IVD regulation, CPD and proficiency testing in Nigeria
findings: MLSCN materials describe practitioner registration and annual practice licensing.
The Council publishes quality, sample-management, laboratory-design, IVD and inspection guidance, and 2025 proficiency-testing guidance.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources support the medical-laboratory domain and regulated practice boundary; they do not establish one software stack for every laboratory role.

source_summaries.name: MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
NASENI Centre of Excellence in Nanotechnology and Advanced Materials
National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
Nigerian allied-health, radiography, rehabilitation and optometry context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian radiography, nuclear and diagnostic imaging, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, chiropractic, osteopathy, prosthetics and orthotics, optometry and allied-health education
findings: RRBN regulates radiography and related diagnostic or therapeutic radiography practice; MRTB regulates and licenses rehabilitation professions including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, prosthetics/orthotics, chiropractic and osteopathic practice; ODORBN regulates Nigerian optometrists and dispensing opticians; NUC allied-health standards identify Nigerian allied-health degree pathways and professional information practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian medical laboratory technology, diagnostics and laboratory quality context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian medical laboratory technology, specimen handling, histology, cytology, phlebotomy, clinical chemistry, microbiology, molecular diagnostics and laboratory quality
findings: MLSCN published a new approved National Diploma medical laboratory science curriculum and laboratory registration guidance.
NBTE curriculum material describes medical laboratory technicians as a trained workforce for accurate and reliable testing in Nigeria's health sector.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian education and regulatory context; exact registration, supervision and scope depend on the laboratory profession and current MLSCN requirements.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Professional Administrators and Office Technology and Management
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian office administration, secretarial administration and office-technology professional training/certification
findings: NIPAS publishes professional certification and examination procedures for office administration and office-technology candidates.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a professional training/membership route, not a universal statutory licence for every office administrator.

source_summaries.name: SMEDAN Nigerian founder, MSME, entrepreneurship and business-development training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian MSME capacity building, entrepreneurship training, business development, access to finance, market support and founder development
findings: SMEDAN describes entrepreneurship training, capacity building, finance, markets and founder support for Nigerian nano, micro and small enterprises.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports entrepreneurial and business-development foundations; it does not establish a universal founder credential, company-registration outcome or demand ranking for every management role.

source_summaries.name: Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria teacher standards and PQE
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian teacher education, accreditation, registration, professional qualifying examination and competency assessment
findings: TRCN describes its responsibility for teacher-education standards, programme accreditation, qualification approval, professional registration and competency assessment; its 2026 updates include PQE results and school-accreditation policy implementation.
source_summaries.limitations: TRCN applies to teaching practice within its mandate, not to every education, training, research or childcare role.

Its functions include surveillance, laboratory networks, emergency preparedness and response, applied epidemiology, research and coordination with state surveillance teams and public-health emergency operations centres.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian public-health system context and relevant work functions; it does not establish a universal licence, vacancy count or identical qualification for every health-support title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian allied-health, radiography, rehabilitation and optometry context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian radiography, nuclear and diagnostic imaging, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, chiropractic, osteopathy, prosthetics and orthotics, optometry and allied-health education
findings: RRBN regulates radiography and related diagnostic or therapeutic radiography practice; MRTB regulates and licenses rehabilitation professions including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, prosthetics/orthotics, chiropractic and osteopathic practice; ODORBN regulates Nigerian optometrists and dispensing opticians; NUC allied-health standards identify Nigerian allied-health degree pathways and professional information practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

source_summaries.name: Bureau of Public Service Reforms National Strategy for Public Service Reform
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian civil-service administration, competency, performance, accountability and professionalisation
findings: The strategy describes a professional, results-oriented, competent, accountable and citizen-centred Nigerian public service, including merit-based recruitment, performance management, job evaluation and professionalisation of core cadres.
source_summaries.limitations: A reform strategy supplies public-service capability context, not a universal qualification for every public or private-sector role.

source_summaries.name: NUC, NCCE and Nigerian education standards
Jobberman Nigeria jobs
MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
Nigeria Association of Social Workers role-family context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice across public services, community development, teaching hospitals, NGOs, rehabilitation, care and correctional settings
findings: NASoW identifies social workers across schools, teaching hospitals, NGOs, ministries, rehabilitation centres, old people's homes, correctional centres and local, state and federal institutions.

NASoW Lagos names public-sector social welfare officers, community development officers, medical social workers, social-work educators, independent social workers and NGO social workers among its professional community.
source_summaries.limitations: Professional-body role-family context demonstrates Nigerian practice settings; it is not a vacancy count, universal title equivalence or proof that every specialised social-care occupation is established in every Nigerian setting.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian agricultural research, horticulture, crop, livestock and extension context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian crop production, horticulture, livestock, plant genetics, biotechnology, agricultural training, extension and production improvement
findings: ARCN coordinates agricultural research, training and extension through national institutes and colleges across Nigeria's agro-ecological zones; its plant-resources work covers crop improvement, seed production, irrigation, pest and disease management, genetics and biotechnology; NIHORT covers fruits, vegetables, spices, ornamentals, post-harvest processing and sustainable horticultural production; NBTE lists Nigerian crop-production and livestock-production technical pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian agricultural role-family and training context, not a universal farm system, commodity, equipment stack, licence or vacancy count for every agricultural occupation.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian social-work, child-care and community-support context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social work, child protection, community development, welfare and early-childhood support
findings: Nigerian social-work education and public-sector sources describe community, welfare, child-care and support work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian social and child-care context; exact professional requirements depend on role, agency and client group.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian early-childhood care, primary education and childcare training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian early-childhood care and education, primary education, childcare settings, NCE minimum standards and learner safeguarding
findings: NCCE minimum standards identify Early Childhood Care and Primary Education as a specialised NCE pathway for early-years and primary teachers.
Federal education sources publish national minimum standards for ECCDE centres.
source_summaries.limitations: Education standards support institution and educator foundations; they do not establish one universal private childcare credential for every nanny, caregiver or family setting.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Correctional Service probation and rehabilitation context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria non-custodial measures, probation, parole, rehabilitation, counselling and correctional support
findings: The Nigerian Correctional Service describes non-custodial measures including probation, parole, community service and restorative justice, together with rehabilitation, counselling and psychosocial support functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes official Nigerian probation and correctional-service functions; it does not establish a current vacancy, one civilian job title or a universal qualification outside the service pathway.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian social-work, child-care, safeguarding and psychosocial pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social work, child and family welfare, childcare, safeguarding, community development, psychosocial support, counselling and correctional or rehabilitation services
findings: NASoW identifies social work across Nigerian schools, hospitals, NGOs, ministries, rehabilitation centres, old people's homes, correctional centres and government levels; the Nigerian social-work curriculum identifies child, family, youth, mental-health, counselling, community, criminal-justice and correctional practice; NBTE lists Children's Care, Learning and Development; NCoS describes counselling, psychosocial support, rehabilitation, probation and non-custodial services.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian practice, service and training pathways; they do not establish a national vacancy count or imply that every caregiver, mentor, nanny or support worker is a regulated social worker.

source_summaries.name: National Universities Commission CCMAS and standards
OHCSF Personnel Audit and Skills Gap Analysis project
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian federal civil-service skills identification, development and gap analysis
findings: The OHCSF PASGA portal describes a project to identify and develop the skills of Nigerian public servants and build a data-driven, globally competitive civil service.
source_summaries.limitations: The portal is public-service skills context and does not establish a private-sector requirement or a single certification.

source_summaries.name: Federal Government social-work professionalisation and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice, professionalisation, standards and capacity-building context
findings: The Federal Government described work to strengthen social-work practice in Nigeria, including professionalisation and standards challenges under the Social Work Practitioners Act 2022 context.
source_summaries.limitations: The article supports Nigerian practice context but does not establish one compulsory credential for every care, counselling or social-service role.

source_summaries.name: TRCN safeguarding resources for Nigerian schools
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian child protection, learner safety, violence-free schools and safeguarding practice
findings: TRCN provides resources on child protection, safety, security and violence-free schools and describes protocols and standards for protecting children and learners.
source_summaries.limitations: Safeguarding resources support education and child-facing practice; they do not create one universal certificate for all social-service or childcare roles.

source_summaries.limitations: TRCN applies to teaching practice within its mandate, not to every education, training, research or childcare role.

source_summaries.name: Bureau of Public Service Reforms National Strategy for Public Service Reform
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian civil-service administration, competency, performance, accountability and professionalisation
findings: The strategy describes a professional, results-oriented, competent, accountable and citizen-centred Nigerian public service, including merit-based recruitment, performance management, job evaluation and professionalisation of core cadres.
source_summaries.limitations: A reform strategy supplies public-service capability context, not a universal qualification for every public or private-sector role.

source_summaries.name: NUC, NCCE and Nigerian education standards
Jobberman Nigeria jobs
MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
Nigeria Association of Social Workers role-family context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice across public services, community development, teaching hospitals, NGOs, rehabilitation, care and correctional settings
findings: NASoW identifies social workers across schools, teaching hospitals, NGOs, ministries, rehabilitation centres, old people's homes, correctional centres and local, state and federal institutions.

NASoW Lagos names public-sector social welfare officers, community development officers, medical social workers, social-work educators, independent social workers and NGO social workers among its professional community.
source_summaries.limitations: Professional-body role-family context demonstrates Nigerian practice settings; it is not a vacancy count, universal title equivalence or proof that every specialised social-care occupation is established in every Nigerian setting.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian agricultural research, horticulture, crop, livestock and extension context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian crop production, horticulture, livestock, plant genetics, biotechnology, agricultural training, extension and production improvement
findings: ARCN coordinates agricultural research, training and extension through national institutes and colleges across Nigeria's agro-ecological zones; its plant-resources work covers crop improvement, seed production, irrigation, pest and disease management, genetics and biotechnology; NIHORT covers fruits, vegetables, spices, ornamentals, post-harvest processing and sustainable horticultural production; NBTE lists Nigerian crop-production and livestock-production technical pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian agricultural role-family and training context, not a universal farm system, commodity, equipment stack, licence or vacancy count for every agricultural occupation.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian social-work, child-care and community-support context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social work, child protection, community development, welfare and early-childhood support
findings: Nigerian social-work education and public-sector sources describe community, welfare, child-care and support work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian social and child-care context; exact professional requirements depend on role, agency and client group.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian early-childhood care, primary education and childcare training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian early-childhood care and education, primary education, childcare settings, NCE minimum standards and learner safeguarding
findings: NCCE minimum standards identify Early Childhood Care and Primary Education as a specialised NCE pathway for early-years and primary teachers.
Federal education sources publish national minimum standards for ECCDE centres.
source_summaries.limitations: Education standards support institution and educator foundations; they do not establish one universal private childcare credential for every nanny, caregiver or family setting.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Correctional Service probation and rehabilitation context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria non-custodial measures, probation, parole, rehabilitation, counselling and correctional support
findings: The Nigerian Correctional Service describes non-custodial measures including probation, parole, community service and restorative justice, together with rehabilitation, counselling and psychosocial support functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes official Nigerian probation and correctional-service functions; it does not establish a current vacancy, one civilian job title or a universal qualification outside the service pathway.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian social-work, child-care, safeguarding and psychosocial pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social work, child and family welfare, childcare, safeguarding, community development, psychosocial support, counselling and correctional or rehabilitation services
findings: NASoW identifies social work across Nigerian schools, hospitals, NGOs, ministries, rehabilitation centres, old people's homes, correctional centres and government levels; the Nigerian social-work curriculum identifies child, family, youth, mental-health, counselling, community, criminal-justice and correctional practice; NBTE lists Children's Care, Learning and Development; NCoS describes counselling, psychosocial support, rehabilitation, probation and non-custodial services.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian practice, service and training pathways; they do not establish a national vacancy count or imply that every caregiver, mentor, nanny or support worker is a regulated social worker.

source_summaries.name: National Universities Commission CCMAS and standards
OHCSF Personnel Audit and Skills Gap Analysis project
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian federal civil-service skills identification, development and gap analysis
findings: The OHCSF PASGA portal describes a project to identify and develop the skills of Nigerian public servants and build a data-driven, globally competitive civil service.
source_summaries.limitations: The portal is public-service skills context and does not establish a private-sector requirement or a single certification.

source_summaries.name: Federal Government social-work professionalisation and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice, professionalisation, standards and capacity-building context
findings: The Federal Government described work to strengthen social-work practice in Nigeria, including professionalisation and standards challenges under the Social Work Practitioners Act 2022 context.
source_summaries.limitations: The article supports Nigerian practice context but does not establish one compulsory credential for every care, counselling or social-service role.

source_summaries.name: TRCN safeguarding resources for Nigerian schools
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian child protection, learner safety, violence-free schools and safeguarding practice
findings: TRCN provides resources on child protection, safety, security and violence-free schools and describes protocols and standards for protecting children and learners.
source_summaries.limitations: Safeguarding resources support education and child-facing practice; they do not create one universal certificate for all social-service or childcare roles.

source_summaries.name: Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria teacher standards and PQE
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian teacher education, accreditation, registration, professional qualifying examination and competency assessment
findings: TRCN describes its responsibility for teacher-education standards, programme accreditation, qualification approval, professional registration and competency assessment; its 2026 updates include PQE results and school-accreditation policy implementation.
source_summaries.limitations: TRCN applies to teaching practice within its mandate, not to every education, training, research or childcare role.

source_summaries.limitations: A reform strategy supplies public-service capability context, not a universal qualification for every public or private-sector role.

Nigeria Association of Social Workers role-family context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice across public services, community development, teaching hospitals, NGOs, rehabilitation, care and correctional settings
findings: NASoW identifies social workers across schools, teaching hospitals, NGOs, ministries, rehabilitation centres, old people's homes, correctional centres and local, state and federal institutions.

NASoW Lagos names public-sector social welfare officers, community development officers, medical social workers, social-work educators, independent social workers and NGO social workers among its professional community.
source_summaries.limitations: Professional-body role-family context demonstrates Nigerian practice settings; it is not a vacancy count, universal title equivalence or proof that every specialised social-care occupation is established in every Nigerian setting.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian agricultural research, horticulture, crop, livestock and extension context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian crop production, horticulture, livestock, plant genetics, biotechnology, agricultural training, extension and production improvement
findings: ARCN coordinates agricultural research, training and extension through national institutes and colleges across Nigeria's agro-ecological zones; its plant-resources work covers crop improvement, seed production, irrigation, pest and disease management, genetics and biotechnology; NIHORT covers fruits, vegetables, spices, ornamentals, post-harvest processing and sustainable horticultural production; NBTE lists Nigerian crop-production and livestock-production technical pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian agricultural role-family and training context, not a universal farm system, commodity, equipment stack, licence or vacancy count for every agricultural occupation.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian social-work, child-care and community-support context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social work, child protection, community development, welfare and early-childhood support
findings: Nigerian social-work education and public-sector sources describe community, welfare, child-care and support work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian social and child-care context; exact professional requirements depend on role, agency and client group.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian early-childhood care, primary education and childcare training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian early-childhood care and education, primary education, childcare settings, NCE minimum standards and learner safeguarding
findings: NCCE minimum standards identify Early Childhood Care and Primary Education as a specialised NCE pathway for early-years and primary teachers.
Federal education sources publish national minimum standards for ECCDE centres.
source_summaries.limitations: Education standards support institution and educator foundations; they do not establish one universal private childcare credential for every nanny, caregiver or family setting.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Correctional Service probation and rehabilitation context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria non-custodial measures, probation, parole, rehabilitation, counselling and correctional support
findings: The Nigerian Correctional Service describes non-custodial measures including probation, parole, community service and restorative justice, together with rehabilitation, counselling and psychosocial support functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes official Nigerian probation and correctional-service functions; it does not establish a current vacancy, one civilian job title or a universal qualification outside the service pathway.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian social-work, child-care, safeguarding and psychosocial pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social work, child and family welfare, childcare, safeguarding, community development, psychosocial support, counselling and correctional or rehabilitation services
findings: NASoW identifies social work across Nigerian schools, hospitals, NGOs, ministries, rehabilitation centres, old people's homes, correctional centres and government levels; the Nigerian social-work curriculum identifies child, family, youth, mental-health, counselling, community, criminal-justice and correctional practice; NBTE lists Children's Care, Learning and Development; NCoS describes counselling, psychosocial support, rehabilitation, probation and non-custodial services.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian practice, service and training pathways; they do not establish a national vacancy count or imply that every caregiver, mentor, nanny or support worker is a regulated social worker.

source_summaries.name: National Universities Commission CCMAS and standards
OHCSF Personnel Audit and Skills Gap Analysis project
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian federal civil-service skills identification, development and gap analysis
findings: The OHCSF PASGA portal describes a project to identify and develop the skills of Nigerian public servants and build a data-driven, globally competitive civil service.
source_summaries.limitations: The portal is public-service skills context and does not establish a private-sector requirement or a single certification.

source_summaries.name: Federal Government social-work professionalisation and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice, professionalisation, standards and capacity-building context
findings: The Federal Government described work to strengthen social-work practice in Nigeria, including professionalisation and standards challenges under the Social Work Practitioners Act 2022 context.
source_summaries.limitations: The article supports Nigerian practice context but does not establish one compulsory credential for every care, counselling or social-service role.

source_summaries.name: TRCN safeguarding resources for Nigerian schools
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian child protection, learner safety, violence-free schools and safeguarding practice
findings: TRCN provides resources on child protection, safety, security and violence-free schools and describes protocols and standards for protecting children and learners.
source_summaries.limitations: Safeguarding resources support education and child-facing practice; they do not create one universal certificate for all social-service or childcare roles.

source_summaries.name: Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria teacher standards and PQE
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian teacher education, accreditation, registration, professional qualifying examination and competency assessment
findings: TRCN describes its responsibility for teacher-education standards, programme accreditation, qualification approval, professional registration and competency assessment; its 2026 updates include PQE results and school-accreditation policy implementation.
source_summaries.limitations: TRCN applies to teaching practice within its mandate, not to every education, training, research or childcare role.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice across public services, community development, teaching hospitals, NGOs, rehabilitation, care and correctional settings
findings: NASoW identifies social workers across schools, teaching hospitals, NGOs, ministries, rehabilitation centres, old people's homes, correctional centres and local, state and federal institutions.

NASoW Lagos names public-sector social welfare officers, community development officers, medical social workers, social-work educators, independent social workers and NGO social workers among its professional community.
source_summaries.limitations: Professional-body role-family context demonstrates Nigerian practice settings; it is not a vacancy count, universal title equivalence or proof that every specialised social-care occupation is established in every Nigerian setting.

NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian agricultural research, horticulture, crop, livestock and extension context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian crop production, horticulture, livestock, plant genetics, biotechnology, agricultural training, extension and production improvement
findings: ARCN coordinates agricultural research, training and extension through national institutes and colleges across Nigeria's agro-ecological zones; its plant-resources work covers crop improvement, seed production, irrigation, pest and disease management, genetics and biotechnology; NIHORT covers fruits, vegetables, spices, ornamentals, post-harvest processing and sustainable horticultural production; NBTE lists Nigerian crop-production and livestock-production technical pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian agricultural role-family and training context, not a universal farm system, commodity, equipment stack, licence or vacancy count for every agricultural occupation.

findings: Nigerian social-work education and public-sector sources describe community, welfare, child-care and support work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian social and child-care context; exact professional requirements depend on role, agency and client group.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian early-childhood care and education, primary education, childcare settings, NCE minimum standards and learner safeguarding
findings: NCCE minimum standards identify Early Childhood Care and Primary Education as a specialised NCE pathway for early-years and primary teachers.
Federal education sources publish national minimum standards for ECCDE centres.
source_summaries.limitations: Education standards support institution and educator foundations; they do not establish one universal private childcare credential for every nanny, caregiver or family setting.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Correctional Service probation and rehabilitation context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria non-custodial measures, probation, parole, rehabilitation, counselling and correctional support
findings: The Nigerian Correctional Service describes non-custodial measures including probation, parole, community service and restorative justice, together with rehabilitation, counselling and psychosocial support functions.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes official Nigerian probation and correctional-service functions; it does not establish a current vacancy, one civilian job title or a universal qualification outside the service pathway.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian social-work, child-care, safeguarding and psychosocial pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social work, child and family welfare, childcare, safeguarding, community development, psychosocial support, counselling and correctional or rehabilitation services
findings: NASoW identifies social work across Nigerian schools, hospitals, NGOs, ministries, rehabilitation centres, old people's homes, correctional centres and government levels; the Nigerian social-work curriculum identifies child, family, youth, mental-health, counselling, community, criminal-justice and correctional practice; NBTE lists Children's Care, Learning and Development; NCoS describes counselling, psychosocial support, rehabilitation, probation and non-custodial services.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian practice, service and training pathways; they do not establish a national vacancy count or imply that every caregiver, mentor, nanny or support worker is a regulated social worker.

OHCSF Personnel Audit and Skills Gap Analysis project
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian federal civil-service skills identification, development and gap analysis
findings: The OHCSF PASGA portal describes a project to identify and develop the skills of Nigerian public servants and build a data-driven, globally competitive civil service.
source_summaries.limitations: The portal is public-service skills context and does not establish a private-sector requirement or a single certification.

source_summaries.name: Federal Government social-work professionalisation and standards context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian social-work practice, professionalisation, standards and capacity-building context
findings: The Federal Government described work to strengthen social-work practice in Nigeria, including professionalisation and standards challenges under the Social Work Practitioners Act 2022 context.
source_summaries.limitations: The article supports Nigerian practice context but does not establish one compulsory credential for every care, counselling or social-service role.

source_summaries.name: TRCN safeguarding resources for Nigerian schools
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian child protection, learner safety, violence-free schools and safeguarding practice
findings: TRCN provides resources on child protection, safety, security and violence-free schools and describes protocols and standards for protecting children and learners.
source_summaries.limitations: Safeguarding resources support education and child-facing practice; they do not create one universal certificate for all social-service or childcare roles.

findings: NRC describes passenger and goods carriage, station management, train safety, control and signalling, route planning, traffic and commercial operations; NCAA regulates air transport, aviation fuel and aerodrome services; FAAN manages Nigerian commercial airports, airport operations, cargo and passenger services; NAMA describes air-traffic-management, communications, navigation and surveillance; the Federal Ministry of Transportation lists rail, road, engineering and transport-planning functions.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operation context, not a vacancy count or a counterpart for every global vehicle, pipeline, event, warehouse or specialist infrastructure title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority radiation-safety training for mining
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian solid-mineral mining and processing radiation-safety roles and adjacent technical occupations
findings: NNRA announced a 2026 national course for current or prospective Radiation Safety Officers in mining and mineral processing, covering NORM/TE-NORM, monitoring, dose assessment, radiation protection, handling, transport, waste management and regulatory compliance.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a specialised radiation-safety pathway and does not apply to every mining or geology role.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian energy policy, planning, statistics, renewable energy, energy efficiency, electricity, fossil fuels and sustainable-energy development
findings: The Energy Commission of Nigeria identifies national energy planning and policy implementation, energy statistics, energy information systems, electricity and fossil-fuel functions, renewable-energy research and energy-efficiency or sustainable-development work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian energy-sector and planning context, not a universal building-assessor licence, project-vacancy count or qualification for every hydropower, pipeline, energy or conservation title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian inland-waterway transport, marine safety and operations context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian inland-waterway navigation, vessel operations, cargo handling, warehousing, ferry services, pilotage, safety inspection, traffic management, maritime security and intermodal transport
findings: NIWA describes statutory Nigerian responsibility for inland-waterway development and regulation, vessel operations, ferry services, cargo handling, storage, stevedoring, pilotage, vessel traffic management, safety inspections, search and rescue and maritime security; it also describes training for boat operators and skippers.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian inland-waterway role and operational context; it does not establish a counterpart for every air, rail, pipeline or ocean-shipping title, or one universal licence for every waterway role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operations context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian railway stations, rail operations, train safety, signalling, route planning, airport operations, baggage, airspace and air-transport services, aviation fuel and road-transport administration
findings: NRC describes passenger and goods carriage, station management, train safety, control and signalling, route planning, traffic and commercial operations; NCAA regulates air transport, aviation fuel and aerodrome services; FAAN manages Nigerian commercial airports, airport operations, cargo and passenger services; NAMA describes air-traffic-management, communications, navigation and surveillance; the Federal Ministry of Transportation lists rail, road, engineering and transport-planning functions.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operation context, not a vacancy count or a counterpart for every global vehicle, pipeline, event, warehouse or specialist infrastructure title.

source_summaries.name: NIMASA and Maritime Academy of Nigeria marine engineering, naval architecture and STCW training
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian marine engineering, naval architecture, maritime education, seafarer certification, safety, security and watchkeeping
findings: NIMASA lists approved maritime training institutions and STCW courses, while the Maritime Academy of Nigeria describes nautical studies, marine engineering and maritime-management training.
source_summaries.limitations: STCW and certificates apply to relevant seafaring duties; they are not universal requirements for every shore-based marine, shipyard, logistics or administrative role.

findings: NIMASA lists Master/Chief Mate, Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch, Able Seafarer Deck, Chief and Second Engineer, Engineering Watch, Electro-Technical Officer and domestic certificates such as River Master, Quarter Master, Marine Engineer Assistant, Coxswain and Motorman.
The framework combines approved education, practical training, sea service and competency certification.
source_summaries.limitations: Certificate-of-competency requirements apply to the relevant seafaring duties; they are not a universal requirement for shore-based maritime work.

source_summaries.limitations: These standards apply to seafarer roles and do not apply to every maritime, port, logistics or naval-architecture occupation.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian inland-waterway navigation, vessel operations, cargo handling, warehousing, ferry services, pilotage, safety inspection, traffic management, maritime security and intermodal transport
findings: NIWA describes statutory Nigerian responsibility for inland-waterway development and regulation, vessel operations, ferry services, cargo handling, storage, stevedoring, pilotage, vessel traffic management, safety inspections, search and rescue and maritime security; it also describes training for boat operators and skippers.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian inland-waterway role and operational context; it does not establish a counterpart for every air, rail, pipeline or ocean-shipping title, or one universal licence for every waterway role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operations context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian railway stations, rail operations, train safety, signalling, route planning, airport operations, baggage, airspace and air-transport services, aviation fuel and road-transport administration
findings: NRC describes passenger and goods carriage, station management, train safety, control and signalling, route planning, traffic and commercial operations; NCAA regulates air transport, aviation fuel and aerodrome services; FAAN manages Nigerian commercial airports, airport operations, cargo and passenger services; NAMA describes air-traffic-management, communications, navigation and surveillance; the Federal Ministry of Transportation lists rail, road, engineering and transport-planning functions.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operation context, not a vacancy count or a counterpart for every global vehicle, pipeline, event, warehouse or specialist infrastructure title.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian trade, technician, craft, agricultural, hospitality, ICT, automotive, construction, fashion and technical occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current catalogue names validated or current NOS/NSQ routes for masonry, electrical installation, carpentry, fashion and garment making, leather, food and beverage, automotive, agricultural equipment, interior-decoration-related craft and many other trades.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and Federal TVET trade pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian vocational and technical pathways including garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web, health and safety and other occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current NOS catalogue names occupational standards and levels for garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web and other trades.

source_summaries.limitations: An NOS or TVET pathway is evidence of a Nigerian training route, not a claim that every employer requires the listed level or that one trade credential is interchangeable with a degree or professional licence.

source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian automotive context; the required certification and supervision depend on vehicle system, workshop and role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian automotive, vehicle mechatronics and component-development context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian automotive maintenance, vehicle mechatronics, automotive engineering, component development, vehicle production, electric or gas vehicles and automotive skills training
findings: NADDC and NBTE identify Nigerian automotive skills development, vehicle mechatronics, component and vehicle production, workshop standards, CNG and electric-vehicle pathways, engineering design, local materials and automotive training centres; the automotive mechatronics curriculum covers vehicle electrical/electronic systems, structured fault-finding, tools, safety, workshop management and environmental practice.

findings: NBTE's current catalogue names validated or current NOS/NSQ routes for masonry, electrical installation, carpentry, fashion and garment making, leather, food and beverage, automotive, agricultural equipment, interior-decoration-related craft and many other trades.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS/NSQ route is a skills/qualification pathway; it is not automatically a separate licence to practise every trade or operate every business.

source_summaries.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and Federal TVET trade pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian vocational and technical pathways including garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web, health and safety and other occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current NOS catalogue names occupational standards and levels for garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web and other trades.
The Federal TVET initiative describes accredited centres, practical skills, employment and entrepreneurship pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS or TVET pathway is evidence of a Nigerian training route, not a claim that every employer requires the listed level or that one trade credential is interchangeable with a degree or professional licence.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian automotive engineering, diagnostics and vehicle-manufacturing context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian vehicle manufacturing, repair, diagnostics, inspection, CNG and electric-vehicle conversion, mechanical and materials engineering
findings: NADDC supports automotive manufacturing, certified CNG conversion workshops, EV transition and automotive design tools and training.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian automotive context; the required certification and supervision depend on vehicle system, workshop and role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian automotive, vehicle mechatronics and component-development context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian automotive maintenance, vehicle mechatronics, automotive engineering, component development, vehicle production, electric or gas vehicles and automotive skills training
findings: NADDC and NBTE identify Nigerian automotive skills development, vehicle mechatronics, component and vehicle production, workshop standards, CNG and electric-vehicle pathways, engineering design, local materials and automotive training centres; the automotive mechatronics curriculum covers vehicle electrical/electronic systems, structured fault-finding, tools, safety, workshop management and environmental practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian automotive and mechatronics context, not a motorsport-specific vacancy count or a counterpart for every aerospace, racing, software or specialist precision-engineering title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian construction-equipment operator training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian construction-equipment operation, excavators, bulldozers, graders, loaders, concrete mixers, maintenance, workplace safety and road regulations
findings: NBTE National Skills Qualifications for Nigerian construction-equipment operations identify operator-helper and operator competencies, daily checks, equipment maintenance, health and safety, road and workplace regulations, and specific excavator, bulldozer, grader, loader and concrete-truck-mixer operation units.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian construction-equipment training context, not a vacancy count or a local counterpart for every mining, snow, cable-vehicle, elevator or specialist crane title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian digital technology, software, AI, cybersecurity and data-protection context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian software, web, data, artificial intelligence, networking, cybersecurity, digital services, information systems, privacy and compliance work
findings: NITDA identifies digital skills, software and hardware development, cybersecurity, digital trust, research and an agile technology workforce as Nigerian strategic priorities.
NBTE lists Nigerian programmes and national occupational standards spanning software, web, data, AI, networking, robotics, computer hardware, cybersecurity and digital service operations.
NDPC describes data-protection compliance, information privacy, information audit, data management and information-security evidence relevant to Nigerian privacy and compliance work.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian technology-sector, training and regulatory context; it does not prove a specific employer requirement, salary, vacancy count or universal certificate for every ICT title.

source_summaries.name: COREN National Clean Energy Skills Certification Scheme
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian renewable-energy and energy-efficiency skills and certification
findings: COREN describes itself as the national certification body for clean-energy skills and reports revalidation of competency standards in July 2024 and a 2025 partnership with NEMSA for renewable-energy and energy-efficiency certification.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports clean-energy skills certification context; it is not a universal licence for every energy or electrical role.

source_summaries.name: Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria registration guidance
COREN 2026 engineering regulation and public-safety reforms
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian engineering practice, registration, public safety, project monitoring and anti-quackery context
findings: COREN's 2026 reforms emphasise qualified and registered practitioners, public safety, project monitoring and enforcement against unqualified engineering practice.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports regulated-engineering context; it is not a personal registration requirement for every technician or non-engineering role in an engineering organisation.

source_summaries.name: COREN and Nigerian Society of Engineers
Nigerian health records registration and digital health information context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian health records officers, health-information management, registration and licensure, electronic content management, digital health, EMR/EHR, data quality and confidentiality
findings: The Federal Ministry of Health describes HRORBN registration, digital compliance and health-records workforce demand, and describes ECM and national digital-health/EMR direction.
source_summaries.limitations: The regulatory requirement applies to defined health-records practice; digital-health context does not make every medical, data or administrative role a registered health-records profession.

findings: A Nigeria-focused physical-sciences jobs page identified a Physicist vacancy in Ikeja, Lagos, with relevant training or certification requirements.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a single dated vacancy signal; it is not a national demand count, universal qualification route or evidence for every scientific-research speciality.

MDCN and MLSCN Nigerian medical, dental and laboratory registration and training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian medical and dental education, housemanship, professional registration, annual practice licensing, medical laboratory training, laboratory registration and continuing professional development
findings: MDCN publishes medical and dental education, accreditation, registration, practising-licence and CPD services.
MLSCN publishes medical-laboratory training, registration, licensure, laboratory accreditation and CPD services, including the 2025 ND curriculum.
source_summaries.limitations: The regulations apply to defined health professions and facilities; they do not establish a universal licence for every health-support, research, technology or administrative role.
