NASENI Centre of Excellence in Nanotechnology and Advanced Materials
National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NEMSA and REAN renewable-energy safety and standards partnership
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian renewable-energy installation safety, standardisation and quality assurance
findings: NEMSA reported collaboration with the Renewable Energy Association of Nigeria to strengthen safety, standardisation and quality assurance and stated that installations should be carried out by certified professionals under national requirements.
source_summaries.limitations: The statement concerns renewable-energy installations and does not impose one certificate on every energy-adjacent role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission generation-licence requirements
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian on-grid, off-grid and embedded electricity-generation facilities
findings: NERC describes generation licences and associated environmental-impact or effluent-management documentation for specified Nigerian generation facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a facility/operator licence context, not a personal licence for every energy worker.

source_summaries.name: NESREA national environmental-regulation review
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian chemicals, waste, energy and environmental-management standards
findings: NESREA reported review of national environmental regulations covering chemicals and waste management and highlighted the role of industry, government, civil society and research in environmental management.
source_summaries.limitations: Regulatory review supports environmental-practice context; it does not establish a certificate or a particular tool for every environmental role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian allied-health, radiography, rehabilitation and optometry context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian radiography, nuclear and diagnostic imaging, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, chiropractic, osteopathy, prosthetics and orthotics, optometry and allied-health education
findings: RRBN regulates radiography and related diagnostic or therapeutic radiography practice; MRTB regulates and licenses rehabilitation professions including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, prosthetics/orthotics, chiropractic and osteopathic practice; ODORBN regulates Nigerian optometrists and dispensing opticians; NUC allied-health standards identify Nigerian allied-health degree pathways and professional information practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian nuclear research-reactor operations and regulatory context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria Nuclear Research Reactor NIRR-I, reactor operations, maintenance, licensing, inspection, nuclear education and operator capacity
findings: NNRA identifies the licensed NIRR-I research reactor at CERT, ABU Zaria and describes inspection of its operation, maintenance, records and operational staff; NAEC identifies nuclear research centres and reactor-infrastructure development in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes a Nigerian research-reactor pathway, not a claim that Nigeria operates commercial nuclear power plants or that every nuclear title is locally available.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operations context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian railway stations, rail operations, train safety, signalling, route planning, airport operations, baggage, airspace and air-transport services, aviation fuel and road-transport administration
findings: NRC describes passenger and goods carriage, station management, train safety, control and signalling, route planning, traffic and commercial operations; NCAA regulates air transport, aviation fuel and aerodrome services; FAAN manages Nigerian commercial airports, airport operations, cargo and passenger services; NAMA describes air-traffic-management, communications, navigation and surveillance; the Federal Ministry of Transportation lists rail, road, engineering and transport-planning functions.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operation context, not a vacancy count or a counterpart for every global vehicle, pipeline, event, warehouse or specialist infrastructure title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority
Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority radiation-safety training for mining
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian solid-mineral mining and processing radiation-safety roles and adjacent technical occupations
findings: NNRA announced a 2026 national course for current or prospective Radiation Safety Officers in mining and mineral processing, covering NORM/TE-NORM, monitoring, dose assessment, radiation protection, handling, transport, waste management and regulatory compliance.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a specialised radiation-safety pathway and does not apply to every mining or geology role.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian renewable-energy and energy-efficiency skills and certification
findings: COREN describes itself as the national certification body for clean-energy skills and reports revalidation of competency standards in July 2024 and a 2025 partnership with NEMSA for renewable-energy and energy-efficiency certification.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian engineering practice, registration, public safety, project monitoring and anti-quackery context
findings: COREN's 2026 reforms emphasise qualified and registered practitioners, public safety, project monitoring and enforcement against unqualified engineering practice.

Nigerian health records registration and digital health information context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian health records officers, health-information management, registration and licensure, electronic content management, digital health, EMR/EHR, data quality and confidentiality
findings: The Federal Ministry of Health describes HRORBN registration, digital compliance and health-records workforce demand, and describes ECM and national digital-health/EMR direction.
source_summaries.limitations: The regulatory requirement applies to defined health-records practice; digital-health context does not make every medical, data or administrative role a registered health-records profession.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria physicist vacancy signal
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based physical-science employment
findings: A Nigeria-focused physical-sciences jobs page identified a Physicist vacancy in Ikeja, Lagos, with relevant training or certification requirements.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a single dated vacancy signal; it is not a national demand count, universal qualification route or evidence for every scientific-research speciality.

source_summaries.name: Jobberman Nigeria jobs
MDCN and MLSCN Nigerian medical, dental and laboratory registration and training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian medical and dental education, housemanship, professional registration, annual practice licensing, medical laboratory training, laboratory registration and continuing professional development
findings: MDCN publishes medical and dental education, accreditation, registration, practising-licence and CPD services.
MLSCN publishes medical-laboratory training, registration, licensure, laboratory accreditation and CPD services, including the 2025 ND curriculum.
source_summaries.limitations: The regulations apply to defined health professions and facilities; they do not establish a universal licence for every health-support, research, technology or administrative role.

source_summaries.name: MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
NASENI Centre of Excellence in Nanotechnology and Advanced Materials
National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NEMSA and REAN renewable-energy safety and standards partnership
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian renewable-energy installation safety, standardisation and quality assurance
findings: NEMSA reported collaboration with the Renewable Energy Association of Nigeria to strengthen safety, standardisation and quality assurance and stated that installations should be carried out by certified professionals under national requirements.
source_summaries.limitations: The statement concerns renewable-energy installations and does not impose one certificate on every energy-adjacent role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission generation-licence requirements
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian on-grid, off-grid and embedded electricity-generation facilities
findings: NERC describes generation licences and associated environmental-impact or effluent-management documentation for specified Nigerian generation facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a facility/operator licence context, not a personal licence for every energy worker.

source_summaries.name: NESREA national environmental-regulation review
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian chemicals, waste, energy and environmental-management standards
findings: NESREA reported review of national environmental regulations covering chemicals and waste management and highlighted the role of industry, government, civil society and research in environmental management.
source_summaries.limitations: Regulatory review supports environmental-practice context; it does not establish a certificate or a particular tool for every environmental role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian allied-health, radiography, rehabilitation and optometry context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian radiography, nuclear and diagnostic imaging, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, chiropractic, osteopathy, prosthetics and orthotics, optometry and allied-health education
findings: RRBN regulates radiography and related diagnostic or therapeutic radiography practice; MRTB regulates and licenses rehabilitation professions including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, prosthetics/orthotics, chiropractic and osteopathic practice; ODORBN regulates Nigerian optometrists and dispensing opticians; NUC allied-health standards identify Nigerian allied-health degree pathways and professional information practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian nuclear research-reactor operations and regulatory context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria Nuclear Research Reactor NIRR-I, reactor operations, maintenance, licensing, inspection, nuclear education and operator capacity
findings: NNRA identifies the licensed NIRR-I research reactor at CERT, ABU Zaria and describes inspection of its operation, maintenance, records and operational staff; NAEC identifies nuclear research centres and reactor-infrastructure development in Nigeria.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes a Nigerian research-reactor pathway, not a claim that Nigeria operates commercial nuclear power plants or that every nuclear title is locally available.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operations context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian railway stations, rail operations, train safety, signalling, route planning, airport operations, baggage, airspace and air-transport services, aviation fuel and road-transport administration
findings: NRC describes passenger and goods carriage, station management, train safety, control and signalling, route planning, traffic and commercial operations; NCAA regulates air transport, aviation fuel and aerodrome services; FAAN manages Nigerian commercial airports, airport operations, cargo and passenger services; NAMA describes air-traffic-management, communications, navigation and surveillance; the Federal Ministry of Transportation lists rail, road, engineering and transport-planning functions.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian rail, airport, airspace and transport-operation context, not a vacancy count or a counterpart for every global vehicle, pipeline, event, warehouse or specialist infrastructure title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority
Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority radiation-safety training for mining
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian solid-mineral mining and processing radiation-safety roles and adjacent technical occupations
findings: NNRA announced a 2026 national course for current or prospective Radiation Safety Officers in mining and mineral processing, covering NORM/TE-NORM, monitoring, dose assessment, radiation protection, handling, transport, waste management and regulatory compliance.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a specialised radiation-safety pathway and does not apply to every mining or geology role.

Nigerian allied-health, radiography, rehabilitation and optometry context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian radiography, nuclear and diagnostic imaging, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, chiropractic, osteopathy, prosthetics and orthotics, optometry and allied-health education
findings: RRBN regulates radiography and related diagnostic or therapeutic radiography practice; MRTB regulates and licenses rehabilitation professions including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, prosthetics/orthotics, chiropractic and osteopathic practice; ODORBN regulates Nigerian optometrists and dispensing opticians; NUC allied-health standards identify Nigerian allied-health degree pathways and professional information practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian allied-health, rehabilitation, laboratory and diagnostic practice context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian physiotherapy, rehabilitation, radiography, medical laboratory, nutrition, occupational therapy, audiology and related allied-health practice
findings: The Federal Ministry of Health identifies Nigerian professional boards for medical laboratory science, medical rehabilitation, radiography and related health professions.
Nigerian university curricula describe anatomy, physiology, therapeutic exercise and patient-care preparation for rehabilitation practice.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian profession and education context; exact registration, scope and supervision depend on the profession and current regulator, and it does not establish a vacancy count for every therapy title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian biomedical, biotechnology, pharmaceutical and epidemiology research context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian biomedical research, molecular biology, biotechnology, immunology, epidemiology, toxicology, pharmacology, diagnostics, vaccines and pharmaceutical development
findings: NIMR describes Nigerian molecular epidemiology, food-safety, immunogenetics, theranostics, microbiome and molecular-technique laboratories; NABDA describes Nigerian biomedical biotechnology work in immunology, vaccinology, antibody generation, DNA, biobanking and diagnostics; NIPRD describes pharmaceutical, biological-product, toxicology, quality-assurance and environmental-science research.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian research and institutional role families, not a vacancy count, personal licence or universal academic route for every biomedical or scientific occupation.

findings: RRBN regulates radiography and related diagnostic or therapeutic radiography practice; MRTB regulates and licenses rehabilitation professions including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, audiology, prosthetics/orthotics, chiropractic and osteopathic practice; ODORBN regulates Nigerian optometrists and dispensing opticians; NUC allied-health standards identify Nigerian allied-health degree pathways and professional information practice.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian regulated-profession context and do not support every therapy, assistant or research title in the global library; licensure must be shown only where the named Nigerian regulator covers the profession.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian physiotherapy, rehabilitation, radiography, medical laboratory, nutrition, occupational therapy, audiology and related allied-health practice
findings: The Federal Ministry of Health identifies Nigerian professional boards for medical laboratory science, medical rehabilitation, radiography and related health professions.
Nigerian university curricula describe anatomy, physiology, therapeutic exercise and patient-care preparation for rehabilitation practice.
source_summaries.limitations: This establishes Nigerian profession and education context; exact registration, scope and supervision depend on the profession and current regulator, and it does not establish a vacancy count for every therapy title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian biomedical, biotechnology, pharmaceutical and epidemiology research context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian biomedical research, molecular biology, biotechnology, immunology, epidemiology, toxicology, pharmacology, diagnostics, vaccines and pharmaceutical development
findings: NIMR describes Nigerian molecular epidemiology, food-safety, immunogenetics, theranostics, microbiome and molecular-technique laboratories; NABDA describes Nigerian biomedical biotechnology work in immunology, vaccinology, antibody generation, DNA, biobanking and diagnostics; NIPRD describes pharmaceutical, biological-product, toxicology, quality-assurance and environmental-science research.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian research and institutional role families, not a vacancy count, personal licence or universal academic route for every biomedical or scientific occupation.

source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian research and institutional role families, not a vacancy count, personal licence or universal academic route for every biomedical or scientific occupation.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian biomedical, biotechnology, pharmaceutical and epidemiology research context

Nigerian electronics, computer-hardware, telecommunications and instrumentation training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian electronic-system maintenance, computer hardware repairs, telecommunications, network cabling, instrumentation, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronics technology and related technician work
findings: NBTE lists Nigerian technical pathways in computer-hardware repair and maintenance, electronic-system maintenance craft, industrial electronics, telecommunications equipment installation and maintenance, telecommunication technology, network cabling, mobile-phone repair, electrical/electronic engineering technology and instrumentation and control; the curricula cover diagnosis, measurement, soldering, component replacement, networking, communication systems and fault repair.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian technical-training and competency context, not a vacancy count, vendor-specific tool stack or universal licence for every electronics, rail, marine, aviation or telecommunications title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian higher-education teaching, administration, research and quality-assurance context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian university and tertiary education accreditation, academic planning, admissions, quality assurance, research, student support, curriculum and institutional administration
findings: NUC describes Nigerian university accreditation, minimum academic standards, academic planning, inspection, student services, research and institutional quality assurance; TETFund TERAS describes Nigerian tertiary research repositories and services for researchers, students and institutions; NBTE documents technical-tertiary admissions and academic-board responsibilities.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian higher-education functions and regulatory context, not a universal appointment route, academic rank or credential for every teaching, coaching or training title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian biomedical, biotechnology, pharmaceutical and epidemiology research context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian biomedical research, molecular biology, biotechnology, immunology, epidemiology, toxicology, pharmacology, diagnostics, vaccines and pharmaceutical development
findings: NIMR describes Nigerian molecular epidemiology, food-safety, immunogenetics, theranostics, microbiome and molecular-technique laboratories; NABDA describes Nigerian biomedical biotechnology work in immunology, vaccinology, antibody generation, DNA, biobanking and diagnostics; NIPRD describes pharmaceutical, biological-product, toxicology, quality-assurance and environmental-science research.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian research and institutional role families, not a vacancy count, personal licence or universal academic route for every biomedical or scientific occupation.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian clinical psychology professional context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian clinical psychology regulation, training, practice, supervision and mental-health delivery
findings: The Nigeria Association of Clinical Psychologists describes standardisation, practice regulation, training, continuing education and clinical-psychology services in Nigerian health and community settings; a Nigerian clinical initiative also identifies licensed clinical psychologists and supervised clinical roles.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish a Nigerian clinical-psychology role and professional pathway; they do not establish a national vacancy count or a single universal route for every psychology-adjacent role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian psychology professional-body context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian psychology education, membership, psychosocial service and professional-development context
findings: The Nigerian Psychological Association describes psychology practice, education, research and psychosocial services in the public interest and lists Nigerian membership pathways for students, graduates, associates and full members.
source_summaries.limitations: The professional-body page establishes Nigerian psychology practice context; it is not a vacancy count and does not by itself settle every licensing or specialty requirement.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Science Laboratory Technology nanotechnology training
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian nanotechnology laboratory training, synthesis and characterisation, imaging, biosensing, safety and applications
findings: NISLT published a 2025 short-term nanotechnology and laboratory-science workshop naming synthesis, characterisation, imaging, biosensing, safety and smart laboratory materials.
source_summaries.limitations: The workshop is a bounded training signal, not a universal nanotechnology credential or employer requirement.

source_summaries.name: National Postgraduate Medical College of Nigeria neurology subspecialty curriculum
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian postgraduate neurology specialist training and clinical practice preparation
findings: The National Postgraduate Medical College of Nigeria publishes a Neurology Sub-Specialty training curriculum.
MDCN materials separately establish Nigerian medical registration and additional postgraduate-qualification registration boundaries.
source_summaries.limitations: The curriculum supports a specialist pathway; it does not state that every neurologist follows one identical appointment route or that a postgraduate qualification alone substitutes for MDCN registration.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian university and tertiary education accreditation, academic planning, admissions, quality assurance, research, student support, curriculum and institutional administration

Esports Federation of Nigeria national esports programmes
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian competitive gaming, schools and university esports, broadcasting, refereeing, tournament operations and team programmes
findings: The federation described a National Esports Championship, Team Nigeria programme, schools and university league, and training for referees, broadcasters and tournament officials.
The federation's career-pathway language identifies athletes, content creators, event managers, analysts and game developers as roles within the Nigerian esports ecosystem.
EFN's current about page identifies players, coaches, referees and support staff as participants in Nigeria's organised esports pathway and describes national representation and player development.
source_summaries.limitations: Federation programmes demonstrate ecosystem and role-family context; they do not establish national job volume or a mandatory credential.

source_summaries.name: Federation of Interactive Games of Nigeria career pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian and African interactive-games pathways covering casting, game development, voice and content creation
findings: FIGN presents distinct pathways for commentary and casting, game development across design/engineering/art/audio, voiceover and content/creator work.
source_summaries.limitations: A pathway page demonstrates ecosystem and portfolio direction; it is not a vacancy count, universal job requirement or personal licence.

source_summaries.name: Federal Ministry of Arts, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy gaming sector context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria gaming, game development, esports and immersive creative economy
findings: Government identifies game development, esports and immersive experiences as a Nigerian creative-economy growth area.
The ministry describes local talent support, digital-skills development and job creation as sector objectives.
source_summaries.limitations: Sector policy context is not a count of vacancies and does not establish an individual licence or credential requirement.

source_summaries.name: Jobberman Nigeria jobs
MENACE Nigerian-linked esports team-management ecosystem page
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian-linked esports organisation and team-management roles, including player and team support
findings: MENACE describes a Nigerian-linked esports organisation focused on developing Nigerian talent internationally and explicitly identifies a team-manager function alongside players, managers and creators.
source_summaries.limitations: An organisation page demonstrates that the role exists in a Nigerian-linked esports ecosystem; it is not a national vacancy count, universal employer requirement or certification pathway.

Nigerian Film Corporation creative-media National Occupational Standards workshop
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian creative-media trades including film, audio, content, photography, animation, graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies
findings: The Nigerian Film Corporation reported a July 2026 critique and validation workshop intended to develop National Occupational Standards for creative-media trades, including film production, audio production, content creation, digital photography, animation, digital graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies.
source_summaries.limitations: The workshop demonstrates Nigerian standardisation activity and named trade families; it does not mean final standards or a personal certificate already exist for every listed role.

source_summaries.name: NITDA 3MTT Nigerian product, data, cloud, DevOps and digital-skills pathways

findings: NITDA and 3MTT explicitly list product management, data analysis and visualisation, data science, cloud computing, DevOps, UI/UX and quality assurance among Nigerian technical-skill tracks.
source_summaries.limitations: A national training track is evidence of a Nigerian skills pathway and ecosystem signal, not a guarantee of employment demand or a universal requirement for each related subgroup.

findings: Current Nigeria-focused job listings identify Broadcast Technician work involving broadcast equipment, audio-visual systems, signal monitoring, live production and technical troubleshooting.
source_summaries.limitations: The checked listings demonstrate a Nigerian broadcast-technology role family but do not establish esports-specific demand, a national vacancy total or one universal tool stack.

source_summaries.name: Nigeria-based broadcast news editor vacancy signal
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria-based broadcast-media news-editing work
findings: A Nigeria-based CNBC Africa posting identified a News Editor role in Lagos and described newsroom agenda-setting, editorial quality, production and team direction responsibilities.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a dated vacancy signal for broadcast news editing in Nigeria; it is not an esports-specific vacancy, national demand count or universal qualification requirement.

source_summaries.name: CPN 2021 Examination Syllabus
Nigerian creative-industry and media sources
Esports Federation of Nigeria national esports programmes
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian competitive gaming, schools and university esports, broadcasting, refereeing, tournament operations and team programmes
findings: The federation described a National Esports Championship, Team Nigeria programme, schools and university league, and training for referees, broadcasters and tournament officials.
The federation's career-pathway language identifies athletes, content creators, event managers, analysts and game developers as roles within the Nigerian esports ecosystem.
EFN's current about page identifies players, coaches, referees and support staff as participants in Nigeria's organised esports pathway and describes national representation and player development.
source_summaries.limitations: Federation programmes demonstrate ecosystem and role-family context; they do not establish national job volume or a mandatory credential.

source_summaries.name: Federation of Interactive Games of Nigeria career pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian and African interactive-games pathways covering casting, game development, voice and content creation
findings: FIGN presents distinct pathways for commentary and casting, game development across design/engineering/art/audio, voiceover and content/creator work.
source_summaries.limitations: A pathway page demonstrates ecosystem and portfolio direction; it is not a vacancy count, universal job requirement or personal licence.

source_summaries.name: Federal Ministry of Arts, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy gaming sector context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria gaming, game development, esports and immersive creative economy
findings: Government identifies game development, esports and immersive experiences as a Nigerian creative-economy growth area.
The ministry describes local talent support, digital-skills development and job creation as sector objectives.
source_summaries.limitations: Sector policy context is not a count of vacancies and does not establish an individual licence or credential requirement.

source_summaries.name: Jobberman Nigeria jobs
MENACE Nigerian-linked esports team-management ecosystem page
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian-linked esports organisation and team-management roles, including player and team support
findings: MENACE describes a Nigerian-linked esports organisation focused on developing Nigerian talent internationally and explicitly identifies a team-manager function alongside players, managers and creators.
source_summaries.limitations: An organisation page demonstrates that the role exists in a Nigerian-linked esports ecosystem; it is not a national vacancy count, universal employer requirement or certification pathway.

findings: The Nigerian Film Corporation reported a July 2026 critique and validation workshop intended to develop National Occupational Standards for creative-media trades, including film production, audio production, content creation, digital photography, animation, digital graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies.
source_summaries.limitations: The workshop demonstrates Nigerian standardisation activity and named trade families; it does not mean final standards or a personal certificate already exist for every listed role.

source_summaries.name: NITDA 3MTT Nigerian product, data, cloud, DevOps and digital-skills pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian technical-talent pathways in product management, data analysis, data science, cloud computing, DevOps, UI/UX, quality assurance, software, AI, cybersecurity and game development
findings: NITDA and 3MTT explicitly list product management, data analysis and visualisation, data science, cloud computing, DevOps, UI/UX and quality assurance among Nigerian technical-skill tracks.
source_summaries.limitations: A national training track is evidence of a Nigerian skills pathway and ecosystem signal, not a guarantee of employment demand or a universal requirement for each related subgroup.

findings: LBS describes certificate programmes for retail professionals, managers and senior executives and an Africa Retail Academy with 2024 programmes.

findings: The National Theatre identifies production and technical-theatre services and operates as a Nigerian hub for artistic expression and cultural production.
source_summaries.limitations: Institutional context does not establish a role-specific vacancy, salary or credential requirement.

NBTE Creative Content Production curriculum
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian audio-visual content, cinematography, sound, editing and scriptwriting
findings: The curriculum includes background music and sound effects, cinematography, shot lists, storyboarding, lighting, screen directing and introductory scriptwriting.
source_summaries.limitations: Curriculum evidence supports skills and learning routes, not role-level demand or a universal credential requirement.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian creative-media and performing-production standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film and media production, cinematography, lighting, sound, editing, production design, performance, special effects and stage/creative production
findings: The Nigerian NBTE Creative Media Production standard covers storytelling, cinematography, sound, production design, editing, performance, special effects, video-camera operation, lighting and casting; National Theatre materials identify stage performances, film shows, exhibitions, cultural shows, circus shows and related production facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian training and production ecosystems, not a national vacancy count or direct evidence for every highly specialised performance title; role-specific gaps remain explicit where the source does not support the title.

source_summaries.limitations: The workshop demonstrates Nigerian standardisation activity and named trade families; it does not mean final standards or a personal certificate already exist for every listed role.

source_summaries.name: National Film and Video Censors Board film classification and distribution licensing
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film/video classification, legal distribution and exhibition
findings: NFVCB states that films and video works must be classified before distribution or exhibition and provides online, national, regional and community distributor-licence categories.
source_summaries.limitations: These requirements apply to film works, distributors and exhibition activity; they are not automatically a personal licence for actors, editors, camera operators or technicians.

source_summaries.name: NIHOTOUR and Nigerian Tourism Development Authority practitioner registration and accreditation
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian hospitality, travel and tourism practitioner registration/certification and enterprise accreditation
findings: NIHOTOUR describes registration, certification and verification of practitioners; NTDA describes accreditation and classification of hospitality and tourism enterprises.
source_summaries.limitations: Practitioner and enterprise routes differ; neither is a universal credential for every tourism or retail role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission creative-economy sector map

source_summaries.limitations: Sector mapping shows an established Nigerian sector context; it does not establish role-level hiring volume or a required tool stack.

source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian training and production ecosystems, not a national vacancy count or direct evidence for every highly specialised performance title; role-specific gaps remain explicit where the source does not support the title.

source_summaries.name: National Film and Video Censors Board film classification and distribution licensing
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film/video classification, legal distribution and exhibition
findings: NFVCB states that films and video works must be classified before distribution or exhibition and provides online, national, regional and community distributor-licence categories.
source_summaries.limitations: These requirements apply to film works, distributors and exhibition activity; they are not automatically a personal licence for actors, editors, camera operators or technicians.

source_summaries.name: NIHOTOUR and Nigerian Tourism Development Authority practitioner registration and accreditation
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian hospitality, travel and tourism practitioner registration/certification and enterprise accreditation
findings: NIHOTOUR describes registration, certification and verification of practitioners; NTDA describes accreditation and classification of hospitality and tourism enterprises.
source_summaries.limitations: Practitioner and enterprise routes differ; neither is a universal credential for every tourism or retail role.

source_summaries.name: University of Ilorin museum and archival certificate/diploma pathway
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian museum, archival, cultural and heritage certificate and diploma education
findings: The University of Ilorin announced 2025/2026 certificate and diploma programmes in museum and archival studies, cultural studies and creative arts.
source_summaries.limitations: An education certificate/diploma route is not a universal statutory licence or proof of demand for every heritage role.

source_summaries.name: WIPO Nigeria and Music Business Academy professional training
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian music and entertainment business training, intellectual property and employability capacity building
findings: WIPO Nigeria described a 2024/2025 Music Business Academy scholarship and a nine-month vocational programme for African music-industry professionals.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports a sector training route, not a universal music-production certification or licence.

source_summaries.scope: African and Nigerian retail practice, consumer behaviour, shopper marketing, selling, customer service and retail-finance training
findings: LBS describes certificate programmes for retail professionals, managers and senior executives and an Africa Retail Academy with 2024 programmes.
source_summaries.limitations: These are professional training certificates, not a statutory licence or universal hiring requirement for retail workers.

source_summaries.name: MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
National Theatre production and technical-theatre ecosystem
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian stage production, technical theatre, performance and cultural programming
findings: The National Theatre identifies production and technical-theatre services and operates as a Nigerian hub for artistic expression and cultural production.
source_summaries.limitations: Institutional context does not establish a role-specific vacancy, salary or credential requirement.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE Creative Content Production curriculum
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian audio-visual content, cinematography, sound, editing and scriptwriting
findings: The curriculum includes background music and sound effects, cinematography, shot lists, storyboarding, lighting, screen directing and introductory scriptwriting.
source_summaries.limitations: Curriculum evidence supports skills and learning routes, not role-level demand or a universal credential requirement.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian creative-media and performing-production standards
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film and media production, cinematography, lighting, sound, editing, production design, performance, special effects and stage/creative production
findings: The Nigerian NBTE Creative Media Production standard covers storytelling, cinematography, sound, production design, editing, performance, special effects, video-camera operation, lighting and casting; National Theatre materials identify stage performances, film shows, exhibitions, cultural shows, circus shows and related production facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources establish Nigerian training and production ecosystems, not a national vacancy count or direct evidence for every highly specialised performance title; role-specific gaps remain explicit where the source does not support the title.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Copyright Commission music and creative-economy rights framework
National Commission for Museums and Monuments functions and museum-practice standards
Nigerian Film Corporation creative-media National Occupational Standards workshop
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian creative-media trades including film, audio, content, photography, animation, graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies
findings: The Nigerian Film Corporation reported a July 2026 critique and validation workshop intended to develop National Occupational Standards for creative-media trades, including film production, audio production, content creation, digital photography, animation, digital graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies.
source_summaries.limitations: The workshop demonstrates Nigerian standardisation activity and named trade families; it does not mean final standards or a personal certificate already exist for every listed role.

source_summaries.name: National Film and Video Censors Board film classification and distribution licensing
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian film/video classification, legal distribution and exhibition
findings: NFVCB states that films and video works must be classified before distribution or exhibition and provides online, national, regional and community distributor-licence categories.
source_summaries.limitations: These requirements apply to film works, distributors and exhibition activity; they are not automatically a personal licence for actors, editors, camera operators or technicians.

source_summaries.name: NIHOTOUR and Nigerian Tourism Development Authority practitioner registration and accreditation
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian hospitality, travel and tourism practitioner registration/certification and enterprise accreditation
findings: NIHOTOUR describes registration, certification and verification of practitioners; NTDA describes accreditation and classification of hospitality and tourism enterprises.
source_summaries.limitations: Practitioner and enterprise routes differ; neither is a universal credential for every tourism or retail role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission creative-economy sector map
source_summaries.scope: Film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming, XR, arts and cultural tourism in Nigeria
findings: The NIPC sector page identifies film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming and XR among Nigeria's creative-economy activities.
source_summaries.limitations: Sector mapping shows an established Nigerian sector context; it does not establish role-level hiring volume or a required tool stack.

source_summaries.name: NITDA 3MTT Nigerian product, data, cloud, DevOps and digital-skills pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian technical-talent pathways in product management, data analysis, data science, cloud computing, DevOps, UI/UX, quality assurance, software, AI, cybersecurity and game development
findings: NITDA and 3MTT explicitly list product management, data analysis and visualisation, data science, cloud computing, DevOps, UI/UX and quality assurance among Nigerian technical-skill tracks.
source_summaries.limitations: A national training track is evidence of a Nigerian skills pathway and ecosystem signal, not a guarantee of employment demand or a universal requirement for each related subgroup.

source_summaries.name: Standards Organisation of Nigeria tourism, travel-agency and tourism-school technical committees
University of Ilorin museum and archival certificate/diploma pathway
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian museum, archival, cultural and heritage certificate and diploma education
findings: The University of Ilorin announced 2025/2026 certificate and diploma programmes in museum and archival studies, cultural studies and creative arts.
source_summaries.limitations: An education certificate/diploma route is not a universal statutory licence or proof of demand for every heritage role.

source_summaries.name: WIPO Nigeria and Music Business Academy professional training
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian music and entertainment business training, intellectual property and employability capacity building
findings: WIPO Nigeria described a 2024/2025 Music Business Academy scholarship and a nine-month vocational programme for African music-industry professionals.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports a sector training route, not a universal music-production certification or licence.
